P061.statement:
Assume the printed-result package \(H'\) and the level and Satake/Frobenius correspondence for the admissible polarized representations. For each imaginary quadratic \(K\) and \(n\ge2\) there exist natural numbers \(c,A\) with the following property. Let \(m_1>\cdots>m_n\) be integral, \(m_i+m_{n+1-i}=w_0,\ |m_i|\le H\), and let \(M\ge1\). At a prime \(p\nmid M\operatorname{disc}(K)\) and \(w\mid p\) there exists a datum \(D\) of normalized eigenvalues of rank \(n\), norm \(Nw\), weight \(m\) and total weight \(w_0\) such that
\[
 |D.S|\le c\bigl(M(H+1)\bigr)^A .
\]
For every prime \(\ell\ne2,p\), every algebraic closure of \(K\) and every \(\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\simeq\mathbf C\), this same \(D\) classifies the admissible polarized representations of level \(M\) and weight \(m\) at \(w\). The assignment to the finite set separates isomorphism classes and recovers the prescribed Frobenius multiset at \(w\).

P062.statement:
Let \(\ell\) be prime, \(\Omega/\mathbf Q\) an algebraic closure, \(A\) a valuation subring, \(S\) a finite set of places, and \(g\) a newform of weight \(2e+1\). Assume \(W\) satisfies the specified normal-form and unramified newform-source conditions relative to these data and \(\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\simeq\mathbf C\). For every coefficient datum, global cocycle \(y\), exceptional set \(S'\), quotient character \(\nu\), weights \(\chi_r\) and local system \(Z_r\), assume the global tame law, the integral Iwasawa system, specialization to \(y\), and \(\mathrm{Pin7}\) for this very tuple. Then there exists \(\sigma\in I_A\) with
\[
  \chi_{\rm cyc}(\sigma)=1,\qquad W(\sigma)_{22}=1,\qquad y(\sigma)_2\ne0.
\]
Here \(\mathrm{Pin7}\) includes triviality of \(\nu\) on inertia, a Frobenius lift with specified unit value, a second unit, a compatible sequence of units, an integral power series, the finite-precision Hodge--Tate formula, and eventual nonvanishing modulo \(\ell^{n_0+r}\) of its weighted primitive-root sums.

P064.statement:
Assume \(H'\), including the prescribed cohomological contribution and the finite-family injection at compact open level. For each CM field \(K\) and \(n\ge2\) there exist natural numbers \(c,A\) such that for strictly decreasing integral \(m_i\) with \(|m_i|\le H\), and \(M\ge1\), every finite family \(S\) of pairwise nonisomorphic cuspidal representations of the given \(\mathrm{GL}_n\) with the specified infinitesimal characters at the embeddings of \(K\), conjugate duality and a nonzero principal-level-\(M\) fixed vector satisfies
\[
                       |S|\le c\bigl(M(H+1)\bigr)^A .
\]

P065.statement: Assume the theorem providing integral layerwise zeta cocycles, the smoothed-class Hodge--Tate law, and the admissibility data for the common Hecke projection and smoothing. For each normal-form \(W\) and unramified newform source as in P062 there exists a single tuple \((c,y,S',\nu,\chi,Z)\) for which all four assertions hold: the global integral tame cocycle condition on \(y\), the local integral Iwasawa condition on \(Z\) with quotient \(\nu\), the specialization from \(Z\) to \(y\) with weights \(\chi\), and \(\mathrm{Pin7}\) on these choices. The latter carries the unit, Frobenius, congruence and power-series nonvanishing conditions specified in P062.

P066.statement:
Take the normal form, unramified source, two embeddings, analytic tower, projection, weights, smoothers, matrices, twist \(\psi_0\), level \(N>0\) and coefficient ring of the weighted symbols. Assume \(\ell\ne2,\ e\ge1\), weighted-symbol admissibility and the designated Hodge--Tate parameter conditions (including the parameter \(\alpha\)). Choose an embedding \(j:\Omega\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\) with \(x\in A\) exactly when \(\|j(x)\|\le1\). Suppose \(Y_r\) realizes the specified zeta classes with fixed initial loss and twisted cocycle law, its second coordinate is integral, and at each level and precision it satisfies the uniform finite-stabilizer congruence in P063. Choose a multiplicative diamond function \(\chi_d\) modulo \(N\) which is a unit on the integers prime to \(N\), and an admissible Fourier-coefficient functional \(\lambda\) of weight \(2e-1\) for this datum. For each \(d_0\ge2\) prime to \(\ell\) there exist \(m_0,c_1\), a nonzero \(\kappa\), and \(\|v_m\|=1\) with \(v_{m+1}\equiv v_m\bmod\ell^m\). The smoothed layer
\[
                 Z_r(s,u)=Y_{r,2}(s,u)-d_0Y_{r,2}(s,ud_0)
\]
has the stated integral Hodge--Tate presentations on one compatible system of primitive roots \(\zeta_m\). For \(m\ge m_0\), a primitive character \(\psi\bmod\ell^m\) and \(z=j(\zeta_m)\), its character sum of presented Hodge--Tate values at level \(m\) is congruent at precision \(m-c_1\) (truncated at zero) to
\[
 (1-d_0\psi^{-1}(d_0))\,v_m\kappa
 \left(\sum_{a\bmod\ell^m}\psi(a)z^{a_{\rm rep}}\right)
 \psi^{-1}(N)\,\lambda\!\left(\mathrm{up}_{\ell^m}
       \left(\sum_{x\bmod N} c_w(x)\,\mathrm{chiProj}_{N,\ell,m,x}\right)\right).
\]
The projection in the last factor uses weight \(2e+1\), the same \(\psi,\chi_d,c,d\) and the chosen integer representative of \(x\).

P053.statement:
Let $P$ be any predicate on the ordinary Euler-system data. Suppose that every ordinary newform datum as below has witnesses $(c,y,S',\nu,\chi,Z)$ satisfying
\[
 \mathrm{Sys}(W,c,y,S')\,,\quad \mathrm{IwSys2}(c,A,\nu,Z)\,,\quad
 \mathrm{SpLink}(A,e,\chi,Z,y)\,,\quad P(e,A,W,c,\nu,\chi,Z),
\]
and that for every such collection there is an inertia element at $A$ with cyclotomic character and second diagonal entry both $1$ and nonzero second cocycle coordinate. Then for every ordinary newform datum $(\ell,\Omega,\iota,e,S,A,W,g)$ satisfying $\mathrm{Nf}$ and $\mathrm{SrcUr}$, there are a coefficient ring $\mathcal O_c$, a finite set $S'$ and an integral cocycle $y$ for the column representation of $W$. Every matrix of $W$ is integral over $\mathcal O_c$. The class of $y$ is unramified away from $\ell$, and it satisfies the prescribed tame relations at $w\notin S'$ whenever $\ell^n\mid Nw-1$, $n\ge1$, for every admissible surjective tame test character. Its ordinary quotient at $A$ fails the local coboundary condition.

P054.statement: Let $I$ be valid and pinned column data, $l$ a choice of its laws and $Z$ later data on its columns. For $D=I.\mathrm{rec7}(l,Z)$ there exists a symmetric column comparison $C$ with $\mathrm{StdC}(C)$ and $\mathrm{StdLvC}(C.\mathrm{forms}_u)$ for every word $u$. Thus the forms, endpoint representatives, interior quotient projections and evaluated frames all refer to the given family, with the generator frames at zero and on the primed space equal to the identity.

P055.statement: In the setting of \nodeid{P054}, fix the level-zero law $l_0$, a choice of $n$, a tied tuple $t_p$ on the resulting character frame, and a symmetric comparison $C$. Assume $t_p.\xi=I.\xi$, $\mathrm{StdC}(C)$ and the interior standard-level condition at every word. Then there is a symmetric twisted column comparison over this $t_p$, this $C$ and $I.\mathrm{tw}(l,l_0,Z)$, having standard forms, levels, points and point evaluations.

P056.statement:
Fix $D$, its character frame, tied tuple and symmetric twisted column data $t$, a divisor datum $Y$, a word $u$, and $\mu\ne\mu_0$. Suppose that for each integral point, each permitted form and each class, the concrete class contraction is the image of a field element integral at every place with residue characteristic outside $Y.Q_p(\mu)$. There are pairings $p_c$ on the row and form spaces such that for all $z,F$
\[
 \mathcal P_{u,\mu}(z,F)=\sum_c |\Gamma_c|^{-1}p_c(z,F).
\]
For every integral point and permitted form each $p_c$ on their specified images has the same simultaneous integrality property.

P057.statement:
For every $D,Y,T$, assume the classwise decomposition of \nodeid{P056} for all words and all $\mu\ne\mu_0$ of the form $\mu_w$. Under the stabilizer-denominator hypothesis, for each used nonreference tuple, integral point $x$ and permitted form $F$ in $V_0(\mu)$ there exists a single $b$ in the coefficient field whose specified embedding is the period. For every $w\mid p$ with $p\notin Y.Q_p(\mu)$,
\[
 b=0\quad\text{or}\quad v_w(b)\ge-e_wv_p(D_{\Gamma,u}).
\]

P058.statement:
Let $e\ge1$, $w=2e-1$, $\ell$ an odd prime, $N\ge5$, $\ell\nmid N$, and take the ordinary datum $W$, the tower $X$ holomorphic on the specified half-plane, a place $A$ above $\ell$ and an embedding $j$ integral on $A$. Suppose the two-dimensional representation $\rho$ realizes $\rho_K(W,e,\psi)$, is upper triangular on the decomposition group, has lower diagonal $1$ on inertia and upper diagonal $\chi_{\rm cyc}^{2e}$ on inertia fixing the specified finite set. Let the admissible eigenvalues agree with the weight-$2e+1$ newform away from $N\ell$ and with $\chi$ on diamonds. Suppose the admissible Hecke polynomial $P$ has value one at this eigensystem and acts on the rational Betti space by $\sum_i\sigma_i\pi_i$, where the inclusions land in that space, the maps are Galois and admissible-Hecke equivariant there, and $\pi_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}$. Let $\lambda$ be a finite-support coefficient functional whose coefficients satisfy the specified inertia-fixedness condition. Assume that at each sufficiently large precision $n$, on every $\chi$-vector and every admitted letter, $\lambda$ on the tower expansion commutes with that letter up to its eigenvalue with precision $n-c_2$, for a common $c_2$.
Then there are $a\ge0$, $\mathcal O_{c'}\supseteq\mathcal O_c$ containing the entries of $W$, and a $\mathbf Z_\ell$-linear map $\mathrm{pr}:X.\mathrm{Fn}_\ell\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^2$ integral on the Betti lattice. There it intertwines Galois actions and sends $T_q$, diamonds and $U_\ell$ to their prescribed eigenvalues. The map and $\ell^a\lambda$ satisfy $\mathrm{IsLamFR2}$ on this tower, including the diamond identity. Explicitly, there are a uniform loss $d$ and inertia-fixed periods $p_n$ of norm one, $p_{n+1}\equiv p_n\bmod\ell^n$, with
\[
 \ell^a\lambda(\operatorname{seq}_j\varphi)
       \equiv p_n\,\mathrm{pr}(b)_2\pmod{\ell^{n-d}}
\]
for every $n\ge d$, every integral $\chi$-vector $b$ and every tower expansion $\varphi$ representing $b$ at precision $n$. Fixedness here is under automorphisms fixing the enlarged coefficient ring and acting trivially on the residue field. The scaled functional still has finite support and fixed coefficients.

P059.statement:
Let $w$ be a served place for a word $u$, and suppose the host, size data and local lattice data satisfy the gate and lattice comparisons. If $2r_G\le k$, then at each position $v$ the resulting parameters satisfy $\mathrm{Std}$. More explicitly $p$ is prime and at least five, $n'_v\ge2$ is even, $1\le r$, $2r\le k_1+1$, $1\le m$, and the marked subset, $a_v,b_v,c$ and $\lambda_{0,v}$ satisfy the base-weight and dominance conditions. For every $s$,
\[
 w_1(s)\ge\max(c,-\lambda_0(s,k_1)),\qquad
 w_j(s)\le w_{j+1}(s)\quad(1\le j<m).
\]

P060.statement: Assume the curve-existence assertion. Fix tied kernel data, a word and tuple, a served place $w$ of prime residue characteristic $p$, specified levels, comparison hypotheses and labels, a standard local model and a joint comparison $J$. There is an element of $J.\mathrm{At}$ at this model. It comprises a comparison embedding and $\lambda:\overline{\mathbf Q}\to\mathbf C_p$ compatible on the specified algebraic complex values, a formal group with Lubin--Tate isomorphism and the required curve, finite class sets and finite stabilizers at all the indicated levels, and a pair $(\Xi,\mu_T)$ satisfying all the adelic laws on $J$.

P067.statement:
Let $\ell$ be odd, $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\simeq\mathbf C$, $e\ge1$, and $g$ a weight-$2e+1$ newform of level $M_g$ prime to $\ell$ with $|\iota^{-1}a_\ell(g)|=1$. For any Dirichlet character $\psi$ modulo $\ell$ and $N_0>0$ prime to $\ell$, there exist $N\ge5$ prime to $\ell$ divisible by $M_g,N_0$, characters $\chi,\theta$ modulo $N$, and a unit root $\alpha$ of $X^2-a_\ell(g)X+\chi(\ell)\ell^{2e}$. Here $\chi$ agrees with the character of $g$ on units, $\chi(-1)=-1$ and $\theta(-1)=(-1)^e\psi(-1)$. For the same choices there is a finite-coefficient Hecke eigenfunctional $(B,c)$ with eigenvalues $(a_q(g),\alpha)$ and the specified $\mathrm{MeasMu}$ measure identity with $v\ne0$. There are $c_1,d_1>1$ prime to $6N\ell$ for which $c_1^e$ avoids every complex number of absolute value one, and
\[
 d_1^2\ne d_1^{e+1}(\theta\chi^{\pm1})(d_1)^{n_1}\psi(d_1)^{n_2}
 \quad(n_1=\pm1,\ n_2\in\mathbf Z).
\]

P068.statement:
Under the two hypotheses for $P$ in \nodeid{P053}, for every $\ell,\Omega,\iota,e,S,A,W,g$ satisfying $\mathrm{Nf}$ and $\mathrm{SrcUr}$, there exist $c,y,S'$ with $\mathrm{Sys}(W,c,y,S')$ and a single $s\in I_A$ such that
\[
 \chi_{\rm cyc}(s)=1,\qquad W(s)_{22}=1,\qquad y(s)_2\ne0.
\]

P069.statement: For standard $H,F$ as above there is a family $A_u$ of Hermitian data at the level primes satisfying $\mathrm{CarT}$, symmetric adelic compatibility and symmetric stabilizer-map compatibility. The carrier condition includes the uniformizer, prime and field identifications, primed lattice and levels, ordinary and kernel projections, the distinguished vector and the matrix identifying its translated representative. Each upward, downward and unit move has the required adelic reading at zero and at a positive stage.

P070.statement: For the valid pinned $I,l,Z$, the coordinate systems satisfy the standard comparison. The primed space and every stage $i\le m$ have identity Gram matrix. The primed inclusion sends $x$ to $(x,0)$, and a vector of the self-dual stage lattice is characterized by all its coordinates lying in $\mathcal O_E$. For all words, tuples and classes, the image of the selected class lattice is the lattice of its decorated representative. There is a frame equivalence with the specified coordinate identification, under which the evaluation at each embedding $\tau$ is the determinant of the $\tau$-frame.

P071.statement: Fix the extra level-zero law, prime predicate, columns $H$, forms $F$, twisted chain $T$, its joint data $J$ with $H$, and forms $W$ on them. Suppose $F$ satisfies the form and chart-level standardness conditions at every word, and $W$ is standard. There exists a family of twisted level data on $W$ whose two projections read the prescribed lattice quotient maps wherever defined. Moreover the level-comparison type $\mathrm{TwLvSameS}(W)$ is inhabited, comparing the zero stage at each tuple and every required stage at the reference tuple.

P072.statement: For valid pinned column data there exist chart sets $\mathrm{Ch}_{u,i}$, maps from the stage classes to those sets and symmetric forms $F_u$ on their fibres. All charts are finite and the top chart is unique at each word. The two standardness conditions $\mathrm{StdF}$ and $\mathrm{StdLvC}$ hold at every word, and the global data of $F_u$ agree for all $u$. At each generator prime $q$ the reference characters are distinct for $a<m$, have the same evaluations on integers across the indicated places and equal $\omega^{2(a+1)}$ there for a character $\omega$ of order $q-1$.

P073.statement: Suppose the chart sets and the maps from classes are given, the sets are finite, the last is unique, and $F_u$ on those charts satisfies the standard form condition for each word. One can choose the zero and higher Hermitian levels with their class data, places over $T_u$ and residue identifications, using the given chart sets and maps. The resulting $H$ satisfies $\mathrm{CarH}(H,F)$, including its comparisons of representatives, local and global subgroups, stabilizers and frame data.

P074.statement: For standard $H,F$, assume $A$ satisfies $\mathrm{CarT}$ and that at every $w\mid T_u$, every local integral lift of $\pi_u=A_u.\pi$ annihilates the value module at stage zero. Then $c_u\pi_u=\pi_{u_0}$ for the prescribed cofactor. At zero and on every relevant chart the base lattice plus $\bar\pi_u$ times its dual equals the specified full coordinate lattice. There are compatible residue-field functionals, and zero-level data with the same generator $\pi_G$ at every word.

P075.statement:
Let $\ell$ be odd, $e\ge1$, $L,G\in\mathcal O_c[[X]]$, $a,a'$ units in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, $\kappa\ne0$, and $v_m,v'_m$ units with successive terms congruent at precision $m$. Let $m_0,c_0\ge2$ with $\ell\nmid c_0$, and let $\phi$ be a character modulo $\ell$. Write $t_m(F,z)=\sum_{j<\ell^{3m}} F_j(z-1)^j$ and $S_m(F,\psi,z)=\sum_{b\in(\mathbf Z/\ell^m)^\times}\psi(b)t_m(F,z^b)$. For every $m\ge m_0$ suppose there is one primitive $z$ of order $\ell^m$ such that for all primitive characters $\psi$ of this conductor
\[
 (1-c_0\psi^{-1}(c_0))v'_m\kappa (a')^m S_m(L,\psi,z)
 \equiv v_m a^m S_m(G,\psi,z)\pmod{\ell^{\max(m-c_1,0)}}.
\]
Put $M_r(F,\xi)=\sum_{0\le x<\ell^r,\,\ell\nmid x}\phi(x)x^e\sum_{k<\ell^r}\xi^{-kx}t_r(F,\xi^k)$. Suppose for all sufficiently large $r\ge1$ and every primitive $\xi$ of order $\ell^r$ the value $M_r(L,\xi)$ is nonzero modulo $\ell^{n_0+r}$. There exists $n_1$ such that for all sufficiently large $r$ and every such $\xi$, $M_r(G,\xi)$ is nonzero modulo $\ell^{n_1+r}$. Congruences denote closed $\ell$-adic precision balls.

P076.statement: For $\ell,\Omega,\iota,e,S,A,W,g$ satisfying the normal-form and ordinary newform source conditions, and every $s\in I_A$ in the kernel of the full cyclotomic character, $W(s)_{22}=1$. Here the second diagonal entry is $(1,1)$ in zero-based indexing.

P077.statement: At a word $u$ take forms $F$ with the standard form law, and a stage-zero level $L$ with the same base lattice, local and global groups, representatives and stabilizer maps as the zero level of $F$. There is one replacement $L'$ preserving all those entries as well as the splitting and generator frame of $L$, such that for every $w\mid T_u$ and every local integer $a$ whose image is the image of $F.\pi_u$, the scalar $a$ kills the entire value module of $L'$ at $w$.

P078.statement: Take standard $H,F$, the additional zero-level law, and a prime predicate $Q(a,v)$ equivalent everywhere to the prescribed $\mathrm{UnderQ}(a,v)$. There exist a twisted chain $T$, a joint comparison $J$ with $H$, and standard twisted forms $W$. The chain agrees at $\mu_0$ and there are joint symmetric forms over the same choices. For each $u,a\ne\mu_0$ when $m\ge1$, there is a family $k_\beta$ on the top charts reading their base lattices, levels, characters, representatives and stabilizers. Whenever $g'$ represents a primed point $d$ and $g$ extends $g'$ along the inclusion and fixes $z_0$, $gk_\beta$ represents the prescribed tilted point for every chart $\beta$.

P079.statement: Fix $H,F,T,J,W$, a zero-level law, the twist-prime predicate equivalent to $\mathrm{UnderQ}$, and a twisted level $L_v$ over $W$. Assume standard forms and chart levels at every word, standard $W,L_v$, and the top reading and extension property of \nodeid{P078} for each nonreference tuple when $m\ge1$. There are twisted points $P$ on $L_v$ and evaluations $E_P$ over $P$, satisfying the generator-place level and character comparisons. On the primed chart they read its given data; evaluation agrees on equal frame matrices, the tilted vector is $z_0$, and the row identification on evaluation is the identity.

P080.statement: For tied kernel data, a word, tuple, served place of prime residue characteristic, and the given levels, comparison hypotheses, labels, standard local model and joint $J$, there exist functions $(\Xi,\mu_T)$ satisfying $\mathrm{AdLawAt}$ for the adelic input, determinant map and exponent of $J$. The kernel reads adjacent class representatives, obeys both rational and level transformation laws and the stated local, support and integrality conditions. The character reads determinants, is algebraic and multiplicative on norm-one ideles, is unramified on the indicated integral ideles and has the prescribed rational values.

P081.statement: Under the automorphic hypothesis record $\mathrm{Hypotheses}'$, for each totally complex number field $E$ and $n\ge0$ there exist natural numbers $c,A$ such that for every strictly decreasing integral weight $m$ of length $n$ with $|m_i|\le H$ there is an algebraic coefficient representation $\Xi$ with dimension $\le c(H+1)^A$. At every embedding its infinitesimal character is the negative of the multiset $\{m_i+(n-1)/2\}_i$.

P082.statement: For every word, stage $i$, selected $v$, residue unit $a$ and class $c$ there is a unitary $\gamma$ such that, if $i\le m$, $\gamma L_{c'}=L_c$ for $c'=\langle a\rangle_v c$, and the chosen adelic representatives satisfy the move relation at $v$. On the dual, the residue reading of $z$ at $c'$ equals $a$ times the reading of $\gamma z$ at $c$ at $v$, and equals the corresponding reading at each other selected place.

P083.statement: Suppose additionally that the level-prime data $A$ satisfy $\mathrm{CarT}$. For each word with $m\ge1$, primed class $c$ and $s\in\Gamma_c$, conjugate the action of the image of $s$ on the top space by the tilted isometry $g_c$. The resulting transformation restricts on $i_X(X')$ to $i_Xs i_X^{-1}$ and fixes the distinguished vector $z_0$.

P084.statement:
For every $u,i,v,c$ and $y\in L_c^\sharp$ there exists a unitary $\gamma$. If $i\le m$ and the selected residue functional on $y$ has value $1$, let $c'$ be its upward class. The class lattice transported by $\gamma$ agrees with $L_c$ away from the pair $P_v,\bar P_v$, and
\[
 (\gamma L_{c'})_{P_v}=(L_c^\sharp)_{P_v},\qquad
 (\gamma L_{c'}^\sharp)_{P_v}
   =(L_c^\sharp+\mathcal O_E T_u^{-1}y)_{P_v}.
\]
On a dual input $z$ with $T_u\gamma z\in L_c^\sharp$ the selected reading equals that of $T_u\gamma z$ at $c$. The other selected places have the unchanged readings on transported inputs, and the adelic move relation uses this same $\gamma$.

P085.statement: For every word there exist class lattices on the smaller Hermitian space, a level and class representatives with stabilizer embeddings. After the rank identification their base lattice, local and global level groups, representatives and stabilizer maps coincide with the forms data, and the coordinate map on the primed space sends the lattice at $c$ to the forms lattice at $c$.

P086.statement: For every $u,i,v,c$ and residual linear functional $g$ there exists a unitary $\gamma$. If $i\le m$ and $g\ne0$, write $c'$ for the downward class. The transported lattice equals $L_c$ away from $P_v,\bar P_v$ after localization, and $(\gamma L_{c'}^\sharp)_{P_v}=(L_c)_{P_v}$. On a vector $z$ of the new dual with $\gamma z$ in the old kernel lattice, the selected value is $g$ applied to the old kernel projection of $\gamma z$. The other residue values and the adelic representative relation agree for this mover.

P087.statement: For $1\le i$ and $i+1\le m$ the chart and one-level projections agree on dual inputs with the same underlying vector. Their kernel-lattice projections also agree whenever the underlying vectors coincide.

P088.statement: Let $w$ have residue characteristic $T_u$, take a selected $v\mid T_u$, and let $x\in\mathcal O_E$ and $y$ in the coefficient field have the same value under the prescribed embeddings at $(w,v)$. Then $v_w(y)>0$ if and only if $x$ belongs to $P_v$ in the selected orientation, or to $\bar P_v$ in the conjugate orientation.

P089.statement: For each $u$, $i\le m$ and class $c$ the quotient of the class dual by the class lattice (regarded as a submodule of its dual) is $\mathcal O_E$-linearly isomorphic to $\mathcal O_E/(T_u)$.

P090.statement: For every chain and adelic datum $A$, determinant map $d$ and exponent $a$ satisfying the given adelic pin and tie conditions, the functions $\Xi=\Xi_{\rm ad}(A,a)$ and $\mu_T=\mu_{\rm of}(t,u,\mu,d)$ satisfy the entire $\mathrm{AdLawAt}$. The first function reads the prescribed adjacent kernels after change of frame, transforms under rational and level actions, depends only on the specified bad-place components, satisfies the local congruence condition, is supported on the prescribed denominator lattice and is integral off the designated primes. The second reads both rank-one determinants and class representatives, is algebraic and multiplicative on norm-one ideles, is trivial on the prescribed integral ideles, and on norm-one rational points is the product of the prescribed integral embedding powers.

P091.statement:
For every tied chain satisfying $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal M$, and
every $i+1\le m$ with $i=m_2$, the property $\mathcal A_i$ implies
$\mathcal L_i$, with all factors and chart arguments as in
\eqref{eq:chartlevel}.

P092.statement:
In every tied chain, $\mathcal A_i$ holds for each $i+1\le m$ with
$i<m_2$. Agreement of both adelic components at each $v\in B_F$ gives
equality of the two point kernels as functions, for any admissible
choices above the two pairs.

P093.statement:
Fix standard column data, a word $u$, stage $i\le m$, level places
$v,v'$ with $v'\ne v$, classes $c,c'$ and $\gamma\in\mathrm{GL}_{N_i}(E)$.
Suppose the classes are related by $\gamma$ at $v$. For $z,z'$ in the
respective class level-vector domains $\mathrm{Ld}_{i,c},\mathrm{Ld}_{i,c'}$
with $z=\gamma z'$ in $E^{N_i}$, one has
\[
       f_{i,v',c'}(\operatorname{pr}_{v',c'} z')
           = f_{i,v',c}(\operatorname{pr}_{v',c} z).
\]
Each projection and each functional is taken in its own class.

P094.statement:
For standard column data, fix $u$, $i\le m$, $v$ and $c,c'$. If
$\gamma$ preserves the stage Gram form over $E$ and its underlying
matrix relates $c,c'$ at $v$ in $F_u$, the corresponding rational
isometry $g_X(\gamma)$ relates the same classes at $v$ in $H$.
At stage zero the Hermitian relation is \code{Ad0S}. At every positive
stage it is \code{AdIS} at that stage, including $i=m$.

P095.statement:
Fix standard column data, a word $u$, a stage $i\le m$, a level place
$v$ and $b\in k_v^\times$, where $k_v$ is the column residue field.
There exists $k\in\mathbb Z$ whose residue is $b$ with the following
properties. If $i=0$ or $i=m$, the endpoint level has a finite unitary
adele $\delta$ satisfying the conditions below. If $1\le i$ and
$i+1\le m$, every chart at $i$ has such a $\delta$. In each case
$\delta_w=1$ for $w\ne v_F$, while $\delta_{v_F}$ belongs to the
local level group \code{levelVL} and stabilizes the localized span of
the dual of the base lattice. For every $x$ in that local dual lattice,
\[
                   k\,f_T(\delta_{v_F}x)=f_T(x).
\]
The same $k$ works for all charts at the fixed $u,i,v,b$. The elements
$\delta$ may depend on the chart.

P096.statement:
Fix standard column data, a word $u$, a stage $i\le m$, a place $v$,
classes $c,c'$, and $\gamma\in\mathrm{GL}_{N_i}(E)$ relating $c,c'$
at $v$. For every height-one prime $Q$ of $\mathcal O_E$ whose
contraction differs from $v_F$, the localizations in $E^{N_i}$ satisfy
\[
                         (\gamma L_{c'})_Q=(L_c)_Q .
\]

P097.statement:
Let a tied chain satisfy $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal A_i$ for every
$i+1\le m$. For any adjacent charts and representatives $x,x'$,
take rational unitary isometries $\gamma,\gamma'$ for their respective
Gram forms. For every $z:E^{N_i}\to E^{N_{i+1}}$,
\[
 \Xi_i(\gamma_f x,\gamma'_f x'; z)
 =\Xi_i(x,x';(\gamma'_{\rm std})^{-1}\circ z\circ\gamma_{\rm std}).
\]
The subscript $f$ denotes diagonal embedding. The standard-coordinate
linear maps are those specified by \code{stdG} for the two Gram forms.

P098.statement:
For standard column data, every $u,v$ determines a prime ideal
$P_v$ of $\mathcal O_E$. If a height-one prime $Q$ of $\mathcal O_E$
contracts to $v_F$, then $Q=P_v$ or $Q=\overline{P_v}$.

P099.statement:
In every tied chain satisfying $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal M$, for every
$i+1\le m$ with $i=m_2+1$, $\mathcal A_i$ implies $\mathcal L_i$.
In particular \eqref{eq:chartlevel} evaluates the last-step kernel
in the source and target charts of this adjacent pair.

P100.statement:
In every tied chain $\mathcal A_i$ holds at each $i+1\le m$ with
$i=m_2$. The equality in \eqref{eq:chartaway} holds for all $w$
with the coupling coset read from the respective target point.

P101.statement:
Every tied chain satisfies $\mathcal M$. Namely, for each $i<m$,
$M_i(\det y)=m_{i+1}(d(y))$ at every rank-one finite adelic unitary
point $y$. On the norm-one finite ideles $M_i$ sends $1$ to $1$,
is multiplicative, and takes values in $\overline{\mathbb Q}\subset
\mathbb C$. If $b$ is a norm-one integral idele and $b_v=1$ for
every place below a transported prime of $S_B$, then $M_i(b)=1$.
There exist integers $e_\tau$ whose images in $\mathbb Q$ are the
specified stage weights $h_{\tau,i}$ such that
\[
       M_i(z_f)=\prod_\tau \tau(z)^{e_\tau}
       \qquad(z\in E^\times,\ z\bar z=1).
\]
Here $z_f$ is the finite principal idele and the embeddings are
those selected by the host data.

P102.statement:
Let $j=m_2+1$ in a tied chain. For each class $c$, write
$p_c=A.\mathrm{pt}(j,c)$ and $\beta=\mathrm{chOf}_j(c)$. If
$F(p_c,P)$ denotes its frame, then
\[
 A.y_b(c)=
 \{y\in E_X^{N_j}: F(p_c,P)^{-1}y
       \equiv y_0(\beta,P)\quad\text{for every }P\in S_B\}.
\]
The congruence means coordinatewise integrality of the difference
divided by $q_P^{s_P}$, with $s_P=0$ at type primes and $s_P=M$
at the other selected primes.

P103.statement:
Let a tied chain satisfy $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal M$.
For every $i+1\le m$ with $i<m_2$, the property $\mathcal A_i$
implies \eqref{eq:chartlevel} for the matrix kernel at $i$, for every
choice of adjacent charts, representatives, level elements and $z$.

P104.statement:
Every tied chain satisfies $\mathcal E$. Moreover, for each $j\le m$
and every class $c$, its selected point $A.\mathrm{pt}(j,c)$
is admissible above the distinguished representative $y_c$ in chart
$\mathrm{chOf}_j(c)$. In both assertions admissibility comprises
the lattice equality, frame congruences and transported level-functional
identities specified above.

P105.statement:
For a tied chain satisfying $\mathcal E$, fix $i+1\le m$ and any
two adjacent charts and representatives $x,x'$. Let $N,N'$ be their
kernel lattices, $c$ the reader level, and $J$ the host scalar module
\code{aaOf} attached to the kernel ideal. Put
$\Pi=J\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_E}(N,N')$, the $\mathcal O_E$-span
of the products of elements of $J$ with ambient $E$-linear maps taking
$N$ into $N'$. For every applicable $z,z'$,
\begin{align*}
 c^{-1}(z-z')\in\Pi_P\quad (P\in B)
     &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Xi_i(x,x';z)=\Xi_i(x,x';z'),\\
 \Xi_i(x,x';z)\ne0
     &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad c z(N_P)\subseteq N'_P\quad (P\in B).
\end{align*}

P106.statement:
Suppose a tied chain satisfies $\mathcal E$. For every $i+1\le m$,
adjacent charts and representatives $x,x'$, and $z$, put
$r=\Xi_i(x,x';z)$ and $S=(t.O\,u\,\mu).S$. Then
$r\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\subset\mathbb C$ and
\[
            |\lambda(r)|_p\le1
     \quad\text{for every prime }p\notin S
      \text{ and every ring map }\lambda:\overline{\mathbb Q}\to\mathbb C_p .
\]

P107.statement:
Let a tied chain satisfy $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal M$. Fix
$i+1\le m$ with $i=m_2$, assume $\mathcal A_i$, and choose any charts
$\beta,\beta'$. Choose $x$ at the source, $x'$ at the target,
$k'\in K_{i+1,\beta'}$, and admissible points $p,p',p'_1$ above
$x,x',x'k'$ in the appropriate charts. Then for every chart
linear map $w$,
\[
 M_i(\det k')\,\sigma_0\!\left(\xi_i(p,p'_1;w)\right)
      =\chi_{i+1,\beta'}(k')\,\sigma_0\!\left(\xi_i(p,p';w)\right).
\]

P108.statement:
Let a tied chain satisfy $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal M$. For
$i+1\le m$ with $i=m_2$, assume $\mathcal A_i$ and choose charts
$\beta,\beta'$. For $k\in K_{i,\beta}$ and admissible points
$p,p_1,p'$ representing $x,xk,x'$ in their respective charts, one
has, for every chart linear map $w$,
\[
 \chi_{i,\beta}(k)\,\sigma_0\!\left(\xi_i(p_1,p';w)\right)
        =M_i(\det k)\,\sigma_0\!\left(\xi_i(p,p';w)\right).
\]

P109.statement:
For a tied chain and $i+1\le m$, take any adjacent pair of charts,
$x,x'$, $k\in K_{i,\beta}$ and $k'\in K_{i+1,\beta'}$. Suppose
$p,p',p_1,p'_1$ are admissible above $x,x',xk,x'k'$. Let
$d,d',d_1,d'_1$ be their decorations. For every chart linear map $z$,
\[
                   \phi_T(d_1,d'_1;z)=\phi_T(d,d';z).
\]
Here $\phi_T(d,d';z)$ takes the value $1$ precisely when, at every
level prime $P$, all $y$ in the decorated local domain of $d$ have
$zy$ in that of $d'$ and $f'_{P}(zy)=f_P(y)$, and it takes $0$
otherwise.

P110.statement:
For a tied chain and $i<m$ there are integers $e_\tau$ with
$e_\tau=h_{\tau,i}$ in $\mathbb Q$ for every $\tau$, such that for
all $z\in E^\times$ with $z\bar z=1$ and every rank-one unitary
finite adelic point $y$ with $\det y=z_f$,
\[
                         m_{i+1}(d(y))=\prod_\tau \tau(z)^{e_\tau}
                            \quad\text{in }\mathbb C.
\]

P111.statement:
For every tied chain, every $i<m$ and every rank-one unitary finite
adelic point $y$, the complex number $m_{i+1}(d(y))$ belongs to
$\overline{\mathbb Q}\subset\mathbb C$.

P112.statement:
For every tied chain, fix $i<m$ and a rank-one unitary finite adelic
point $y$. Suppose $\det y$ lies in the integral idele subgroup
$\mathrm{intU}$ and its component equals $1$ at every host place
$v$ below a transported prime in $S_B$. Then $m_{i+1}(d(y))=1$.

P113.statement:
In a tied chain satisfying $\mathcal M$, put $j=m_2+1$ and suppose
$j+1\le m$. In adjacent charts take $k\in K_{j,\beta}$ and
$k'\in K_{j+1,\beta'}$. For every $P\in S_B$, take chart linear
automorphisms $g_P,g'_P$ of the respective ranks and scalars $z_P,z'_P\in K_X$.
Assume the following.
\begin{itemize}
\item $(g_P,z_P)$ satisfies the middle-level relation in $\beta$ and
$g_P$ preserves the specified coset of $y_0(\beta,P)$. In the
reference frame $g_P$ matches $k$ to the assigned depth $D(P)$.
\item $(g'_P,z'_P)$ satisfies the top-level relation: its projection to
the upper coordinates intertwines with an element of the prescribed
top row group, it fixes the last coordinate functional, and $z'_P$ is
the corresponding row character value. In the target frame $g'_P$
matches $k'$ to the top depth (one at type primes, $2M$ otherwise).
\end{itemize}
Then, for the source and target determinant factors $\rho_S,\rho_T$
of step $j$,
\[
 M_j(\det k)\;
 \sigma_0\!\left(\prod_{P\in S_B}
       \rho_{S,j,P}(\det g_P)\rho_{T,j,P}(\det g'_P)\right)
       =M_j(\det k').
\]

P114.statement:
In a tied chain fix $j<m$ with $j\le m_2$, a chart $\beta$, a
representative $x$, and $\kappa\in K_{j,\beta}$. For any admissible
points $p,p_1$ above $x,x\kappa$ there exist, simultaneously for every
$P\in S_B$, locally integral invertible chart matrices $k_P$ and
$c_P\in K_X^\times$ with the following properties:
\begin{align*}
 F(p_1,P)&=F(p,P)\,k_P^{-1},\\
 \chi_{j,\beta}(\kappa)&=\sigma_0\!\left(\prod_{P\in S_B} c_P\right),
       &\det\kappa&\sim_P\det(k_P^{-1})\quad(P\in S_B).
\end{align*}
Moreover each $(k_P,c_P)$ satisfies the prescribed local level relation.
At a type prime the reduction of $k_P$ belongs to the specified
level subgroup and its character has value $c_P$. At a selected twist
prime outside the type primes, $k_P$ itself belongs to the specified
level subgroup and its character has value $c_P$.

P115.statement:
Let a tied chain satisfy $\mathcal M$. Take $i<m$ and, independently,
$j\le m$. Choose $\beta$ at $j$, a level element
$\kappa\in K_{j,\beta}$, and $e_P\in E_X$ for each $P\in S_B$.
If $\det\kappa\sim_P e_P$ for all $P$, put $b=M_i(\det\kappa)$.
Then
\[
 b\,\sigma_0\!\left(\prod_{P\in S_B}\rho_{S,i,P}(e_P)\right)=1,
 \qquad
 b=\sigma_0\!\left(\prod_{P\in S_B}\rho_{T,i,P}(e_P)\right).
\]

P116.statement:
In a tied chain fix $i+1\le m$, rational matrices $\gamma,\gamma'$
in the general linear groups of the respective stage ranks, and
standard unitary isometries $g,g'$ over $E_X$. Suppose
\[
 \iota(g)=C_i\gamma C_i^{-1},\qquad
 \iota(g')=C_{i+1}\gamma' C_{i+1}^{-1}.
\]
Let $f_i,f_{i+1}$ be the standard coordinate maps \code{toStdCo}
from the respective Gram forms and $C_i,C_{i+1}$, and define
$T(z)$ by transporting $f_{i+1}^{-1}\circ z\circ f_i$ to $E_X$.
For every $z:E^{N_i}\to E^{N_{i+1}}$,
\[
 T(z)=g'\circ T\bigl((\gamma'_{\rm std})^{-1}\circ z\circ
                         \gamma_{\rm std}\bigr)\circ g^{-1}.
\]
Here $\gamma_{\rm std},\gamma'_{\rm std}$ are the maps \code{stdG}
for the two rational matrices and Gram forms.

T01.statement:
Assume $P,F$, local matching, agreement of theta integrals, the closed
covolume bound of T13, the reciprocity existence assertion $h$, and the
primitive-character window with constant $401$. Then for every $N\ge1$,
every complex Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $N$, and every $s$ with
$\Re s>1/2$, one has $L(s,\chi)\ne0$ whenever $\chi\ne\chi_0$ or $s\ne1$.
Here $h$ chooses a compatible reciprocity map for each place over a nonzero
prime of a number field in its algebraic closure. The two theta assumptions
are the two conclusions stated in T11.

D001.statement: For every host and all allowed transported system constants, for every pair of further constants there is C>0 such that every admitted instance satisfying HI has meanKapT at depthD at most C(t+1)N\ensuremath{{}_{1}}/Y.

D002.statement: Assume global Artin reciprocity, local Tate duality and Euler characteristic. At each member with G1–G6, tame generators, its finite local, Fontaine, continuity, semisimplicity and coefficient conditions, the prescribed local lengths, lifts and TB bounds imply the global lattice-index estimate for the given constituent.

D003.statement: At each host the admitted base-level hypotheses imply the closed projection lemma: after the specified thresholds, the admissible weight data in the unramified quadratic setting satisfy the depth-t projection condition at every sufficiently large t.

P015.statement: Assume $\mathcal B,V,\mathcal F$. For every $\psi\in\mathcal P$ and every $s$ with $\Re s>1/2$, one has $L(s,\psi)\ne0$.

D004.statement: Every host with compatible local Wach, Fontaine and comparison data satisfies the full Delta-invariant norm-bound package: Wach freeness and characterization, P2–P9, semisimple Gamma quotient, Pr2a–Pr2d, the third lemma and Conclusion E.

D005.statement: For an unramified CM field over its real fixed field, the integral positive Hermitian lattice and the indicated orthogonal splitting of a nonzero-norm vector give the local density at a maximal prime: psiP equals the prescribed norm power times alphaStd times alphaN divided by alphaL.

D006.statement: For compatible local Wach/Fontaine data, the Bloch–Kato local, Tate duality and Euler-characteristic assumptions give both TBat on the specified tie and TBeAt for every good pair of local fields and index.

D007.statement: For every host, the extremal-projector tools imply the two covariant-degree conclusions and the hyperplane-rank assertion. The required positivity, integral-form weight conditions and exponent hypotheses are discharged for this same host.

D008.statement: For every compatible local Wach/Fontaine package, Bloch–Kato, local Tate duality and the Euler characteristic supply the auxiliary lifting bounds with fixed coefficients 10,23,32,32.

D009.statement: Uniformly for a reduced residue class and the specified exceptional-zero datum, for X at least a fixed power of the modulus, the difference between phi(M) times the prime count and the adjusted main term is bounded relatively by the sum of the two displayed decaying exponential errors.

D010.statement: There exist positive A,c,c\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} such that for d a prime at least 100 congruent to 3 modulo 4 and M\ensuremath{\ge}3, whenever log(4dM\ensuremath{{}^{2}})\ensuremath{\le}c sqrt(log X) and exp(\ensuremath{-}c sqrt(log X))\ensuremath{\le}h\ensuremath{\le}1, the interval [X,X(1+h)] contains at least c\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}hX/((4dM\ensuremath{{}^{2}})\textasciicircum{}A log X) designated norm primes.

D011.statement: For an unramified CM extension with fixed field F and rank m\ensuremath{\ge}2, assume the Hermitian representation and local density inputs. A positive mass constant c in rank m\ensuremath{-}1 gives mass constant c times the specified local-to-global mass ratio in rank m.

D012.statement: Finite Levi control implies the unfolding property for each word in every full Hida datum with normalized level and Wu decay.

D013.statement: Under the printed two-place Galois hypotheses choose A=6000 and B=30000. On every sufficiently large admissible family datum all twisted 2-places and all their good constituents satisfy the local vcc bound with costC(L,A,B,2), in the specified representation.

D014.statement: For each axial host on a frame the induced arithmetic data satisfy the host prime conditions with exceptional set consisting of its distinguished q and its given small primes.

D015.statement: Under the same two-place Galois hypotheses choose A=6000 and B=30000. On every sufficiently large admissible family datum the vcc bound with costC(L,A,B,3) holds for all good constituents at twisted 3-places outside the small set.

D016.statement: Assume 3 differs from the two host primes, and each of the separate 2- and 3-place estimates has nonnegative coefficients. Every family admits a common threshold and constant such that at twisted places of residue characteristic 2 or of residue characteristic 3 outside the designated small set, vcc is bounded by the representation contribution, the common middle term, VVr, the class-number contribution, and the local epsilon term.

P014.statement: Assume $\mathcal B,V,\mathcal F$. Then $H$ holds, with the principal-character exception in P003.

D017.statement: Under the two-place Galois hypotheses, each family has constants C,x\ensuremath{{}_{0}} valid for all eligible indices at scales x\ensuremath{\ge}x\ensuremath{{}_{0}}: at twisted places of residue characteristic 2 or of residue characteristic 3 outside the designated small set, vcc is bounded by the representation contribution, the common middle term, VVr, the class-number contribution, and the local epsilon term.

D018.statement: If membership of a family in C implies P(F,CH) for every epsilon and every real CH, then P is closed on C: there are common threshold functions imposing that implication on all sufficiently large qualifying families.

T02.statement:
Assume $P,F$, agreement of the theta integrals, local matching and T13's
covolume bound. For any reciprocity system $h$, suppose that for every real $c$
the closed family bound at two and three of T25 satisfies the linked norm
condition at $p(c)$. Then there exist a family class $\mathcal A$, a raw selection
of its bundles, a threshold function of two real variables, and all certificates
in \nolinkurl{HypsAlt} for the definite-side condition and $N(\mathcal C)
=\forall F_m\in\mathcal C,\ \mathrm{LinkN}(F_m)$.
The certificates include the existence and duty bounds, twists, row
primitivity and divisibility, spectral rows and counts, selected and twisted
periods, local kernels, masses and the remaining linkage. They belong to the
same selection. The proof takes the maximum of the evaluation-grid and
Fourier-fit thresholds before constructing it.

D019.statement: Under the indicated trace, classification, cusp, local and theta hypotheses, for a good level-three family with weak characterization, realization, parameter choice, full host coefficient field, guard and good types, the multiplicities of the prescribed twisted row data agree.

D020.statement: The two closed covariance and Siegel–Weil mass inputs, together with the lattice, determinant, measure, test kernel, congruence and row-representative conditions in the signature, give the normalized counting tie for the two rows with the explicit representative constant.

D021.statement: Uniformly in tied Hida row parameters satisfying the KTwo and concrete-tie conditions there are nonnegative constants for the type estimate; once the gap parameters exceed the specified successive thresholds, TypeAt holds for each word.

D022.statement: The given local theta inputs, equality of integrals, matching and LNe imply the tower statement for the specified families and scale.

D023.statement: Assume the ordinary and square theta matching and integral identities, square convergence and local inputs. At large admissible scales the row sums exist, squared test data and constants are nonzero, twisted characters satisfy the indicated independence condition, the two-sided row formula holds and the designated sums belong to the coefficient field.

D024.statement: The local theta inputs, smooth cuspidal lifts and existence of the row sums give the row unfolding identity at every admitted large-scale datum.

D025.statement: For the admissible even-rank, interlacing and half-integral discrete-series parameters in the two-unitary-group setup, there are vectors and group elements with a nonzero specified matrix-coefficient Bessel integral.

D026.statement: For every nonnegative weight exponent and each height parameter, there exist constants bounding the rotated-point sum uniformly over all hosts and all sufficiently large gap parameters as in theoremBRotated.

D027.statement: For the specified discrete series with sufficiently separated parameters and normalized K-finite coefficient, the pointwise coefficient bound holds uniformly beyond the common gap threshold, with the prescribed distinction according to agreement of the two signatures.

D028.statement: For the given compact Fourier-decay setup one obtains the radial test spaces satisfying the slice and level-zero composition formulas. For each admissible compactly supported operator-valued test function separated from the singular set, its transformed restriction is represented by an element of the level-zero space.

D029.statement: Under the admissible counting and tie hypotheses the group weights admit a positive rescaling equal to one on regular elements, with the uniform square bound. For each compatible local family and represented point the rescaled group sum equals its local weight–amplitude expression.

D030.statement: From the local theta input and existence of all row sums, the derivatives in the indicated successive jets satisfy the prescribed assembly identities.

D031.statement: Global Artin reciprocity implies rationality of the indicated good-cover series and the integrality assertion for the twisted series.

D032.statement: Assume cusp rapid decay, uniform size control, the specified level character and the family, model and theta-map conditions. For each index and parameter, the linear image of the finite theta transform equals the full prescribed wall subspace.

D033.statement: The convergent unitary Siegel–Weil input supplies a common nonnegative row-error constant and two largeness thresholds for each set of admissible parameters. Every tied, standard two-word datum satisfying Hyp0 and absolute convergence has the required nondiagonal row bound with that error scale.

D034.statement: Given the real Howe, matching, local theta, join, functional-equation, ordinary and square integral, square convergence and separation hypotheses, there is a threshold valid for every larger grid constant. At sufficiently large admissible contexts, after the finite algebraic and prime exclusions, every admissible initial grid admits a full grid with the same key.

D035.statement: Assume the unitary Siegel set, real Howe duality, Green cuspidal input, local theta inputs, the join, the Hecke functional equation, ordinary integral agreement/local matching and separating functionals. At each indicated datum there is a finite separating family of complex linear forms on the row output whose values on every indicated rational test vector lie in the distinguished embedded coefficient field.

D036.statement: Assume discrete-series cover, Harish–Chandra modules, cusp decay, Casselman–Wallach, the ray class field statement and a uniform constant-function fit. For every sufficiently large grid parameter and allowed extension refining its list, openness supplies linked rows with the required eventual functional identities for the same chosen summands on divisible families.

D037.statement: Under the unitary Siegel-set and local theta inputs, at a signature (r\ensuremath{-}p,p) and target rank less than 2(r\ensuremath{-}p), every indicated theta test function satisfies the moderate integrability requirement for the prescribed Weil representation and Haar fundamental domain.

D038.statement: Under the ordinary and square theta hypotheses and square convergence, beyond a uniform family threshold the square datum is nonzero and the distinguished row constant c(i,j,t) is nonzero at all indices.

D039.statement: Keep the reciprocity choice, auxiliary extension and geometric class fixed. If the new norm-choice condition gives a witness of the old one at every datum, every old linked row transfers to the new parameters for every row predicate, and every old open-parameter package transfers as well.

D040.statement: Given the projection, flip, unfolding and jet identities, row-constant nonvanishing and summability, each admissible coefficient-field datum admits parameters realizing its principal-level row formula.

D041.statement: Assume the four archimedean representation inputs, ray class field input and closed covolume estimate. For every allowed refinement of the origin choices, open parameters imply linked rows whose selected third-place summands satisfy the eventual L3 volume bound with common constants.

D042.statement: Local theta inputs and cuspidality of these lifts imply the coefficient test ConvK for all allowed rows and words at large parameters.

D043.statement: For every sufficiently large admissible family, all row sums for every parameter and every supplied test vector satisfy the specified summation conditions.

D044.statement: From the local theta inputs and ordinary agreement and local matching obtain square-model integral agreement. Each matched datum has a nonzero scalar such that each second-space vector has an integrable representative modulo finite coinvariant relations, and matching first-space vectors have integrals related by that scalar.

D045.statement: Each indicated twisted theta lift from the local input package is cuspidal in the smooth family model.

T03.statement:
Assume $P$ and row rationality: every datum in the starting row test with the
prescribed group, geometric, weight and residue-characteristic conditions passes
the rational row test. Fix a reciprocity system $h$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and an
eventually large retwisting predicate $A$. Suppose the small-prime norm bound
is linked at $p(c)$, and the functional inequality of T10 and covolume
inequality of T13 are linked in their row versions at $p_A(c)$.
Then the definite-side family, selection and certificates of T02 exist.
The two types of parameter have distinct roles in this implication.

D046.statement: Under the rank, Witt decomposition, additive and Hecke character, covolume-one measure and Weil-action hypotheses, every allowed continuation has zero Laurent coefficients of order at least two at t/2. Any compactly ranged integrable test annihilating all smaller-space theta kernels also annihilates the first Laurent coefficient there.

D047.statement: Assume the non-endoscopic automorphy hypotheses and the geometric Galois comparison. The elliptic hypothesis, the published third-layer inputs and the series condition then hold. There is a single choice of local Langlands parameters satisfying the required archimedean comparison, conjugate-dual stability, point condition and cuspidal parameter condition.

D048.statement: For every real-place instance with tied character frame/tuple, the cusp-decay, unramified Howe and geometric Galois compatibility assumptions imply: at each indexed pair, an admissible simultaneous eigenvector of the good type whose theta image is zero is itself zero.

D049.statement: With the indicated local theta, Harish–Chandra finiteness and cusp-decay inputs, every linked host realizing the jump cardinalities satisfies the prescribed pointwise theta and local parameter conditions.

D050.statement: If twice the column rank is below the Hermitian rank, the additive character, infinite datum and both given covolume-one measures admit the required fiber measure/data at each nonsingular Hermitian target matrix.

D051.statement: Cusp decay, local doubling integrals, the unramified doubling identity, partial Hecke continuation and unramified Howe duality imply injectivity of the indicated lift, together with its nonvanishing and typewise kernel criterion at every index for the given full face.

D052.statement: For an admissible full face and the unramified Howe input, if a vector has NoChi and every downward integral against all finite-type tests and all indicated linear forms and translates vanishes, then no prescribed lift of this vector is nonzero.

D053.statement: At rank p\ensuremath{\ge}1 and every compact set of group translates, the spherical height series is summable for p/2<sigma\ensuremath{\le}p/2+1, and (sigma\ensuremath{-}p/2) times its sum is bounded uniformly over translates and sigma.

D054.statement: For an admissible full face, if the finite theta transform of y is zero then all downward integrals against every finite-type test, linear form and translate vanish.

D055.statement: Given CM mass ratios, thin scales, decay, finite row dimension, row positivity and both row estimates, volume ties, genus mass at rank two, and the base, extension, bundle and all-row hypotheses with the same slots and normalizations, there exists one definite-side record with those prescribed predicates.

D056.statement: For definite base change and the stated local representation hypotheses, an automorphically realized side compatible with the given Galois and Weil–Deligne ties satisfies the first spherical inert-place conclusion.

D057.statement: For the indicated pinned column system with good laws and later data, a tied character tuple with the specified characters and standard columns and levels has symmetric twisted columns at the primes with the required standard twisted-chain conditions.

D058.statement: For the specified base, field/frame, ramification, prime selection, character set and ambient datum there is one good column input with exactly that frame, set, character range, selected primes and ambient form; its listed lengths equal the terminal rank and its depth off the distinguished primes is twice that rank.

D059.statement: Assume the Bernstein–Zelevinsky finiteness and polynomial-ring statements. For an irreducible automorphic subrepresentation containing the specified nonzero level/type vector, every compatible local factor at a split place over the given level place has toral class.

D060.statement: The third-layer and series hypotheses supply at every selected member a Galois side with the prescribed frame in both its character-frame and lambda fields, and compatible nonempty Galois–local comparison data.

D061.statement: For the admitted staged tuple, the required matrix-state data can be chosen with the specified character at each designated prime and with every listed local vector frame equal to an identity frame for the transported form.

D062.statement: For the indicated finite product group with the stated good-idempotent hypotheses, an irreducible character on which the selected idempotent has full trace splits pointwise as a product of cuspidal characters of the individual finite general linear factors.

D063.statement: If the designated idempotents exist, then in any allowed orbital measure over a nonsingular target the set where the idempotent action is not free has measure zero.

D064.statement: From convergent unitary Siegel–Weil, the fixed volume tie on every host implies the rank-drop volume-ratio formula for the orthogonal complement of a unit vector of either allowed sign in rank at least three. The complement has the rank and signatures prescribed by the sign.

D065.statement: Under the convergent unitary Siegel–Weil input, each admissible set of parameters has a common nonnegative constant and two thresholds for the diagonal row estimate. The bound applies to tied one-word data satisfying the counting conditions, concrete tie and absolute convergence.

D066.statement: From the idempotent, generation and majorization hypotheses, for a Weil representation with the specified character and normalized measure there is a finite exception set; every good section is fixed by every allowed compact factor outside every larger set.

D067.statement: If the indicated idempotents exist, each allowed infinite datum and Schwartz function has a finite exceptional set; after enlarging it, the function is good for every associated idempotent.

D068.statement: From the non-endoscopic automorphy and geometric Galois hypotheses one obtains the elliptic, third-layer and series conditions and one common choice of local Langlands parameters satisfying the local hypothesis.

D069.statement: For any host, every everywhere positive-definite Hermitian space of rank two with the prescribed signature condition and starting lattice has genus mass equal to the host mass factor at two.

D070.statement: At every finite set of places there exists an allowed adelic idempotent e. Every such e satisfies e\ensuremath{{}^{2}}=e and is fixed by the specified conjugation cA.

D071.statement: The marked hypotheses give every primitive character its exponent-401 window, using the K-bound, marked lifts, symplectic density, the Kato input, the four character counts and their combination.

D072.statement: For an ordinary determinant ring at matching level with the stated residual and local conditions, automorphic support implies the required patching support condition on the given ideal.

D073.statement: At the prescribed split, deep and Iwahori places, a rank-two eigenform produces either a rank-three form with eigenvalue triples (a,1,a inverse), or a rank-two form of the stipulated doubled weight with squared eigenvalues at the Iwahori places.

D074.statement: The rank-n record gives an exponent-401 window for each primitive character by applying weak unitary descent to obtain the marked hypotheses and then the height-window implication.

D075.statement: On the ordinary deformation space in ranks two through four, a locally generic automorphic parallel-weight point satisfies the adjoint vanishing condition under the stipulated Hida and residual restrictions.

D076.statement: Under the marked automorphy, multiplicity and companion hypotheses, every eligible residual rank-three ordinary determinant ring and weight object admit an ideal satisfying the specified modularity and numerical conditions together.

P027.statement:
Let \(O\) be a complete characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring and
\(K\) an algebraically closed extension of its fraction field with
valuation \(v\) extending the normalized order. Let \(A=\bigoplus_j A_j\)
be graded, with marked \(O\)-point \(x\) zero on nonzero weights.
Its degree-zero algebra is Noetherian, complete local, with local
structure map surjective on residue fields. It generates \(A\) together
with finitely many elements of weights \(-2,-1,1,2\).
Let \(I\) be generated by lists of weights \((-1,-2,1,2,0)\) and sizes
\((r+1,s,r',s',m)\); denote the first list by \(F\), and assume the
weight-zero equations vanish at \(x\). Put
\[
 P=\{b\in A:\,tb\in(\ker x)^2\text{ for some }0\ne t\in O\},
 \qquad L_j=\operatorname{im}(A_j\cap\ker x\longrightarrow A/P).
\]
Assume \(r\ge1\) and the smooth graded chart \(M_1\): its variable
counts in the five weights are \((r,s,r'+1,s'+1,m)\); individual
linear coordinates can be isolated, and vanishing of the linear
part on \(\ker x\) implies membership in \(P\). The negative and
weight-zero equation lists span the corresponding cotangent lattices
over the fraction field. Assume the image of \(A_0\) in \(A/I\)
is finite over \(O\). In what follows take \(K\)-points of \(A/I\).
For each point vanishing on both signs other
than \(x_K\), at least one strictly one-sided sign is absent in its
fibre over \(A_0\). At every two-sided point (nonzero on some element
of each sign), point derivations killing \(I\) have dimension at most
one. Let \(a\in A_0\) vanish at \(x\) and be nonzero at all two-sided
points. There exists a finite set of two-sided points meeting every
such \(K^\times\)-orbit. For every such cover \(T\),
\[
 L=\operatorname{length}_O(L_{-1}/\langle\overline F_i\rangle)
 <\infty,\qquad L\le 2\sum_{\xi\in T}v(\xi(a)).
\]

D077.statement: At split primes satisfying the slope test, every sufficiently large weight of the correct parity gives the specified Eisenstein lift with its local conditions and unlinked adjoint.

P020.statement: Assume the local, automorphy, cohomological and CM input records of \code{LiteratureRankNHypothesis}, the existence of one $C_K\in\mathbb R$ satisfying \code{LemmaK}, and the four bounds \code{CountI}, \code{CountII}, \code{CountIII}, \code{CountV} of \nolinkurl{HeightAndVanishing/Counts.lean:53--69}. Then the assertion $V$ above holds for every primitive $\psi$. In \code{LemmaK} the same $C_K$ bounds the log cardinality of the finite group $H^2(\mathrm{zlTw}(D,j+1))$ by $\exp((2j[L:\mathbb Q])^{C_K}\log(2|\operatorname{disc}L|))$ for every prime $\ell$, every admissible totally complex field $L$ with the required root of unity, closure and local datum $D$, and every $j\ge1$ (\nolinkurl{LemmaK.lean:9--17}).

D078.statement: For the indicated local representations and subgroups at the Taylor–Wiles places, if every residue-field cardinality is a coefficient-ring unit then there is a simultaneous family of operators satisfying all theta-level identities.

D079.statement: The transfer, modularity, level, weight, pro-modular, rank-three density, seed, twist, tangent and threshold inputs give unlinked points for the indicated linked even-level CM data.

D080.statement: Over totally complex quadratic extensions, a rank-positive cusp form spherical below some ramified place of the extension admits a cuspidal lift with the specified local and infinite base-change data.

D081.statement: Given the marked automorphy hypotheses, every rank-positive residual representation at unitary Hida level admits compatible Hecke data for the chosen auxiliary places, coefficient embedding and weight object.

D082.statement: For the specified embedding and compatible local restriction maps, a continuous cocycle satisfies the Bloch–Kato finite condition after restriction precisely when its pullback to the indicated decomposition subgroup satisfies that condition.

D083.statement: If the rank-two space has finite weight map and all components good, a rank-three space over a large admissible frame satisfying finite weight, the two propagation conditions and the seed condition has all components good and satisfies the off-locus finiteness condition.

P024.statement:
Assume the automorphic hypotheses \(H'\) together with weak descent,
cyclic base change and quadratic descent, the specified quaternion
existence theorem, and real semisimplicity of the cusp data.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every admitted CM field \(K\), coefficient ring, nonzero level,
weight parameter, character and marked datum \(D\), every
\(\iota:\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\simeq\mathbb C\), and every valuation
above \(\ell\), there is a single \(g_1\) satisfying the marking equations
for \(D\), the finiteness condition \(\mathrm{FinEnd}\), and both automorphic
end conditions, of ranks three and two respectively.
\item Suppose also that \([K:\mathbb Q]=2\) and \(K\) contains a root
of \(X^2+1\). For every admitted host datum and host frame \(F\) there
is a marked \(g_1\) such that for each universal representation \(u\)
at that mark, its weight-zero part is finite as a module over the
coefficient ring. At every Type~I specialization \(r\) of \(u\), the
indicated matrix representation satisfies the prescribed
automorphy condition over \(K\) with twist \(-1\).
\end{enumerate}

D084.statement: Under the global and local cohomology inputs, a potentially crystalline linked rank-three local point with the specified character-ratio coincidence admits two linearly independent tangent derivations trivial on the prescribed inertia characters.

D085.statement: For the prescribed level module and auxiliary places away from p, uniformizers and generators of the local quotient, the stated level conditions supply the two compatible maps on the same module.

D086.statement: The global cohomological hypotheses give, for every admissible generator datum and nonzero integer Q, a frame for the same sign, character, marking, valuation, level and Q.

D087.statement: A regular algebraic cuspidal GL(2) representation over a totally real field with a totally imaginary quadratic extension either admits the corresponding quadratic self-twist or has a cuspidal base change to that extension.

D088.statement: The indicated unitary multiplicity is uniform across admissible decompositions: the number of summands lying over the fixed representation is independent of the chosen realization with the imposed local fixed vectors.

D089.statement: Each quadratic-field datum in the totally real to totally complex theta construction admits the requested Weil model with compatible operators, their relations, the Gaussian action and the auxiliary integral data.

D090.statement: At a split place with the specified local matrix embedding, the Whittaker function of every element in the theta span, translated by any adelic h and restricted to the local GL(2), belongs to the matrix-coefficient space of the original cuspidal representation.

D091.statement: Under the stated rank-n inputs and spectral-output hypothesis, a qualifying regular rank-two system yields either a rank-three unitary representation with reciprocal character-ratio components or a rank-two representation realizing the squared ratios at almost all prescribed places.

D092.statement: For the specified local deformation setup, construct graded generators, relations and matrix entries so that the number of variables of each weight is the dimension of its first-cohomology space and the corresponding relation count is the dimension of its obstruction space.

D093.statement: Under the printed patching-module hypotheses, matching Hida level and the prescribed alternating-level condition imply automorphic support at the given ordinary determinant-ring ideal.

D094.statement: For the stated equivariant map of local p-adic representations, surjectivity lifts finite cocycles; for an injection with positive target the finite-cocycle condition is detected after applying the injection.

D095.statement: The pure-weight compatibility and unitary adjoint lift give conjugate-self-dual automorphy and the required local weights for the inverse-cyclotomic twist of the trace-zero adjoint of every eligible rank-two representation.

D096.statement: For a standard residual frame of a compact totally disconnected group over a complete coefficient DVR with finite residue field there exists a framed deformation space with its specified universal and graded data.

D097.statement: For the universal ordinary rank-three local datum the saturated ideal has both crystalline-locus properties: its characteristic-zero points satisfy the specified crystalline condition and the admissible crystalline test lifts kill the ideal.

D098.statement: For a continuous representation through the specified finite-level local map, H1 and H2 are finite-dimensional; their dimensions satisfy the local Euler formula with the residue-characteristic contribution and H2 has the dimension of the cyclotomically twisted dual invariants.

D099.statement: For a finite-index subgroup of rational GL(n) over a totally real or totally complex field, cohomology at principal level 3M with a d-dimensional coefficient system is bounded by c times M to a fixed power times d, uniformly in M and the coefficient representation.

D100.statement: With the indicated field and character triples, split ramification, parity and residual inertia conditions, a qualifying rank-two Eisenstein lift acquires the prescribed adjoint-input conditions after restriction and a character twist.

D101.statement: Over a totally real field, two rank-n cuspidal GL representations with a common Satake multiset at all but finitely many finite places are isomorphic in the adelic and archimedean model.

D102.statement: The classical automorphy record gives the rank-three trace-counting bound over an imaginary quadratic field: an integer of controlled height simultaneously bounds products of differences from the Eisenstein trace for all admissible pairwise inequivalent families.

D103.statement: For a totally complex base with a cyclic prime-degree extension, the regular cuspidal Satake and infinitesimal systems have the stated norm-character self-twist or a weak cuspidal base change with the prescribed weights.

D104.statement: The marked hypotheses with the Galois row imply rank-three density in the seed problem: above every weight threshold some weight in the prescribed congruence class supports an irreducible rank-three seed.

D105.statement: Assuming the printed Hida inputs, an admissible odd-prime rank-two representation gives a conjugate-self-dual automorphic realization of its trace-zero adjoint twisted by inverse cyclotomic, with the additional weight conditions at all specified places.

D106.statement: The marked hypotheses imply adjoint Selmer vanishing at a parallel locally generic automorphic point of a universal ordinary determinant ring in ranks two through four, with the stated level, residual and coefficient conditions.

D107.statement: Uniform second cohomology and the stated dualities force a continuous cocycle for the inverse of an open-kernel character times a positive cyclotomic twist, locally a coboundary on inertia, to be a global coboundary.

D108.statement: For an odd prime and a nontrivial character of order prime to it whose reduction differs from cyclotomic, a unit first Bernoulli value for the inverse character forces every residual cocycle satisfying UnrEv to be a coboundary.

D109.statement: In the divisible coefficient module of a finite coefficient DVR, every cyclic submodule has finite length, every element is killed by a power of p, multiplication by a nonzero scalar is surjective, and the kernel length is its valuation.

D110.statement: Unit norm of the generalized first Bernoulli value and the residual cocycle criterion imply that for the prescribed product character or its inverse every unramified even cocycle is a coboundary.

D111.statement: Assume semisimplicity and admissibility for totally real cusp forms. A newform of weight k at least two and each integral twist j determine a rank-two rational cusp form with weights 1/2+j and 3/2-k+j and the prescribed good-prime Hecke polynomial.

D112.statement: Uniform second cohomology, Poitou–Tate, local finiteness and local Tate duality imply finite Selmer length in every positive twist of every integral character with open kernel over a number field.

D113.statement: For a coefficient DVR finite over the p-adic integers, the structure map is injective and local, the ring is free and adically complete, and the index equals the quotient length and valuation of p, is nonzero and bounded by the rank. Integers prime to p are units.

D114.statement: For a common open-image record, isobaric base change, a normalized Galois row and the CM record, every primitive character has the simultaneous Selmer window with twist exponent 401.

D115.statement: From open image obtain the common cohomology record: global and local finiteness, Euler characteristics, normalised Poitou–Tate and local Tate duality, unramified orthogonality, Greenberg–Wiles comparison and Bloch–Kato local conditions.

D116.statement: From the open-image record obtain the local GL representation package, including constituent finiteness, reducibility and segment classification, Jacquet modules, local converse, depth-zero and the remaining local-field inputs.

D117.statement: Open image, isobaric base change and the normalized Galois row supply the automorphic record, with cuspidal finiteness, multiplicity and purity, algebraic character comparison, local Galois properties and both supplied rows.

W01.statement:
Assume the one-field open-image record with field $\mathcal R$, the
isobaric base-change assertion W02, and the Galois row for local
parameters satisfying \code{IsRecT}. For each primitive character, each
$0<\varepsilon<1/52$ and each admissible page function, the window $V$
of \nodeid{P013} holds. In particular a single $[Y,Y^2]$ works for all
prescribed fields, all local data, and every finite set of primes, with
twist cutoff $\lfloor x^{401}\rfloor$ and bound $\exp(x^\varepsilon/2)$.

D118.statement: From the open-image record obtain the CM hypotheses: deformation and de Rham comparison for abelian varieties, dual crystalline data, reduction, the elliptic CM and class-field formulas, and the required zeta and Hecke functional equations.

D119.statement: For even level, the marked automorphy hypotheses turn a linked Galois datum in a large admissible CM frame with its seed clause into an unlinked point.

D120.statement: The marked hypotheses supply unramified adjoint-lifting inputs jointly: the printed local and global cohomology, unitary modularity, level, weight-character and residual base data.

D121.statement: Assuming the rank-n local, automorphic, Galois-cohomological and CM inputs, the exponent-401 window holds for each primitive Dirichlet character.

D122.statement: The printed automorphy hypotheses produce arbitrarily high admissible weights in the prescribed congruence class, carrying irreducible rank-three Galois seeds with the required residual characters, twists and local restrictions.

T13.statement:
Assume resolution, principalisation, integrated Poincaré--Lelong, the three
Hilbert--Samuel statements, the arithmetic bigness bound, Hodge--Tate
orthogonality, the Zarhin splitting and nef Riemann--Roch (T17--T24).
Assume also integral Siegel toroidal models, the toroidal-fan input for KS,
seminegativity of the semiabelian Lie bundle, separation of pairs of
points, arithmetic degree, the 28 Hodge-bundle inputs, and Grothendieck
deformation. There exists $\varepsilon_1>0$ such that for each
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_1$ there is a largeness parameter $K$.
For every family $F$ at $\varepsilon$ and real $H$ with
$\mathrm{FamHyp}(F)$ and $F.\mathrm{Large}(K,H)$, there are
$C_0\ge0$ and $x_0$ such that, for $x>x_1$ with $x\ge x_0$, every family
index and point $p$ with the point conditions and reciprocity tie (\nolinkurl{RowsTAlt}), every
$C\ge C_0$ and every $j$, the false-side row satisfies
\[
   \operatorname{lcv}(XW_j,M_j)/D\ \le\ N(C)_{L3,j}.
\]
The normalization $D$, row space and lattice in this expression belong to $p$.

D123.statement: Give an adelic norm to the flat generator. Its degree is (p\ensuremath{-}q)/2 times the real CM period logarithm plus q times twice the logarithm of the square root of d minus the logarithm of the root discriminant.

D124.statement: For every CM field and every admissible host, the finite-place constancy condition holds simultaneously for that host.

D125.statement: For each permitted specialization of the germ system, the power functions, generic point condition, characteristic-zero height hypothesis and fibre hypotheses imply freeness of the indicated order-r height system.

D126.statement: There are analytic eigenframes of ranks p and q realizing the two specified bases at each point; evaluation of the section equals the fixed scalar times its frame function.

D127.statement: The cardinality of the set of small sections for the given weight and power 8i is at most the cardinality of the small sections of the shifted Hermitian line bundle to power 8i.

D128.statement: The common theta scalar is a unit at the valued points of each admissible integral model with the level structure, splitting and regularity conditions.

D129.statement: Injectivity on the tangent characteristic factor implies conjugate injectivity for the point germ in residue characteristic p.

D130.statement: At each point of the open parameter set, a smooth group and the holomorphic variation of its base points give a family exponential on a smaller positive-radius ball.

D131.statement: Under the stated generic-point and closed-constant conditions, the zero set of the uniformizer in the chosen coefficient embedding is connected.

D132.statement: On the logarithmic cover of the punctured polydisc there is a holomorphic lattice basis with the prescribed period relations and a polynomial bound on the restricted strip.

D133.statement: For each allowed component, toroidal flag and weight, the boundary vanishing order is bounded by the dimension of the indicated space of sections.

D134.statement: An analytic unit frame function admits nonzero scalar multiples with the required flat restrictions for every component in the given cover.

D135.statement: For a characteristic-p curve with its weighted valuations and the given family with number-ring action, assume all multiplication characteristic polynomials split over the field and every valuation bounds the character values by one. If matrices express the transported local H-bases in a global H-basis modulo the character eigenspace, all determinants are nonzero, only finitely many have valuation other than one, and the weighted sum of their logarithmic valuations is zero.

D136.statement: For a projective normal scheme X over a field with a finite affine cover carrying the stated compatible coordinate, coefficient and determinant data, there exist a normal scheme Z proper over X, the indicated family of maps from Z to projective spaces, and affine chart maps satisfying the Plücker formulas. The chart maps are open immersions and cover Z. A map into Z from any test scheme is determined by its composite to X and all of its projective components.

D137.statement: Given a good embedding, uniformization, compatible analytic arc and matching eigenframe on the punctured ball, and a lifted orbit, each vector v in E\textasciicircum{}N and strip width R admit constants C and B such that eventually as Im(w) tends to infinity in |Re(w)| \ensuremath{\le} R every marked period coefficient of v has absolute value at most C Im(w)\textasciicircum{}B, uniformly over all embeddings of E and coefficient indices.

D138.statement: The designated arc has a holomorphic lift to the prescribed orbit of adapted frames.

D139.statement: On a smooth proper complex scheme, local holomorphic functions satisfying the given line-bundle transition law are represented by an algebraic section with those values.

D140.statement: For the specified semiabelian family with compatible CM involution on a locally Noetherian scheme, assume every power operation induces a bijection on global functions, and the characteristic-zero point satisfies the stipulated generic-point condition. Its Lie space admits coordinates of some finite dimension d supporting a compatible system of germs.

D141.statement: Fix CM moduli data of positive signature sum, a coefficient field and a model over a Noetherian subring whose fraction field is the coefficient field. Assume the restriction-of-scalars and GAGA section comparisons, a geometric compactification over the specified open set, and two embeddings that send the chosen root to the prescribed complex value. For an analytic unit frame function and a line frame function flat on the model, one nonzero complex scalar multiplies the former to the latter at every framed complex point over that open.

D142.statement: Base change of a group realized by a split torus extension again has such a realization.
