The new character lattice identifies with the old one, the abelian part identifies as a group with the pullback, and for each character the line-bundle isomorphism preserves the specified generator.

D143.statement: The stated geometric condition on the positive-characteristic fibre implies the associated condition on its tangent action.

D144.statement: At each point of the base of the stated CM moduli flag model, there is an affine open neighbourhood whose preimage in the flag model carries an ample line bundle of the specified weight. Its first block is zero and its flag entry indexed by an embedding and position j is the corresponding multiplicity minus j.

D145.statement: The degree of the given line on the special fibre satisfies the displayed relation under the marked model and base change.

D146.statement: Let U be the unit ball with the first a coordinate divisors removed. Suppose a rank-2g free integral lattice with perfect alternating form has local holomorphic markings of period groups Gamma(z), polarized by positive Hermitian forms H(z). Assume the central subgroup spans the complex fiber, has additive holomorphic lifts to the ball, contains all central limits of continuous-at-zero period sections, and for each N>0 admits a subset T of its quotient modulo N with |Gamma0/N| times |T| equal to N\textasciicircum{}(2g) whose representatives pair with all lifted central periods in N times the integers. Then there is a logarithmic period datum with Hermitian form H whose period image at every log-cover point is Gamma at its exponential image.

D147.statement: Assume embedded resolution and GAGA for sections. Let the component be geometrically admissible over a noetherian domain with the prescribed fraction field, p+q \ensuremath{\ge} 1, and τ a selected CM embedding. For a frame function that defines a line and is flat on this model, conjugate embeddings admit the same archimedean norm parameter. On each uniformizing family of the prescribed type whose corresponding period points lie in the chosen open, the frame function is a flat generator.

D148.statement: For a family in characteristic p and each indexed valuation, the maps alpha and beta preserve the two designated lattices and beta after alpha is zero. There exist lattice-preserving maps r and s with r after alpha and beta after s both identities and alpha after r plus s after beta equal to the identity.

D149.statement: A wedge of the chosen eigenframes yields a frame function in the indicated eigenline representing the two geometric sections.

D150.statement: For a semiabelian group over a scheme and a complex point of the base, let e from complex g-space onto the complex fibre be a surjective holomorphic additive parametrization, sending addition to the group law. Suppose its differential at zero assigns a unique tangent vector to each direction and identifies the directions bijectively with the tangent vectors at e(0). The complex linear span of its period subgroup, the kernel of e, is all of complex g-space.

D151.statement: Let a geometric integral model of the specified compactification lie over a Noetherian ring embedded in the coefficient field as a ring of fractions, and choose an embedding tau with the prescribed value on the distinguished root. Two frame functions satisfying the line-function and flatness conditions differ by one nonzero scalar from the coefficient field, uniformly after every field extension and on every admissible framed point.

D152.statement: Assume extension on Riemann slices, the punctured exponential order assertion, and descent from the logarithmic cover. For every period polydisc, each real monodromy matrix B(i) is positive semidefinite, and the corrected period matrix tau0 is the pullback under the exponential covering of a matrix whose entries are analytic on a neighborhood of each point of the unit ball.

D153.statement: For every admissible point and dominant weight there is an auxiliary dominant weight with sections at the auxiliary and total weights both nonvanishing at that same point.

D154.statement: Slicing the first block of the Chow form by a hyperplane gives, up to a nonzero scalar, the product of the component Chow forms raised to the intersection multiplicities.

D155.statement: The published Hodge-bundle package gives the Fubini–Study expression for the height of the common Chow form.

D156.statement: The given homogeneous integral prime ideal has a Chow form of the prescribed Hilbert degree, unique up to multiplication by a nonzero field scalar.

D157.statement: The toroidal Kodaira–Spencer hypothesis supplies compatible boundary charts for the specified fan, together with its positivity and boundary conditions.

D158.statement: The representation, congruence, crystalline, jump, Frobenius, cutting, twisting, cardinality and subrepresentation compatibility assertions hold together for the selected geometric data.

D159.statement: The holomorphic fixed-point formula gives all six Kodaira–Spencer requirements on the level system, including goodness, congruences and its Hodge occurrences.

D160.statement: For every admitted Harris–Taylor datum and level N\ensuremath{\ge}3 prime to p there exists a representing family whose structure map is quasi-projective.

D161.statement: At every good place over \ensuremath{\ell} the jumps prescribed by the geometric Hodge data occur in the selected representation.

D162.statement: The holomorphic Lefschetz and fixed-point packets give the Hodge occurrences in the chosen tower and its conjugate weight.

D163.statement: For the specified compact and Hecke data the fixed-point trace equals the weighted sum with the stated level indices, character and central terms.

D164.statement: For a smooth projective complex scheme, a finite étale correspondence with finitely many transverse fixed points satisfies the holomorphic Lefschetz trace identity in each Hodge degree.

D165.statement: The prescribed representation space has a common plan realizing both sets of Hodge data and a plan simultaneously satisfying the Hodge and congruence conditions.

D166.statement: The étale cohomology hypotheses D1–D3 and E1–E3, with the preceding assumptions in the exact signature, imply the E4 comparison.

D167.statement: For the specified henselian étale-cover presentation the degree-one twisted cohomology of the generic fibre is subsingleton.

D168.statement: The joint inputs for the Künneth and Lefschetz comparison on the chosen cohomology complexes are available.

D169.statement: The integral model, open-and-closed generic-fibre comparison, finite-level models, quotients, normalization and base-change compatibilities can be chosen together.

D170.statement: From the holomorphic finite-étale Lefschetz formula, obtain the simultaneous odd-rank weight-one Galois realization with the prescribed good primes, Hodge jumps and Frobenius conditions.

D171.statement: The projective bundle formula on each specified space expresses its twisted étale cohomology via pullback and the powers of the tautological first Chern class.

D172.statement: When the Harris–Taylor datum is compact, the structure map of its prime-to-p model of level at least three is projective.

D173.statement: The given étale package gives invariance of cohomology after the specified proper family is restricted to the residue field of the local base.

D174.statement: For the given endomorphism, the de Rham homology characteristic polynomial is the image of the integral characteristic polynomial for the \ensuremath{\ell}-adic endomorphism.

D175.statement: For each Harris–Taylor base of the stated type and level N\ensuremath{\ge}3 prime to p, there exists an integral model.

D176.statement: The Frobenius condition for the representation follows at the selected place from the congruence polynomial and its specified multiset of roots.

D177.statement: For the indicated projective space and its tautological line, the d-th power of its de Rham first Chern class is nonzero.

D178.statement: For a place over \ensuremath{\ell} admitting a surjective cover as specified, the geometric representation satisfies the crystalline condition there.

D179.statement: The specified Harris–Taylor isogenies of type Tj are represented compatibly with their two maps, levels and pullbacks.

D180.statement: The divided-power filtration and descent data give the local Rees-module relation for each bounded small chart.

D181.statement: The étale-side comparison for the indicated smooth models supplies all three conclusions: crystallinity, de Rham comparison and Frobenius comparison.

D182.statement: For a finite-type Dedekind domain B over an algebraically closed field k and nonzero q invertible in k, H\ensuremath{{}^{n}}(Spec B,Z/q(i)) vanishes in all degrees n \ensuremath{\ge} 2 and twists i.

D183.statement: Under the eleven listed étale-cohomology inputs, for any smooth X over an absolutely integrally closed local domain T and any nonzero q invertible in T, restriction to the generic fibre of X induces a bijection on étale cohomology in every degree and twist.

D184.statement: If A is a commutative ring henselian along an ideal I and the natural number q is a unit in A, restriction from Spec A to Spec(A/I) is a bijection on étale cohomology with coefficients in the i-th Tate twist of Z/q, for every cohomological degree and every integer i.

D185.statement: A good group at the prime of the reflex datum makes the corresponding place of the finite-level Kodaira–Spencer tower good.

D186.statement: The following 34 inputs to the Künneth–Lefschetz argument hold together: excision and pairs, projective-space and hyperplane facts, finite covers and fibres, components, ring and low-degree calculations, towers, affine vanishing, twists and Gysin maps, the limit and quotient maps, Künneth bijectivity and external products, interchange and slicing, integration at a point, detection and duality, finite support, projective-space classes, injectivity, trace comparison, divisors, and the basis and top-degree decompositions. Each input retains the hypotheses in its own statement.

D187.statement: On each specified rational base and at every index there exists a Kodaira–Spencer object in the given system.

D188.statement: The output period-ring data satisfy the indicated divided-power and filtration descent conditions at \ensuremath{\ell}.

D189.statement: The indicated level object and its generic-fibre group identification extend to an object over the discrete valuation base, with an object map on the generic fibre.

D190.statement: There are ample divisors on the allowed smooth models, with compatible period and Frobenius morphisms for the chosen pullbacks.

D191.statement: For a nice tower over a number field and a continuous representation occurring as a piece, assume crystallinity at places above l with a surjective cover, occurrence of the prescribed Hodge jumps at good places above l, and the Frobenius assertion for every congruence datum with identified roots above l. These imply the seventeen-field Steps package, including representation existence, the ES and cut steps, their specified twist and descent consequences, cardinality and jump assertions, and the character, semisimplicity and continuity clauses on the left subrepresentation.

D192.statement: If q is nonzero and invertible in a henselian local ring A with separably closed residue field, then for each integer twist i the étale cohomology of Spec A[t,t\ensuremath{{}^{-}}\ensuremath{{}^{1}}] with Z/q(i) coefficients vanishes in degrees n \ensuremath{\ge} 2, and its degree-one group is additively isomorphic to Z/q.

D193.statement: The normalization furnishes the flat model and universal isogeny of type Tj with the specified local rings and identifications.

D194.statement: For a prime l, a local resolution and a good smooth model, the cohomology systems in adjacent degrees j and j+1 admit compatible restriction, multiplication and connecting maps. Level n is killed by l\textasciicircum{}n. The composites of multiplication and restriction give the prescribed powers of l, and at c=a+b each kernel of restriction or connecting map is reached by the preceding map.

D195.statement:
For a finite extension K of 
olinkurl{Q_l} inside its fixed algebraic closure, the period ring admits a system of good divided-power levels whose transition maps respect the integral and rational structure maps, divided powers and Galois actions, and whose rational inverse limit recovers the period ring. At every level the image of the distinguished element 
olinkurl{xi_0} lies in the divided-power ideal. If a in 
olinkurl{O_K} and w in 
olinkurl{A_inf} have the same image under the inclusion of 
olinkurl{O_K} and Fontaine's theta map, their images at that level agree modulo its divided-power ideal.

D196.statement: For each prime \ensuremath{\ell} the basic period-ring record exists, with the maps and coefficients appearing in the exact definition.

D197.statement: Let p be prime and y a nonzero element of the algebraic closure of \nolinkurl{Q_p.} If two crystalline period-ring elements a,b with b nonzero satisfy iota(a) = y iota(b) in the de Rham period ring, then the norm of y equals the norm of p raised to an integer power.

D198.statement: The given level, field and element fixed by the specified decomposition action admit a factorization with the designated pinning.

D199.statement: Let q be positive and invertible in a field K with separable closure Omega. For a discrete rank-one Z/q representation M with a chosen basis vector on which every automorphism taking a chosen primitive q-th root to its a-th power acts by a\textasciicircum{}i, the degree-n, twist-i cohomology of Spec K with Z/q coefficients is additively isomorphic to degree-n profinite Galois cohomology of M for every natural n and i.

D200.statement: For every commutative ring A in which q \ensuremath{\ne} 0 is invertible and every integer twist i, pullback along Spec A[t] \ensuremath{\to} Spec A induces a bijection on étale cohomology with coefficients Z/q(i) in every degree.

D201.statement: There is a Kummer boundary on the indicated cohomology groups, normalized up to a fixed unit of Z/q, taking the Picard class of each line bundle to that unit times its first Chern class.

D202.statement: For each nice Hodge tower and specified character there is a finite-dimensional continuous semisimple Galois representation occurring as its designated piece.

D203.statement: For the specified p-adic field K, every element of the de Rham period ring fixed by all automorphisms of the p-adic algebraic closure over K is the image of an element of K.

D204.statement: Let q be nonzero and k=i+j. Suppose I and J are nonnegative complexes resolving the i-th and j-th Tate twists of Z/q, with specified degree-zero sections representing their generators at each primitive q-th root, and that every term of J is flat as an étale sheaf. If a pairing from I and J to T gives the tensor product locally (every section lifts locally and its kernel vanishes locally), then T resolves the k-th twist and the products of the specified sections represent its generators.

D205.statement: For a prime l, an intermediate field K of the algebraic closure of \nolinkurl{Q_l}, a \nolinkurl{Q_l}-coefficient field L, a tower satisfying the stated regularity assumptions, and a character function theta, take any surjective cover over the integers of K compatible with theta. Pullback on total cohomology after extending scalars to L is injective and its image contains the theta piece. Before extending scalars, pullback intertwines every Galois action on the two total cohomology spaces.

D206.statement: For q dividing nonzero Q, coefficient reduction on every space preserves cup products. Under Inv(Q,E) it preserves the unit and first Chern classes of all line objects. Reduction from Q to itself is the identity, and reduction from Q through q to any divisor r of q equals direct reduction from Q to r.

D207.statement: For prime \ensuremath{\ell}, a smooth model M over the chosen \ensuremath{\ell}-adic intermediate field K, its residue data r, and every degree j, the level-one module of the Witt-cohomology system attached to M and r has finite length over W\ensuremath{\ell}(r.k).

D208.statement: For a prime l and the specified local-prime and A-inf data, a local period comparison supplies isomorphisms to the chosen crystalline and de Rham period rings. They respect the l-adic integers, Galois actions, Frobenius, the comparison inclusion and the Hodge filtration; they identify the designated period with the logarithmic period and agree with the given A-inf map.

D209.statement: Let R be a commutative coefficient ring and F an étale sheaf of R-modules whose evaluation on rings preserves filtered colimits. If A is the filtered colimit of rings \nolinkurl{A_j}, then in every integer degree each cohomology class of Spec A with coefficients in F is the restriction of a class on some Spec \nolinkurl{A_j.} A class at stage j that vanishes on Spec A vanishes after a transition to some later stage.

B02.statement:
Fix a CM field and coefficient data as above, odd rank $a$, admissible field
datum $d$ and $x\in E$ with $x^2=-d$. Fix the nonsplit exceptional set $T$,
separated places $w_0,v'\mid\ell$ agreeing on integral elements of
$\mathbb Q(x)$, and a finite set $S$. Let $U$ satisfy the automorphic
condition off $T$, the specified $\ell$-type at $w_0$, the spherical condition
off $w_0,S$, and the Satake-existence and lacunary-weight conditions at $v'$.
Then there exists a continuous semisimple $\rho$ of some dimension with
the source's Satake polynomial condition off a finite set of admissible
places away from $\ell$, and a Hodge-jump witness containing $a$ lacunary
integers. Call these common properties $V(\rho)$.
At each such admissible $w\nmid\ell$ with Satake data one can insist on
$V(\rho)$ and the polynomial condition at $w$ for every Satake multiset
there. At each $w\mid\ell$ agreeing with $v'$ on $\mathbb Q(x)$, separated
from $w_0,v'$ and having Satake data, the following two witnesses exist:
one has $V(\rho)$, crystalline comparison and the prescribed weight jumps
among its jumps at $w$; another has $V(\rho)$ and, for each Satake datum
and inducing bridge, crystalline comparison and a degree $-1$ Weil element
whose characteristic polynomial divides a power of the Satake polynomial.
The dimension and representation may vary with the demanded witness.

D210.statement: The prescribed weight of a finite morphism over a locally normal base satisfies the normalization condition.

D211.statement: For the stated algebraic extension of the function field in one variable over an algebraically closed field and q invertible, the project twists have vanishing cohomology in degrees \ensuremath{\ge}2.

D212.statement: Each smooth model over a finite local extension has the designated comparison of its geometric components.

D213.statement: For a smooth scheme over a field of characteristic zero and an affine open V, the degree-j cohomology of the filtration quotient from r to r+1 in the level-s complex on V vanishes whenever r<s and j differs from r.

D214.statement: For a divided-power base with graded splitting and torsion-freeness through s, and an open family covering X with a coordinate cover available, the degree-j cohomology of each admissible filtered interval [r,r\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}] after base change is additively the product of the tensor products of the splitting pieces with the correspondingly shifted cohomology modules. The isomorphism on elementary tensors is the given cohomology action.

D215.statement: Permuting the arguments changes the filtered alternating form by the sign of the permutation, with the same class in the designated graded piece.

D216.statement: Assume that the Rees restriction on small charts has kernel and cokernel killed by a uniform power of X through any fixed degree. For fixed atlas dimension d and degree j there is an exponent N working through degree j on every atlas of dimension d, for every positive level n and slow weight function \ensuremath{\rho} with k false or \ensuremath{\rho} identically zero.

D217.statement: In a tower of commutative algebras R, S, T, suppose S over R and T over S are each unions of nonempty directed systems of subalgebras isomorphic to prime localizations of étale algebras over their respective bases. Then T also has such a directed presentation over R.

D218.statement: The specified Kummer maps and the filtration satisfy the required compatibility on the given period complexes.

D219.statement: For a commutative ring B, an ideal J with divided powers and a divided-power polynomial algebra Q over B, the extended ideal in Q admits divided powers. They are compatible with those on J under the structure map from B, and the n-th divided power of the first polynomial generator is the specified generator of degree n for every n.

D220.statement: The trace construction satisfies the stated finite-level Lefschetz condition.

D221.statement: Consider a morphism between divided-power systems over R and an R-algebra R', compatible d-dimensional frames, and injective coefficient maps. Take a finite family of flat R-modules, maps from them to R', and compatible source and target filtration ladders at r. If the induced maps identify the target frame module with the product of the corresponding tensor products at every level from r\ensuremath{-}d through r, the cohomology pullbacks induce the same additive tensor-product identification at level r in every degree.

D222.statement: For modules on the specified thickening category, vanishing on all nonempty intersections of a finite family of opens in degrees below s, in all degrees, or in degrees above s gives global vanishing respectively below s, in all degrees, or from degree s plus the family size onwards. For any family, membership of the Čech cohomology terms of total degree n in a Serre class implies membership of the global group in degree n. For finite families and compatible natural semilinear maps with flat coefficient factors, the specified tensor comparison on every nonempty intersection in all degrees gives that comparison globally in all degrees.

D223.statement: Every local ring R admits a flat henselian local R-algebra S with \nolinkurl{m_R} S = \nolinkurl{m_S} and unchanged residue field. S is the union of a nonempty directed family of R-subalgebras, each isomorphic to a localization at a prime of an étale R-algebra.

D224.statement: The designated divided-power thickening satisfies the flatness condition used by the comparison construction.

D225.statement: For the divided-power thickening category and an allowed object class Q0, take Q\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} between the objects over a family of opens and those over its union. Suppose maps from Q\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} to Q0 stay in Q\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}. In every degree j restriction along the inclusion of objects over the opens into Q\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} is bijective on the ordinary cohomology and on the indicated filtration quotients, both for integral indices and for the optional indices and scalar parameters.

D226.statement: For every ring map R \ensuremath{\to} S, space E and sheaf F of S-modules, restricting scalars from S to R induces a bijection on the degree-n cohomology of F on E for every integer n.

D227.statement:
The Alexander–Whitney diagonal and its transposed diagonal admit an integral chain homotopy. In simplex degree N it is represented by a finite integral sum 
olinkurl{h_N} of pairs of total degree N+1. Its degree-zero boundary is the difference of the two diagonals, and in degree N+1 the boundary of 
olinkurl{h_}(N+1) plus the precomposition boundary of 
olinkurl{h_N} is their difference.

D228.statement: For any homomorphism of commutative rings R\ensuremath{\to}S, injective sheaf I of S-modules, presheaf P and positive integer degree n, the degree-n R-cohomology of the discrete object associated to P with coefficients in the restriction of I to R vanishes.

D229.statement: For every module sheaf F on the specified étale site and ring A there are additive maps from the degree-one cocycles of each A-algebra B to H\ensuremath{{}^{1}}(Spec A,F). If B is faithfully flat and étale, a cocycle maps to zero exactly when it is the right pullback minus the left pullback of one section over B. The image equals the kernel of pullback to B, and the class is unchanged on refinement along an A-algebra map between such covers.

D230.statement: For an element of the chosen crystalline period ring fixed by Gal(Q̄\ensuremath{\ell}/K) (with \ensuremath{\ell} the local prime), its image in the de Rham period ring is the image of an element of the maximal unramified subfield of K.

D231.statement: Fix a filtered divided-power system, a d-dimensional frame with sections at every object, and assume frame evaluations agree modulo the next filtration step. Impose the polynomial coefficient criterion through r+1. Degree-j cohomology of the rth graded piece vanishes for r<j. For r=j+q every class is represented by the frame j-forms with coefficients in filtration q, and such a sum represents zero only if all coefficients lie in filtration q+1.

D232.statement:
Let G from C\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} to C be a functor, R to R\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} a homomorphism, and 
olinkurl{N_i} a finite family of flat R-modules. Suppose coefficient diagrams 
olinkurl{F_i} on C and F\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} on C\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} carry natural pairings with 
olinkurl{N_i} that are additive and linear over the coefficient homomorphism in each variable. Choose finite covers by cosieves on both categories, with G preserving membership in corresponding cosieves. If the comparison from the finite family of tensor products of 
olinkurl{N_i} with the cohomology of 
olinkurl{F_i} to the cohomology of F\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} is an isomorphism in all degrees on every nonempty finite intersection, the global comparison is an isomorphism in all degrees.

D233.statement: For an onto chart functor and a Zariski cover, the specified restriction relation holds in every degree.

D234.statement: Over a discrete valuation ring in which each nonzero element divides a power of \ensuremath{\ell}, with the stated divided-power lattice and torsion-freeness assumptions, cohomology in each degree of each allowed filtered interval [r,r\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}] of a proper scheme with covering charts is finitely generated up to \ensuremath{\ell}: some power of \ensuremath{\ell} carries every class into one fixed finitely generated submodule.

D235.statement: Let q be a positive integer invertible in a commutative ring A. If every unit of A is a qth power and the Picard group of A has trivial q-torsion, the first étale cohomology of Spec A with coefficients in the first Tate twist modulo q vanishes.

D236.statement: For a filtered divided-power functor with a polynomial datum and a d-frame, assume chosen maps from the frame object to every object, constancy of the graded frame, and the criticality condition through level r+1. Degree-j cohomology of the r-th graded piece vanishes for j>r. If r=j+q with q natural, every class is represented by a sum of the indicated j-indexed frame forms with coefficients in filtration q, and any such sum representing zero has all coefficients in filtration q+1.

D237.statement: For nonzero q invertible on E, the degree-zero unit acts on the left as the identity on H\ensuremath{{}^{n}}(E,Z/q(i)) for every n and i. A primitive q-th root on a scheme defines classes in all twists whose cup product adds the twists and whose twist-zero class is the unit.

D238.statement: For nonzero q, the cup product on the cohomology of any given space with Z/q Tate twists is associative. For three classes of degrees n,m,k and twists i,j,l the two products agree after identifying the total degrees and twists by associativity of addition.

D239.statement: Let C and D be diagrams of cochain complexes of abelian groups on a category with a class of covering arrows stable under composition, and assume a common lower bound for all their terms. Suppose every covering arrow refines to an augmented cosimplicial diagram whose augmented complexes resolve each term of C and D. If a natural map C to D is locally surjective and locally injective on cohomology, it is bijective on cohomology at every object in every degree.

D240.statement: For a surjective integral morphism Y \ensuremath{\to} X and q invertible in the global sections of X, its Čech nerve augmentation induces a bijection on étale cohomology for every degree and every twist Z/q(i).

D241.statement: For a proper scheme over a Noetherian ring O, let a finite open cover have affine finite intersections. If a cosimplicial O-module carries the specified vector-bundle gluing data over this cover, every cohomology module of its cochain complex is finitely generated over O.

D242.statement: For a morphism of double complexes over a commutative ring, suppose s annihilates the kernel and cokernel of the degree-q cohomology map on column p whenever p+q \ensuremath{\le} n+1. Then s\textasciicircum{}(2n+3) annihilates the kernel and cokernel of the map on degree-n total cohomology.

D243.statement: If a functor M from commutative rings to R-modules preserves small filtered colimits, the étale sheaf obtained from U ↦ M(Γ(U)) is finitary: its induced functor on rings also preserves small filtered colimits.

D244.statement: For nonzero invertible q the five component statements hold in their stated settings: higher twisted cohomology vanishes on finite-type affine Dedekind schemes over algebraically closed fields; generic-fibre restriction is bijective for étale algebras over the polynomial ring of an absolutely integrally closed local domain; polynomial extension preserves twisted cohomology; Laurent extension of a strictly henselian ring has degree-one group Z/q and vanishing in degrees at least two; powers of the tautological first Chern class give the projective-bundle decomposition for a rank-N bundle.

D245.statement: Let epsilon in the tilt have untilt 1 and suppose the untilt of its inverse Frobenius is different from 1. If y in the positive crystalline period ring has zero de Rham theta image after every nonnegative Frobenius iterate, then the Frobenius of y is a multiple of the image of the crystalline period t(epsilon) in that ring.

D246.statement: For every ring A there is an assignment from tensor-square units of each A-algebra B to Pic(A). On faithfully flat B it is multiplicative on descent cocycles, a cocycle has trivial class exactly when it is the coboundary of a unit of B, and every Picard class becoming trivial over B is represented. The descended module is invertible with the assigned class, and a further faithfully flat A-algebra receiving B gives the same class for the induced cocycle.

D247.statement: On the nonlogarithmic thickening category, take the allowed object condition Q (TF for p=0, or all objects or flat objects for nonzero p). If the restricted subcategory for one family of opens lies in that for another and every open in the latter lies in the union of the former, the inclusion induces bijections in each cohomological degree for every pair of integer filtration levels, for every pair of standard levels with their scalars, and on the underlying cohomology.

D248.statement: For a local ring R and a prescribed separable closure Ω of its residue field, there exists a flat strictly henselian local R-algebra S with \nolinkurl{m_R} S = \nolinkurl{m_S} and residue field isomorphic to Ω over k(R). It is the union of a nonempty directed family of localizations at primes of étale R-algebras, identified with R-subalgebras of S.

D249.statement: The geometric generic fibres satisfy the indicated component and base-change requirements.

D250.statement: For a scheme over a characteristic-zero field, fix the stipulated cover whose local dimensions are all less than s, and any family of opens with union X. Restriction to the resulting K-complex is bijective on degree-j cohomology. For each r at most s, a de Rham cohomology class belongs to filtration r exactly when its image in the corresponding quotient complex vanishes.

D251.statement: Let R be an O-algebra, I a divided-power ideal whose s-th divided-power filtration term vanishes, with every filtration quotient free of l-torsion and every positive integer dividing a power of l in R. For X over Spec O with a d-coordinate chart on an open V and the structural map O to R/I, there is a divided-power thickening chart on V with ring isomorphic to R tensor over O with the sections on V. The isomorphism identifies the structural copy of R and the coordinate lifts, and evaluation of every section is its reduction modulo the thickening ideal. The new filtration still vanishes at s and its quotients have no l-torsion.

D252.statement: For every commutative ring A, the first étale cohomology group of Spec A with coefficients in the multiplicative group is isomorphic as an abelian group to the Picard group of A.

D253.statement: The adic trace and correspondence operations satisfy reduction, the specified trace identity Hl, base change, composition, degree, equality for correspondences, the graph identity and the splitting formula, as expressed by the ten constituent statements of Adic.

D254.statement: The prescribed projective line bundle admits the indicated degree-one identification and compatibility data.

D255.statement: The designated good base-change statement holds for the selected place and smooth model.

D256.statement: Let t be a non-zero-divisor in the Jacobson radical of a commutative ring. Suppose f and g are comparable for divisibility whenever their ideal contains a power of t, and every monic positive-degree polynomial modulo t\ensuremath{{}^{2}} has a root. For every monic polynomial Q of positive degree d and natural n with t\textasciicircum{}n dividing Q(0), there is z with t\textasciicircum{}(n+1) dividing Q(z) and t\textasciicircum{}n dividing z\textasciicircum{}d.

D257.statement: If evaluation O[x\ensuremath{{}_{1}},…,\nolinkurl{x_d}] \ensuremath{\to} R at coordinates T is étale, then for every ideal I of Λ and map O \ensuremath{\to} Λ/I there is a Λ-algebra D with d coordinates, étale over Λ[x\ensuremath{{}_{1}},…,\nolinkurl{x_d}], and a compatible map R \ensuremath{\to} D/ID carrying T to those coordinates modulo I. This reduction has the universal property for compatible maps from R and Λ to rings annihilating I.

D258.statement: The filtration and cup product satisfy the indicated multiplicative compatibility.

D259.statement: Assume the formal étale hypotheses A9, B2 and B3. If K is a purely inseparable extension of a field k and q is nonzero and invertible in k, then pullback from a k-scheme to its base change to K induces a bijection in every cohomological degree, for every Tate twist of Z/q.

D260.statement: The chosen first Chern class for an étale line bundle agrees with the normalized Kummer class of its transition data.

D261.statement: For q positive there is an injection of étale sheaves from the first Tate twist of Z/q, viewed as an abelian sheaf, into the multiplicative group. It sends the generator attached to each primitive q-th root to the corresponding unit and its image is killed by the q-th power map. On a scheme where q is invertible its image on sections equals the q-torsion units, and every unit is a q-th power étale locally.

D262.statement: Assume the stated étale chapter results A1–A5, A7–A11, B1–B5, B7, C1–C5, D1 and D2. For any group, coefficient ring, scheme X and homological degree m, every m-cycle for the trivial representation has a chain-level slant cocycle on X. For any coefficient sheaf and degree n, slanting from degree m+n on the product of the group classifying space with X to degree n on X is precomposition with this cocycle for every representative.

D263.statement: If Q > 0 and q divides Q, extending scalars from Z/Q to Z/q preserves acyclicity of a bounded-below complex of coefficient sheaves whose individual terms are flat.

D264.statement: Assume smooth proper cohomological base change between algebraically closed fields with l invertible, realization of the tower correspondence operators, and preservation of niceness by base change. For a nice tower over a characteristic-zero field and compatible maps of base and closure fields, every matrix realization of its specified character yields a realization on the base-changed tower with the same dimension, coefficient field and character. Its matrices agree with the original matrices on every pair of automorphisms commuting with the closure-field map.

D265.statement: For \ensuremath{\ell}-almost-finitely-generated modules M and M\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} over a divided-power lattice base, a single exponent k kills all \ensuremath{\ell}-power torsion in M\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} and all infinitely \ensuremath{\ell}-divisible elements of M. Every sequence in M with n-th successive difference divisible by \ensuremath{\ell}\ensuremath{{}^{n}} admits z congruent to \ensuremath{\ell}\ensuremath{{}^{k}} times its n-th term modulo \ensuremath{\ell}\ensuremath{{}^{n}}, for every n.

D266.statement: Assume the stated étale-cohomological inputs for Künneth and Lefschetz, duality for integral smooth projective varieties over algebraically closed fields of characteristic different from l, cohomological additivity for finite disjoint unions, the component decompositions for good and smooth models, and the geometric generic-component hypothesis. For each prime l and finite extension K of \nolinkurl{Q_l} in the chosen closure, cup products exist for every model. On every good smooth model the rational l-adic groups are finite-dimensional, the connected models have the prescribed duality in their dimension, and finitely many connected good smooth models over it jointly detect zero cohomology classes in every degree.

D267.statement: For vector bundles V and W over E, the projective bundle of V⊕W has a subobject over E mapping to the projective bundle of V with the same tautological line. Every simplex of the direct-sum bundle satisfying the first-chart condition lifts to that subobject.

D268.statement: For two morphisms of indexed coefficient systems over a ring homomorphism, a natural transformation between their indexing functors that intertwines the two maps on every coefficient section implies equality of their pullbacks on cohomology in every degree.

D269.statement: For nonzero q and any integral twist i, sections of the twist are étale-locally zero or multiples of a primitive-root generator. With a chosen primitive root, its restrictions generate locally, and on a nonempty scheme a multiple that vanishes has coefficient divisible by q. Generators commute with restriction and raising the root to a unit power a scales its generator by a\textasciicircum{}i modulo q. Every rule into a Z/q-module sheaf satisfying these restriction and power laws extends uniquely to a sheaf morphism from the twist.

D270.statement: On a smooth scheme of fixed relative dimension over a characteristic-zero field, tautological line data admit a class in degree-two de Rham cohomology. For every family of nilpotent divided-power thickenings admitting local sections, its restriction is represented by the degree-two cocycle obtained by applying the divided-power logarithm to the multiplicative defect of lifted transitions.

D271.statement: Let q be a nonzero integer invertible on X. If a global unit w has zero Kummer class, there is a global unit v on X with v raised to q equal to w.

D272.statement: The specified bounded truncations of the cohomological construction on the proper scheme have finite cohomology modules over O.

D273.statement: The constructed twist Kummer map satisfies the exact Kummer condition.

D274.statement: Let a cofiltered diagram of simplicial presheaves have a cone, with coefficients in an étale sheaf of modules over a commutative ring. If cohomology is continuous on the induced cone of discrete presheaves in each simplicial degree, it is continuous on the original cone in every cohomological degree. Each class at the vertex descends to a stage and every stage class that vanishes at the vertex vanishes after a further transition.

D275.statement: For any positive modulus q and integer twist i, the canonical resolution with its marked generators is a twist resolution with flat terms. Every other marked twist resolution maps to it preserving the degree-zero generators, and two such chain maps agreeing on all marked generators are chain homotopic.

D276.statement:
For a tilted integral element epsilon with untilt equal to 1 and with the untilt of its inverse-Frobenius image different from 1, the crystalline period t in 
olinkurl{A_cris} is the image of mu(epsilon) from 
olinkurl{A_inf} multiplied by a unit of 
olinkurl{A_cris.}

D277.statement: If A is noetherian and O is a local A-algebra for which the structural map is ind-étale in the stated sense, then O is noetherian.

D278.statement: For two complexes C,J of étale module sheaves, suppose C is locally acyclic and every term of J admits the stated local flat presentation. A sectionwise tensor in degree (s,t) killed by the differential on C is, after étale restriction, the image of a tensor in degree (s\ensuremath{-}1,t).

D279.statement: Assume the local graded comparison, polynomial torsion condition, global Serre theorem and global vanishing condition for the specified thickenings. Let O be Noetherian with the zero divided-power ideal satisfying the base filtration and divisibility conditions at l and s. For a proper scheme over O with the given cover, every p-th Čech cohomology module of the r-th graded piece of the thickening filtration, on the allowed thickenings of the cover, is finitely generated over O whenever r<s and p is nonnegative.

D280.statement: For a smooth surjection the Čech augmentation induces the specified bijection on cohomology for every coefficient sheaf.

D281.statement: At an invertible coefficient modulus the trace along the given finite morphism acts on twist sections by the specified weighted sum on every test square.

D282.statement: For a divided-power thickening system on a scheme, compare the level-s truncated subcategory on a chosen set of opens with an encompassing subcategory. Suppose the latter is either unrestricted with l=1, or truncated at a higher level s' with the same l. For any integers r,r' with r'\ensuremath{\le}s, pullback along the inclusion is bijective on degree-j cohomology of the filtration subquotient for all j.

D283.statement: For every natural q and integer i, the functor from commutative rings to modules over the lifted ring Z/q, generated by primitive q-th roots modulo the twist-i relations, preserves filtered colimits of universe size (0,0).

D284.statement: The generic comparison gives a good restriction record for each probe, nonzero modulus and integral twist.

D285.statement: Let T be an absolutely integrally closed local domain with fraction field K, and q nonzero and invertible on T. For every strictly henselian algebra A ind-étale over T[t], H\ensuremath{{}^{n}}(Spec(K \ensuremath{\otimes}\nolinkurl{_T} A),Z/q(i)) vanishes for every n \ensuremath{\ge} 2 and every integer twist i.

D286.statement: For the fixed prime l the crystalline comparison maps at every finite level commute with reduction, the Galois action fixing the base, Frobenius, pullback and the transition between the two presentations. They preserve cup products and units; reduction preserves filtration, and multiplication by a scalar in the indicated divided-power ideal raises filtration by one.

D287.statement: The class represented by a cocycle has the prescribed edge image in the étale resolution of the probe, uniquely among the designated representatives.

D288.statement: For rings A and B, every q, every degree n and twist i, restriction along the two ring projections identifies the étale cohomology of Spec(A\ensuremath{\times}B) with coefficients Z/q(i) bijectively with the product of the corresponding groups for A and B.

D289.statement: For a divided-power polynomial system with a frame of dimension d+1, take filtration ideals b contained in a and satisfying the polynomial filtration criteria at r and r\ensuremath{-}1 for both families. The canonical inclusion on the cut frame has a natural quotient map from the level-r subquotient to the level-(r\ensuremath{-}1) subquotient making the sequence objectwise short exact. On divided-power polynomials the map sends the coefficients (\nolinkurl{c_k}) to (\nolinkurl{c_}\{k+1\}).

D290.statement: Let f:K \ensuremath{\to} L be a map of complexes of sheaves over a commutative ring, both zero outside degrees \ensuremath{-}P through 0. For a coefficient sheaf F and integer n, if each piece of f induces a surjection in degree n\ensuremath{-}1 and an injection in degree n on the indicated contravariant cohomology with coefficients F, then f induces a surjection in degree n\ensuremath{-}1 and an injection in degree n there as well.

D291.statement: For a functor \ensuremath{\pi} from the indexing category to I and a morphism m of R-linear coefficient systems, suppose the relative maps over all objects of I have kernel and cokernel annihilated by s in every degree at most n+1. Then the kernel and cokernel of the total degree-n map are annihilated by s\textasciicircum{}(2n+3).

D292.statement: Every good smooth model admits a finite atlas for its functor of points with some uniform dimension bound d. The charts cover after localization at finitely many elements generating the unit ideal, lift membership across surjections with kernel in the Jacobson radical, and have small nonempty intersections of dimension at most d in the specified sense.

D293.statement: Let I, I\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}, J, T and T\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} be complexes of étale sheaves of modules over a commutative ring. Suppose given tensor pairings from I and J to T and from I\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} and J to T\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}, and maps f from I to I\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} and u from T to T\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} intertwining the two pairings with the identity on J. The mapping cone of u then admits a tensor pairing from the mapping cone of f and J.

D294.statement: If the weighted sum of finite correspondences vanishes on the indicated geometric fibres, the weighted sum of their cohomological actions vanishes in every stipulated degree and weight.

D295.statement: If two monomorphisms U\ensuremath{\to}E and V\ensuremath{\to}E of étale spaces jointly surject after taking free R-module sheaves in each simplicial degree, their chains form a short exact sequence. It runs from the chains of U\ensuremath{\times}\nolinkurl{_E} V by the difference of the two projections, through the direct sum of the chains of U and V, to the chains of E by the sum of the inclusions.

D296.statement: If a pairing of complexes I,J into K satisfies IsTensor, then every pairing of I',J' into K' and maps I \ensuremath{\to} I', J \ensuremath{\to} J' induce a unique compatible map K \ensuremath{\to} K'. If both inputs are strictly concentrated in nonnegative degrees so is K. Every map K \ensuremath{\to} K' induces a pairing of I,J into K' compatible with the identity on both inputs.

D297.statement: For every nonzero q, classes a and b of cohomological degrees n and m and twists i and j satisfy a ∪ b = (\ensuremath{-}1)\textasciicircum{}(nm) b ∪ a, after the canonical identifications of degrees and twists.

D298.statement: For q nonzero and any integral twist i, a section is étale locally zero or a multiple of a twisted generator attached to a primitive qth root. Given a primitive root locally, its generator suffices and has exact order q on any nonempty scheme. Generators commute with restriction, and replacing a root by its ath power scales the generator by a\textasciicircum{}i for a unit a modulo q. These rules characterize maps out of the twist sheaf uniquely.

D299.statement:
Let L and T have the stated column decompositions. Take finitely many shifts 
olinkurl{e_j} and nonnegatively supported target complexes 
olinkurl{I_j} and I. Suppose a degree-preserving additive comparison from the product of the shifted Hom cochains from L to 
olinkurl{I_j} to the Hom cochains from T to I commutes with coboundaries and preserves the filtration by vanishing on columns. If its column restrictions agree on cocycles with isomorphisms in every degree for all columns p at most zero, any induced comparison on total cohomology is bijective in every degree.

D300.statement: Let E\ensuremath{\to}E' be a map over S, with both spaces quasi-compact and quasi-separated over S, and use a finitary sheaf of R-modules. If pullback induces cohomology isomorphisms on every indicated strictly henselian stalk, then over every étale U\ensuremath{\to}S and in every degree, a class on E lifts from E' after a surjective étale cover of U, and any class on E' killed on E vanishes after such a cover.

D301.statement: The map associated with the chosen place descends to its valuation ring, agrees with the designated field embedding and preserves irreducibility of uniformizers.

D302.statement: For each degree r of a period algebra at a prime l, every element of Fil0(r) is congruent modulo Fil0(r+1) to a coefficient from W times dxi0(r). Such a multiple is in Fil0(r+1) exactly when its coefficient lies in the ideal generated by xi. For each element z of Fil0(r) some l-power times z equals the image in Acr0 of xi\textasciicircum{}r times an element of W.

D303.statement: For a parameter algebra A at the prime \ensuremath{\ell}, the expansion of finitely supported coefficients (\nolinkurl{c_k}) is zero if and only if every coefficient belongs to the principal ideal (\ensuremath{\pi}\textasciicircum{}\ensuremath{\ell}) in A.

D304.statement: For a nonzero q and an injective étale sheaf M of Z/q-modules, sections over every scheme form a flat Z/q-module. There is also a presheaf mapping to M which is locally surjective on sections, has locally vanishing kernel, and is sectionwise flat on nonempty schemes.

D305.statement: For nonzero q invertible on a scheme, primitive q-th roots and q-th roots of any unit exist étale locally. Given a primitive root, every q-th root of unity is locally a power of it, and every other primitive root is locally a power with exponent a unit modulo q.

D306.statement: The geometric steps, all Kodaira–Spencer comparisons and the common plan give the odd-rank Galois representations with their Hodge jumps and Frobenius constraints at the marked places.

D307.statement: A finite flat subgroup of a relatively polarized abelian scheme over an affine base has a quotient abelian scheme with a relatively ample line and a finite flat surjective homomorphism having exactly the specified kernel on all test rings.

D308.statement: Resolution, principalisation and Poincaré–Lelong invariance give existence of one full arithmetic intersection system for the specified charts.

D309.statement: The Fargues exactness input gives the specified annihilator bound on the Hodge–Tate cokernel and identifies the Hodge–Tate kernel by orthogonality to the kernel of the dual logarithmic differential.

T14.statement:
Assume the eight statements T17--T24. There is a real $C\ge0$ uniform in
the following data. Let a core $T$ on $D$ satisfy the core laws and
$m^2\le k$. Take $1\le j<m$, a deep datum $Y$ of index $j$, an integer
$e\ge0$ and a real $o$ with $Y$ good at $(e,o)$. Suppose its integer
$M'$ has at most fifteen distinct prime factors. For each admissible
weight $u$ with gap $g>0$, there are real numbers $s_Z$, indexed by
components, such that
\[
  s_Z\le\mathrm{compVolSlope}_{Y,\xi_R,8,\mathrm{mixVals}(B),Z}(u),
  \qquad
  \frac{\sum_Z^{\mathrm{fin}}s_Z}{\#\mathrm{Comp}}
   \ge -C\,\mathrm{errX}(\ell(D),u,g),\qquad B=\mathrm{bndB}(u,g).
\]
Here the weight decreases strictly at each embedding, and differences
from each index on the $q$-side to any other index there or on the
$p$-side have absolute value at least $g$.

D310.statement: Resolution and principalisation in characteristic zero give an embedded resolution over the given projective model, with a closed immersion into its product with a projective space and the required local coordinates over the distinguished open.

D311.statement: A homomorphism between two semiabelian schemes over a dense open of a normal noetherian base extends uniquely over the base.

D312.statement: The common geometric data, positive family and comparison inputs give existence of a good tower and the uniform tower volume statement.

T26.statement:
Assume an arithmetic intersection system, the three Hilbert--Samuel
consequences T18, the bigness bound T17, the resolution statement
\nolinkurl{ResKStatement}, extension of homomorphisms of semiabelian
schemes, the Fargues Hodge--Tate input, GAGA for sections, quotients by
finite flat subgroups, the Zarhin splitting T22 and nef Riemann--Roch T23.
Then the uniform component-slope estimate in T14 holds with the same
restrictions on $D,T,j,Y,e,o$ and the number of prime factors.

D313.statement: Given the common geometric, flag, flat-degree, automorphism and comparison structures, one constant controls every allowed good tower in the volume formula.

D314.statement: A positive family supplies the flag Chern comparison on the Frobenius-labelled Hodge lattices at all indicated places over p.

D315.statement: The prescribed Hodge–Tate and ordinary-curve data give the positive family needed for the arithmetic flag model.

D316.statement: Reduced Part I, the two numerical inputs, compatible toroidal levels and the remaining displayed hypotheses give a good root tower and one uniform volume estimate.

D317.statement: On a good root tower with positive ranks the full intersection system satisfies the I8 identity for the flag-height intersection expression.

D318.statement: For good CM data satisfying the prime-count bound and common period norm, one constant bounds the mean height in terms of log root discriminant and the absolute L-value parameter.

D319.statement: The flag-cover realization supplies a square system in each specified adjacent-root position separated from the chosen index.

D320.statement: Given the Part I and level/Hecke compatibility inputs, the key formula, homomorphism extension, numerical Segre identity, embedded resolution, Fargues–Hodge–Tate, GAGA, the large-degree line theorem, projective-bundle inputs, and the stated height and analytic inputs, one obtains the full conjunction Top.Given, including the additional semiabelian, slope-bound and antisymmetric-perturbation assertions.

D321.statement: For every Hermitian rank-i lattice over a number field, i\ensuremath{\ge}1 and \ensuremath{\varepsilon}>0, a finite number field extension admits a nonzero vector of line degree at least slope \ensuremath{-} (log i)/2 \ensuremath{-} \ensuremath{\varepsilon}.

D322.statement: For a good origin on the global root tower and a full intersection system, positive ranks give the I5 and I6 tower intersection identities.

D323.statement: The stated inputs give the second tower estimate and the mean-slope bound with common coefficient 2C+3C\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}+5, together with the listed companion identities.

D324.statement: The intersection, volume, resolution, group-extension, Hodge–Tate, GAGA and large-degree-line inputs supply the full simultaneous geometric input record.

D325.statement: There are two common real height constants for the nine geometric estimates under the given geometric, Weil and flat-degree hypotheses.

D326.statement: The global split-component model admits a good root tower with a good origin, the prescribed regularity and the terminal ramification conditions.

D327.statement: For each listed index of a good tower the strict base-degree setting holds with the two height constants, root discriminant and L-value parameters.

D328.statement: The cusp weight has two compatible regularizations with a common torus-invariant function and the prescribed conjugation law.

D329.statement: At each specified level-two root, its flat records satisfy the near-height bounds with the tower's bad primes, root discriminant and L-value.

D330.statement: A dominant weight meeting the numerical threshold gives nefness at the indicated prime with zero additional shift on the compactified Hodge model.

D331.statement: Integrating the cusp weight on the chosen fundamental set yields the stated bound involving its volume, the root discriminant and the CM-type and rank parameters.

D332.statement: The mixed intersection number for the projected flag ideal is zero below N\ensuremath{-}1 and otherwise equals the indicated sum of mixed intersection numbers over tuples of total weight n\ensuremath{-}(N\ensuremath{-}1).

D333.statement: For either of the two specified CM-sign choices, a base uniformization exists in dimension the number of CM types times the two ranks, and satisfies the local chart condition.

D334.statement: For N\ensuremath{\ge}2, evaluating the universal flag-degree polynomial at the supplied weights yields their geometric flag degree.

D335.statement: From the generic characteristic-zero point and finite prime set choose a characteristic-zero coefficient field extension satisfying the simultaneous local conditions.

D336.statement: The stipulated polarized divisible-group and Tate-module data determine a Hodge–Tate point realizing the given comparison, framing and level.

D337.statement: The root line degrees on the model give the prescribed trivial flag modulo p raised to the specified ramification power minus two.

D338.statement: The pulled-back Lie metric along the period chart is bounded by the uniform multiple of the initial Hermitian metric at every tested tangent vector.

D339.statement: Local frames at the point on the given flag model yield the required norm identity on the common refinement.

D340.statement: The selected period Gram expression is bounded by the displayed exponential of the sum of boundary logarithms on the polydisc.

D341.statement: For the specified local unitary form and normalized isotropic pair, the special unitary group is the submonoid generated by the associated Eichler transformations.

D342.statement: Let a generic field-valued point specialize to every point of X, with finite coordinates tied to X over the integers. Suppose a finite family of lattices gives vector bundles of the indicated ranks with twist-generating forms and chosen bases of the generic subspaces. Let X' have generic flag coordinates tied to the enlarged generic field and specializing to all its points. If X'\ensuremath{\to}X induces the given extension on generic points and membership in every original coordinate chart is equivalent at corresponding specializations, this morphism is smooth.

D343.statement: At a characteristic-zero point satisfying the CptGen and NormalCpt conditions on a locally Noetherian scheme, let a semiabelian group have full n-torsion for n\ensuremath{\ge}1 and the stated generic Weil pairing for a line bundle. On a dominating point with the same two point conditions, take a commutative group pullback, its line bundle and generic Weil pairing, and Lie models with maps compatible on dual-number points and evaluation. Then its Hodge–Tate differential object and its differential lattice are the pullbacks of the corresponding original objects along the specified dual map.

D344.statement: For a characteristic-zero n-dimensional simple-normal-crossings model with coordinate ideal of arithmetic dimension n+1 and boundary invariant under blockwise nonzero complex scalings, there is a finite collection of analytic boundary charts. Every complex point in the coordinate locus is a blockwise torus multiple of a point in one of these charts with parameter norm at most 1/2.

D345.statement: Suppose the multihomogeneous coordinate data define an arithmetic variety of dimension n+1 with the indicated normal crossings model. Suppose its boundary locus is closed in the model’s complex points and stable under block rescaling and conjugation. There is an analytic log resolution with a potential and section having simple normal crossings, log norm at most zero, zero divisor supported precisely over that boundary, and the same boundary weight on conjugate lifted orbits.

D346.statement: Let a compact Hausdorff space carry a finite holomorphic atlas, a potential L and section s with simple normal crossings of the specified multiplicities, and log norm of s everywhere at most zero. Let Theta be a positive potential, let a local potential th and function u give the prescribed singular weight, and assume the negative of th+u is plurisubharmonic off the boundary of s. Then u has a smooth replacement u\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} equal to u off that boundary. Both signs of th+u\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} are plurisubharmonic globally, the singular-weight bound holds for some constant, and the constant family u\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} satisfies the regular-family bounds at scale exp(\ensuremath{-}exp(1)) and the required second-derivative regularity.

D347.statement: Assume resolution with coordinates in characteristic zero, algebraization of compatible holomorphic line-bundle sections on proper smooth complex schemes, and the stated Part I local-system results. For a positive-signature CM moduli datum at a level good at every prime, fix an admissible embedding and type. If a clopen irreducible set is identified at complex points with the specified period component, it admits a flat generating frame function together with logarithmic norms realizing that function and satisfying the adelic condition.

D348.statement: For the isotropic special unitary group with the given number-field and finite-adèle topology, the rational special unitary matrices are dense in the stated finite-adèlic group.

D349.statement: Let a characteristic-zero field point carry the integral coordinate-tie data, and let B be a set of its specializations of characteristic zero. Suppose every characteristic-zero specialization has a prime-local presentation of its regular ring by a rational subalgebra carrying an SNC patch of dimension parameter e for the prescribed point sets. Then an ideal in the indicated coordinate ring defines an SNC model with that parameter. For every complex point and every compatible coordinate tuple, the tuple lies in the ideal's complex point locus exactly when the center is a specialization belonging to B.

D350.statement: For the indicated period chart the Levi form has the displayed diagonal norm expression, and at an immersion the associated linear map is injective.

D351.statement: On a compact Hausdorff space with a finite holomorphic atlas of complex dimension e+1, let a section of a metrized line datum have a simple normal crossings divisor with multiplicities \nolinkurl{m_k} and holomorphic component inclusions. For any smooth test function and e admissible potentials, integration against the log norm equals the sum of the component integrals weighted by \nolinkurl{m_k} minus the ambient curvature integral.

D352.statement: For a universal CM family of signature (j,j\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}) on its integer lattice, there is a Hermitian form on E\textasciicircum{}(j+j\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}) and a compatible lattice embedding recovering the given orthogonality relation. A majorant realizes the ball as a quotient of the archimedean unitary group by its stabilizer with the prescribed length formula, and the lattice stabilizer identifies equivariantly with the form automorphisms. The ball action is holomorphic and changes the potential by a real part.

D353.statement: For any family of arithmetic intersection functions satisfying its axioms, the projection identity for relative dimension r implies the identity in relative dimension r+1. The asserted identity is intersection upstairs equals generic-fibre intersection degree times intersection on the image for the prescribed block map and Hermitian line bundles.

D354.statement: The designated plurisubharmonic functions on the punctured chart extend with the stated boundary conditions.

D355.statement: For a semiabelian family over a CM moduli compactification, fix a point of its exponential parameter domain. Suppose the exponential intertwines the specified endomorphism actions, the embedding labels specialize correctly, the chosen sections are a frame at the specialized point, and their Lie values equal the specified evaluated coordinates via the given family map. Those complex coordinate vectors are linearly independent and span the eigenspace belonging to the selected embedding.

D356.statement: For a CM field E, a finite index set of embeddings, a host, and a universal family with integral lattice Lambda and numerical data j, j\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}, n, g, there is a Hermitian form on E\textasciicircum{}(j+j\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}) and an injective \nolinkurl{O_E}-linear embedding of Lambda into it. The embedded lattice has bounded integral denominator and its orthogonality is equivalent to vanishing of the family form against all \nolinkurl{O_E} multiples. The family form is the rational trace of the Hermitian pairing in reverse order multiplied by an element whose chosen archimedean images are purely imaginary of one positive absolute size. A Z-basis of Lambda with 2g elements maps under the chosen embeddings to a real basis of the corresponding product of complex spaces.

D357.statement: There is a positive factor depending only on the three integer indices f,j,j'. For the given component and sheet decomposition of an integral model for an abelian Galois CM host, take a function constant on the relevant torus saturations whose restrictions to sheet charts agree with functions integrable against their ball densities. Its point integral with the Hodge measure equals this factor times the sum over pieces of the sheet degrees multiplied by the corresponding density-weighted integrals over the fundamental regions.

D358.statement: Assume the Fargues–Hodge–Tate proposition. At every p in the prescribed finite set where the compactification satisfies HTFree, a flag realizing the root lines of the chosen CM root model makes every dominant weight nef at p with zero offset: its degree is nonnegative on every curve of that model at p.

D359.statement: The indicated intersection degree is given by the specified integral formula on the chosen model.

D360.statement: Assume the Weil input. Let a normal projective model map generically to the specified integral moduli model, and let S be a finite set of primes containing every ramified prime of E, with exponents R(p) \ensuremath{\ge} 4, full p\textasciicircum{}R(p)-torsion and primitive roots of that order. Enlarging the projective coordinates while preserving the old ones produces a dominating Hodge compactification with the same R, the prescribed Hodge–Tate freeness at S, and a map locally isomorphic over every point of the former generic fibre.

D361.statement: For a CM period family with holomorphic eigenframes, suppose I lies in W and is isotropic, the boundary periods inject equivariantly and extend continuously from the logarithmic cover, and the positive semidefinite limiting Hermitian form has kernel contained in the period span of I. Assume the stated continuous form and orthogonal projection identities near zero. Any boundary squared norm nu satisfying the specified frame and period-lattice normalization is positive. As the exponential coordinate tends to zero, log determinant minus log of the prescribed normalization tends to log nu.

D362.statement:
Let a semiabelian commutative group over X be pulled back to the generic point of an 
olinkurl{O_L}-point of X, where L is a number field. Suppose its generic fibre has a split torus extension whose quotient is the generic fibre of a semiabelian model over 
olinkurl{O_L.} For compatible Lie models and a Z-basis of the torus cocharacters, the corresponding generic tangent vectors lift to linearly independent elements of the integral Lie module. There is an 
olinkurl{O_L}-linear map to the quotient model's Lie module inducing the given generic quotient on lifted vectors. Its kernel is the span of those lifted cocharacters and its cokernel is torsion.

D363.statement: A nef Riemann–Roch input, the common geometric data, intersection system, birational formula, good tower and volume theorem imply a uniform constant for the deep height estimate.

D364.statement: For a complex boundary chart of the stated CM moduli problem with p+q\ensuremath{\ge}1, there is a radius 0<rho\ensuremath{\le}1, an abelian group of logarithmic periods, and a family exponential on the radius-rho ball. At each point of the log cover the image of the period map is exactly the exponential period group at the scaled covering point. At every point of the punctured unit domain the prescribed form satisfies the Riemann condition after scaling by rho.

D365.statement: Given a universal CM family, its lattice embedding and a frame A0 adapted at the origin, there exist holomorphic maps Z and G on the ball domain, vector- and scalar-valued respectively. At every point t and for every frame A adapted there, Z(t) is the Möbius action at zero of the block family obtained by multiplying the specified inverse of A0 into A. The potential at Z(t) equals the potential at t plus the real part of G(t).

D366.statement: Suppose a characteristic-zero point specializes to every point of the scheme and its projective coordinates satisfy the given coordinate identification. For a smooth commutative group scheme and a model of its Lie algebra, the complex fibres admit positive-definite Hermitian inner products compatible with complex conjugation. Pairings of two model vectors vary continuously on the locus where both vectors and the marked coordinates specialize.

D367.statement: Let u from a split torus with character group X to G be a group morphism, Y a subgroup of X, and B a local ring with square-zero ideal I. If every torus point trivial on Y maps to the identity after arbitrary base change from B/I, then the same universal assertion holds over B.

D368.statement: Let X be locally Noetherian with a characteristic-zero field-valued generic point satisfying the component and normality assumptions. Let G be semiabelian, let L be a line bundle on G, and fix positive n, full n-torsion and a generic Weil pairing for these data. For any Lie model with tangent space E and any component point q, an open neighbourhood of q admits a choice of a functional in the dual of E for each n-torsion point, satisfying the Hodge–Tate condition at every component point in the neighbourhood. At q all functionals satisfying it for a fixed torsion point form a single coset of n times the lattice of invariant differentials.

D369.statement: For the abelian part of the specified Hodge compactification at a point over a number field L, there are an element rho of L with square \ensuremath{-}d and nonnegative integers p',q'. For every map from L to an algebraically closed field and every embedding of the CM integer ring into it, the corresponding multiplicity of the Lie action is p' when the distinguished root maps to the image of rho and q' otherwise.

D370.statement: The polarization induced on each marked abelian part over the given valuation point is principal.

D371.statement: For a projective model over an essentially finite-type Z-algebra, finitely many nonzero projective coordinate tuples, vector-bundle lattices and independent vectors in their generic subspaces admit a common dominating normal model. Each tuple lies in a chart at every compactification point, the pulled-back lattices acquire the indicated flags there with direct complements at every step, and the normalization condition holds at old points where the chart and quotient-frame conditions already held.

D372.statement: For semiabelian data t for a CM host over S and a point Spec L \ensuremath{\to} S over a number field, there exists a number field L' with an embedding L \ensuremath{\to} L' such that the base-changed point admits an abelian-part datum, comprising a torus extension and an identification of the quotient compatible with the group homomorphism, action and polarization line bundle.

D373.statement: In the specified characteristic-zero CM moduli and semiabelian family, assume the marked point is generic in the given sense, n is positive, all geometric n-torsion descends to that point, and the chosen stalk is Noetherian and integrally closed. The zero form satisfies the stated Hodge–Tate extension condition, the field contains a primitive nth root of unity when the signature dimension is positive, and the Hodge–Tate differential and lattice modules at that stalk coincide.

D374.statement: The stated intersection, Hilbert–Samuel, bigness, extension, resolution, GAGA, line-degree, quotient and Zarhin inputs produce both a good root tower and the uniform volume law.

D375.statement: Global reciprocity, the position condition on a slot, and the standard ties of its chosen kernel imply both eventual twisted-unitary rows and the point condition for that kernel on every linked family.

D376.statement: A carrier estimate, positive rows, finite dimensionality, uniqueness of the Bessel functional and the Siegel-Weil mass data yield the closed spectral hypotheses, including absolute convergence, choices, row sums, mass compatibility, linking and splitting.

D377.statement: Assume the mass, positivity and finite dimensionality inputs. For each selection of a family class with tied local spaces, rank bounds and the loop condition, the selected spectral estimate holds eventually for every family, with rank parameter three.

D378.statement: At constructed positions with good slot data and the given linkage, each of the six rows is eventually valid: reference and twisted chain evaluations, their two periods, compatibility, and the level-prime column valuations. The proof uses the same true-column restriction in the six applications.

D379.statement: Under the convergent unitary Siegel-Weil formula, one can choose counting constants as a function of the output list and a positive constant bounded by its c-component, with nonnegative C-component and exponent at least 2(CYL+1). The same choices give the counting estimate for every family and test predicate.

D380.statement: The actual compact Fourier estimate, the model at a built place and its compact bounds all hold.

D381.statement: With a genus-one lattice model, curve dictionary, inert integrality, entry admissibility and the required curves, any positioned slot with its standard kernel ties has the family-level twist and pointwise kernel properties.

D382.statement: Given inert entry admissibility and curve existence, every partial object admits compatible models whenever its lattice is tied and twice its geometric rank is at most the stage rank.

D383.statement: For compatible local models, congruent indices and the prescribed prime, row, stabilizer and frame data, the cut has its orbit sums, scalar types, coefficient products, partner and fibre counts, eligible representatives and a common unramified restricted theta choice.

D384.statement: Uniform carrier constants can be chosen so that every admissible tied pair, pinned character and sufficiently large scale satisfying the stated size and separation conditions has the required full archimedean carrier estimate.

T04.statement:
Assume global Artin reciprocity, the convergent unitary Siegel--Weil formula,
the discrete-series cover, Harish--Chandra modules, rapid decay, the
Casselman--Wallach statement, discrete-series classification, and both estimates
of T05. For any reciprocity system, norm-choice extension, series extension,
geometry and family predicate $N$, let $p$ be their extension parameters.
Suppose T08's open conditions and the linked covolume, functional and
$N$-norm conditions hold at $p$. Then all 26 large-slot row conditions hold
for its built and good slots and its bundle linkage. They give class counts,
the $j$-invariant, rank, the second complement, prime column valuations,
arithmetic at bundle points, reference and twisted points and periods, the
row tie, row bounds, twists, primitivity, lambda primes, divisors,
decomposition points, selection jumps, the $L^p$ and order conditions,
service, zero locus, the frame condition, irreducibility counts, definite
rows and the $N$-norm condition. Each row condition has its own existential
large-slot quantifier.

D385.statement: The stated good Weierstrass model for CM period pairs at primes at least five away from the squarefree discriminant implies admissibility of the inert theta entries for the specified small chain.

D386.statement: Assuming the real representation-theoretic inputs, surjectivity and the lambda lower bound, the nine pointwise row hypotheses yield the definite rows on the specified slot and linkage.

D387.statement: Given the convergent unitary Siegel-Weil formula, arbitrary base predicate, slots and linkage, each of the Lp, order and torsion-free rows holds after restriction by a large base condition.

D388.statement: If the chosen slot system has its prescribed rank component, every good built member eventually satisfies the arithmetic condition at its linked bundle points.

D389.statement: Given the unitary Siegel-Weil and finite-dimensional row hypotheses, there is one positive irreducibility constant for every size-controlled family class with eventually tied, compatibly labelled Hida settings. Eventually each member admits joint rows with injective label counts and the prescribed epsilon-scaled counting bound.

D390.statement: For every boundary condition, slot and linkage, the second-complement division constants are admissible at all constructed points in that row.

D391.statement: Assume global Artin reciprocity. If the linkage of every bundle implies reciprocity linkage of its boundary record, each selected family in the good slot satisfies the service condition.

D392.statement: Assume the convergent unitary Siegel-Weil formula. A slot whose linked rows carry a common Hida setting, operator, Hilbert-space identification and matching labels admits uniform counting and irreducibility constants.

D393.statement: For arbitrary base predicate, slots and linkage, the convergent unitary Siegel-Weil formula and a large row of compatible labels give positive irreducibility and counting constants on a large row. The counting exponent is at least twice one plus the family constant.

D394.statement: For every slot system and bundle linkage, six conditions hold eventually on built and good members: evaluation on the reference chain, twisted points, periods at zero and after twisting, compatibility of the two evaluations, and the level-prime column valuations.

D395.statement: If the chart restriction holds at each prime, then at all indicated CM moduli points and levels the seven local packages hold: inert, Frobenius/conjugation, split, vanishing and their specified variants.

D396.statement: From the twelve indicated unitary, Galois, local correspondence and real representation inputs, every sufficiently large divisible family eventually has a nonnegative threshold beyond which its augmented points satisfy the untwisted surjectivity condition.

D397.statement: From the eight stated automorphic, Galois, crystalline, character and local correspondence inputs, every eligible record object satisfies the prescribed exponent bound for each pair of size parameters.
