Its proof matches an exact Weyl exponent cut, a numerical expansion and a crystalline model.

D398.statement: Under the page-run, rank, numerical and realization hypotheses, the same chosen prime data give the definite and indefinite lift-index height inequalities.

D399.statement: There exist a real constant and two functions of the growth constants giving, past threshold and under the run and record hypotheses, the normed net inputs and the page support inequalities, including the archimedean lower bound for the distinguished section.

D400.statement: The chart-restriction hypothesis for every prime gives a single lower threshold such that any tied leaf with the page, size, scale, rank and content conditions satisfies the local depth inequalities at good primes.

D401.statement: Under the stated detection input, stabilizer hypotheses and rank and size restrictions, a cusp form whose designated coefficients vanish on every qualifying CM arc over every coefficient extension belongs to the indicated filtered subspace.

D402.statement: A threshold depending on two constants works for every top datum with the prescribed laws, injective coefficient map and valid parameters in every rank: each eligible page run past threshold admits the required normalized inputs.

D403.statement: The decay, reciprocity, ray-class, discrete-series, globalization and rational-series assumptions imply the export compatibility at every eventual augmented point, twisted place and row index.

D404.statement: If the export, twist, shared, bad-place and exponent statements hold, every sufficiently large divisible family eventually satisfies the untwisted surjectivity requirement above a single nonnegative threshold.

D405.statement: The page conditions on the record objects imply their geometric conditions, comprising the supremum and spanning estimates and the other components of the specified geometric record.

D406.statement: For each of the two compatible runs, at every twisted place and row index the specified trace-class rank comparison holds away from the owned position, using that run's level and the fixed two characters.

D407.statement: The seven decay, unitary Siegel-Weil, doubling, finiteness and formal-degree hypotheses give a closed family estimate: eventually at each point the twisted-side lambda inequality holds for every real size parameter.

T05.statement:
For every $P$, both of the following assertions hold on the admissible
families. First, for a family with \nolinkurl{DIVinN}, some $C_0\ge0$ works
eventually at points $p$ satisfying \nolinkurl{More}: for $C\ge C_0$ the
false-side row satisfies \nolinkurl{ON}. This gives the upper bound on the
sum of the two conjugate-place indices for every twisted place, nonnegative
row errors there, and the summed weighted-error bound $E_{1,j}$ for each $j$.
Second, eventually at points and for all $C$, the true-side row satisfies
$N_{L6,j}\le\log\lambda_j(\mu_0,p,v)$ for every $j,p,v$ in the row datum.

D408.statement: The eight stated cohomological, character, density, Galois, base-change, crystalline and local hypotheses give an exponent bound for every record object, for all two size parameters.

D409.statement: Given the third-place unitary hypotheses and rational row, for every local correspondence, dependence constant and eventually large retwisting property, one obtains the CM mass ratio, eventual membership and linked bundles on a large good restriction for that extension.

D410.statement: For the member, elliptic, third-layer, weight, local, series and multiplicity hypotheses, the normalized extension at the origin has both eventual membership and linked bundles on a large good slot.

D411.statement: With the stated arithmetic, real and local inputs, stage extensions, witnesses for moving data and good normalized objects, the given extension belongs to the eventual member class with trivial extra extension slot.

D412.statement: Given the discrete-series, decay, mass and comparison assumptions, when the extra extension is empty and the third-level condition holds, a pinned third-stage datum extends to a fourth-stage one.

D413.statement: Under the paired-stage assumptions on automorphy, lattices and multiplicities, the specified extension admits eventual members and admits linked bundles on a large restriction of its good slot.

D414.statement: The specialization inputs give the four third-layer existence statements for every dependence constant at the chosen local correspondence: settings and forms, series, moduli points and the bounded character data at those points.

D415.statement: For the given real datum and face, assume the comparison hypotheses, unit conductor ideal, agreement of the indicated place sets and the fixed-point condition at conjugation-invariant good places. Every admitted scalar form then satisfies the bilinear formula, and each theta operator has injective adjoint.

D416.statement: The seven listed real representation and unitary Weil inputs imply zeroth-stage extension of the adelic data over the allowed larger coefficient fields.

D417.statement: Given the listed representation, reciprocity and ray-field hypotheses, a compatible parameter extension and the stipulated multiplicity identities, there is a large restriction of the good slot on which a linked bundle exists.

D418.statement: The member and multiplicity-cover hypotheses give a stage with a saturated pre-state, empty localization index type and zero eta at every rank and place.

D419.statement: Global reciprocity, the CM good-model and Weber assumptions, the named real representation inputs and convergent Siegel-Weil formula together furnish the compatible-system hypotheses for family members.

T06.statement:
Assume $P$ and row rationality. For any $h,c,A$ as in T03 with $A$
eventually large, three conclusions hold. For every unramified CM datum and
$M\ge3$ the ratio of standard lattice masses in ranks $M$ and $M-1$ equals
the prescribed \nolinkurl{massRatioRightSide}. At $p_A(c)$ one has the base,
first stage, export and second stage of automorphic membership. Finally, there
is a large-base slot $R$ such that eventually every constructed point of
the good slot intersected with $R$ admits, at every real scale, a bundle
with the specified linkage.

D420.statement: The prime-stage member hypotheses, together with the indicated series and multiplicity conditions, give eventual membership and existence of a linked bundle after a large restriction for the extension with origin.

D421.statement: For each twist-good family satisfying the common normalization facts with nonnegative bound and the special bounds at two and three, there are uniform constants such that every eligible member with finite odd Selmer data admits a hub satisfying the required estimates.

D422.statement: Bloch-Kato local conditions, local Tate duality and the local Euler characteristic give the stated truncated-series conclusion for every local comparison datum and every real constant at least 320.

D423.statement: Given crystalline lattices and the stated Fontaine, numerical and good-lattice hypotheses, a surjective map of the two lattices lifts finite local cocycles after multiplication by the prime to exponent seven times the indicated period and length expression.

D424.statement: Under the rank hypotheses, for each family there is a threshold such that every member beyond it satisfying the normalization facts obeys the congruence-index bound at the eligible nonexceptional places and rank parts.

D425.statement: With the stated hub, numerical and position conditions, at an inert prime in the permitted range every selected good representation satisfies the truncated-series admission condition for the given representation, length and conductor data.

D426.statement: Under the enumerated local admissibility, Fontaine, de Rham/crystalline and unit-generator hypotheses, the local counting conclusion for the datum holds at constant 800.

D427.statement: For a twist-good family whose every sufficiently large member has the Galois normalization preconditions and four ties, the recorded cut and two/three-prime assumptions imply uniform constants for the family link at every eligible lift.

D428.statement: The third-layer and depth-zero hypotheses give at each member a tied character, an admissible depth-zero pair with the eigenspace spanning property, the polynomial inequality and the local series property.

D429.statement: Degree-one Chebotarev, local finiteness, Tate duality and the Euler characteristic, together with the chosen normalization preconditions and four ties, give a good cut; on the cut the normalization facts and the four ties both hold.

T07.statement:
Assume the two-layer linkage hypotheses, the third-layer published inputs,
geometric Galois compatibility, the series input \nolinkurl{SerN},
depth-zero support, local finiteness, local Tate duality and the local Euler
characteristic. For each $h,c$, the linked norm bound at two and three
implies the linked norm condition for $\mathrm{LinkN}$ at the same $p(c)$.
On a family $F_m$, the latter conclusion says that some $C,x_0$ work for
every $x\ge x_0$, index $i$ with finite odd Tate--Shafarevich part, and lift
$j$: the local condition \nolinkurl{LinkN_at} holds for its size datum at
$j,C$. This unfolds the abbreviation \nolinkurl{NLink.Final.mainTheorem}.

D430.statement: The published third-layer, geometric Galois, series, depth-zero, finiteness and local duality inputs imply, for every chosen local correspondence, the Galois preconditions for the given normalization at each member of the third-layer point data.

D431.statement: Given the rank and cut hypotheses, third-layer data, geometric compatibility, depth-zero support and Galois preconditions at members, the linked family bound at two and three implies the linked normalized family condition.

D432.statement: With the stated local and good-cut inputs, intersect the linked restriction on which normalization preconditions and four ties hold with the one giving the family bounds at two and three. On that restriction the norm row gives the eventual family linking condition.

T15.statement:
Assume the self-intersection bound and injectivity on small sections.
Take (i) the toroidal KS, seminegative Lie, Green cuspidal, point
separation and Fubini--Study Chow inputs, (ii) the Hodge-bundle record,
(iii) integral Siegel toroidal models, charts for fans, toroidal charts
and arithmetic degree, (iv) Grothendieck deformation, (v) the eight
statements on Kawamata--Viehweg, log-canonical $L^2$ extension, holomorphic
sections, nef numerics, Chow forms, their integrality and hyperplane
sections, and proper-intersection length, and (vi) the deep estimate T14.
Then T13's uniform inequality for all the covolumes holds.

D433.statement: The global volume, deep-model, size, cover-degree and flat-degree inputs imply the common lower height estimate for the admissible covering data.

D434.statement: The Hodge class pulls back as prescribed, and a positive power of its line bundle divided by any chosen line bundle has a section nonvanishing at the chosen interior point.

D435.statement: For each allowed determinant subgroup the assigned cusp weight has a section whose determinant multiplier acts injectively on the full section ring.

D436.statement: The published Hodge bundle fields, Gram bound and anchor estimate imply the low-defect inequalities at the distinguished lifts.

D437.statement: The common degree, share, flat-degree and deep-goodness estimates give the weighted sum of heights over the selected cover.

D438.statement: The squared supremum norm of each admissible section is bounded by the stated Tamagawa constant times its squared Petersson norm.

D439.statement: Extension of a section across the boundary is equivalent to extension after pullback and multiplication by the displayed canonical differential on the resolution.

D440.statement: On the split toroidal model each determinant section in the prescribed character space is a unique scalar multiple of the chosen one.

D441.statement: Componentwise antitone weights with the prescribed gap give goodness of the model and goodness of every component chart.

D442.statement: For an admissible family and weight run, give the valuation and multiplicity bound comparing the two indicated weights on the same model.

D443.statement: The published Hodge bundle records imply the flat-degree bound for the designated flat generators on the cover.

D444.statement: For the designated toroidal flag, component and generically closed function field, every weight with nonnegative gaps gives the stated nefness on curves.

D445.statement: Assume the abelian de Rham input and the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism at every field-valued frame for the selected CM type. On the interior of the chosen modification of the flag model there is a nowhere-vanishing section identifying its canonical bundle with the pulled-back standard line of weight \ensuremath{\kappa}, and the identification satisfies the Kodaira–Spencer compatibility condition.

D446.statement: The specified lower gap bound at successive positions of the weight implies the required birationality on every component of the chart.

D447.statement: The common geometric and Hodge data, together with the Gram, deep-existence, goodness, size, degree and share bounds, control the bad set on the lifts.

D448.statement: Suppose the generic boundary is a simple normal crossings divisor, and B is the given variety embedded openly in the generic fibre compatibly with the base. A flag compactification factors through B and has dimension dim B plus the sum, over embeddings, of the binomial coefficients choose(multiplicity,2). Each compatible field-valued point of B and eigenframe of its image has a unique lift carrying that frame.

D449.statement: Assume the published Hodge-bundle inputs. There is a nonnegative absolute constant C with the following property. Take an admissible row of the project data with both signature parts positive, half the CM field degree greater than two, the comparison laws and a good deep cover. Write f,r for its numerical parameters. Suppose L is at least one, log M is at most 30L, the field size is at most 3L, log(fr) is at most L, and the cover parameter o is at most 391(frL)\ensuremath{{}^{2}}. For dominant weights a and even n at least 8fr+4, with every indicated positive-signature entry exceeding n/2 and log(sizeK) at most 20L, the weight lattice contains a set spanning the coefficient space. At every embedding its norms and all its specified Petersson quantities are bounded by exp(C(frL)\ensuremath{{}^{2}} sizeK).

D450.statement: Assume the indicated covering hypotheses and Grothendieck deformation theorem. For a framed field-valued point of the CM moduli problem with p+q\ensuremath{\ge}1, use the embeddings carrying the distinguished root to its chosen complex value. There is a universal first-order deformation over the square-zero extension indexed by their Hodge coordinates. Every tangent lift is its pullback in a unique coordinate direction, and a direction is the Kodaira–Spencer coordinate precisely when it gives that lift.

D451.statement: Under the stated adelic-to-frame comparison laws, for each good coefficient embedding and each choice of orthogonal base frames and fundamental sets, their total volume is positive and finite. For any nonnegative extended-real measurable family invariant under the specified left arithmetic and right Borel actions on the domains, its integral for the adelic probability measure times that total volume equals the sum of its transported integrals over the fundamental sets.

D452.statement: Under the cover laws, p,q \ensuremath{\ge} 1, [E:Q]/2 > 2, an admissible index and a good deep cover, each even weight preserves the cusp condition. Pullback along any level automorphism carries integral cusp forms into the same lattice and preserves the norm at every embedding.

D453.statement: The specified admissible PEL data have integral framed points outside their finite set of bad primes.

D454.statement: Assume the specified published Hodge-bundle input. Uniformly on all sufficiently large eligible family points and lifts, each complex embedding admits a positive factor c with |log c| bounded by C times the point’s scale unit. For every cusp form at that lift, its real-model norm equals c times its Petersson expression, with the same c for all forms.

D455.statement: The Gram and measure estimates from the Hodge bundle package give the lambda bound for the lift.

D456.statement: On the admissible deep model, the compactified top Chern number equals the specified volume.

D457.statement: Under the size condition, every admissible family eventually satisfies the following simultaneously at all points, for each nonfinal row and good cover. The row laws hold, its successor is in range, L is at least one, log M is at most 30L, the field size is at most 3L, log(fr) is at most L, expL is at least four, every host rank exceeds r+1, f is at least eight and r at least 100. The flat degree has absolute value at most 9rL and log(kappa) is at most 2L. Writing z for zBase, P for the sampling parameter and t for the row length, one has z\textasciicircum{}12 \ensuremath{\le} P, tP \ensuremath{\le} sqrt(b), zed·P·kappa \ensuremath{\le} b and zed \ensuremath{\le} 1/2 for the first endpoint weight. The coordinate absolute sums of both endpoint weights are at most z\ensuremath{{}^{2}}(kappa/t+1), and the corresponding sum along every weight through step t is at most z\ensuremath{{}^{2}} kappa.

D458.statement: Assume the stated covering, Hodge-bundle, integral Siegel, toroidal, deformation, quoted Hodge and Lie seminegativity inputs. Take an admissible index of a core satisfying its laws, with p,q\ensuremath{\ge}1, half the host degree greater than two, and a good deep model. Write h for the flag dimension. If u has gaps at least (h+3)(binom(h+1,2)+4(p+q)+h+3), both lambda and n u\ensuremath{-}lambda are decreasing in each embedding, and n times the top degree of u is strictly less than (a+1) times its degree on the component, then the complex rank at lambda is at most binom(a+h,h) times that degree.

D459.statement: Assume the frame comparison laws on both levels, the level-cover predicate and the Galois coefficient extension. For dominant data with even n there exists a semilinear pullback of weight-wtZ(a,n) cusp forms realizing pullback of rules. It preserves finite linear independence after scalar extension and the norms at compatible embeddings, and it detects integral-lattice membership. Its scalar span consists exactly of fiber-constant rules. For any source subspace C, multiplication by any element of the target different carries target lattice vectors in the span of pullbacks of C into the integral span of pullbacks of lattice vectors in C.

D460.statement: Assume the published Hodge-bundle input. There is an absolute C \ensuremath{\ge} 0 such that on each good deep cover and component satisfying the specified level, field-size and flat-line bounds, dominant weights \ensuremath{\lambda} with the stated gap and size bounds admit n short generators of the cusp lattice. Writing u = frL, their norm radius b satisfies log b \ensuremath{\le} C(u\ensuremath{{}^{3}}\ensuremath{\sum}|\ensuremath{\lambda}|+u\ensuremath{{}^{5}}) and log n \ensuremath{\le} C u\ensuremath{{}^{3}}.

D461.statement: The Gram, recursion, truncation, bad-set, lambda, size, core and lower bounds imply the common covolume estimate for the family.

D462.statement: The low-defect, ring, map, rank, minimal-generator, flatness and uniform lower estimates together give the lower-bound condition on the lifted cover.

D463.statement: The height, sum, size, degree, share and good-model inequalities imply the uniform lower bound on the selected lifts.

D464.statement: The published Hodge-bundle inputs give the Gram matrix condition on the selected cover.

D465.statement: The Gram and measure hypotheses and the rationality condition on the lift imply the core inequality.

D466.statement: Under the deep-goodness, size and flat-degree bounds, the stated toroidal and Grothendieck deformation input bounds the degree of the cover.

D467.statement: For a geometric family and its constants, valid mutually compatible rows admit columns, two sets of weights and forms meeting both the family column conditions and all output conditions at those rows.

D468.statement: From the geometric family, compatible rows and existence of the required column outputs, one obtains columns simultaneously satisfying row laws, the chart at zero, the tail link, commutation and the family-ratio condition.

D469.statement: The real-pack family conditions, positive bottom rank and surjectivity at every chain stage, with the indicated strong approximation and real hypotheses, yield a common central bottom element and for every word compatible character and bottom data pinned to it.

D470.statement: With the family and local inputs in the statement, the multiplicity condition holds at every bundle and also as an eventual linked row for the same parameter extension.

D471.statement: A placed and framed bottom realization at the prescribed central element produces bottom data having exactly the specified lattice and base element and satisfying the pin at that element.

D472.statement: For the Weil representation, discrete-series, finiteness and decay hypotheses, every specified extension of the local normalization has the linked defect row giving the definite-side condition at all eligible bundles.

D473.statement: Green and Zelevinsky inputs and the linked good finite-type assumptions produce on a linked slot a Hida setting, an appropriate operator and an isometric identification simultaneously tying automorphy, the row dictionary and the labels.

D474.statement: The third-place unitary inputs give, for every choice of local parameters and dependence constant, the open parameter record; its fields include primitive, lambda, divisibility, tie, labeling, geometric, multiplicity, kappa and defect rows.

D475.statement: The indicated Harish-Chandra, decay, factorization and local representation hypotheses take a linked lambda-prime row to the linked row satisfying the three kappa laws.

T08.statement:
Given $P$, every reciprocity system $h$ and every real $c$, the following
twelve conditions are linked at $p(c)$: primitivity, lambda-prime bounds,
divisors, decomposition points, selection jumps, ties, labels, goodness,
weak geometric compatibility, multiplicities, kappa and defect. In
particular the geometric field supplies a comparison with the prescribed
point summands, class-sum normalization, point compatibility and the
additional point condition \nolinkurl{More}.

D476.statement: Suppose the local reduced criterion holds, finite class stabilizers are eventually trivial, the designated subgroup is standard, and second admissibility and the required nonprincipal descent hold on the class. Then the full family group link holds, including its primewise bounds and subpower loss.

D477.statement: For every admitted datum and every admissible quadruple of constants, there is a positive threshold C0. Every C at least C0 satisfies the auxiliary orbit-valuation conclusion for that datum.

B05.statement:
Assume the finite-field Green character statement. For any family class
$\mathcal A$, take the data and hypotheses of the alternative shape:
existence from the Minkowski division input, the family duties, and a
twist selection with spectral, level, height, column and bounded-row
realisations. Impose its twist, primitivity, division, point, size,
literature, volume, decay and count conditions; its definite rows and
indefinite selections; its point, period and complement conditions for
the served twists; its closed count, projection and real-place ties;
and its volume-ratio and genus-mass hypotheses. The two scalar predicates
$V,NR$ in the shape are true. Its extra family premise is the following
closed link on $D_3(3,\mathcal A)$: eventually there are common constants
$C,x_0$ for a family so that, for each member at $x\ge x_0$ with finite
prescribed localisation lengths and each lift $j$, summability of their
weighted prime terms $v_\ell$ gives
\[
  \eta_j\le dZ_{0,j}\left[C\{fmbL^2+(\log x)^2N_c\}
                         +\sum_\ell v_\ell\right].
\]
Here $\eta_j$ sums weighted local errors at the varying places. The shape
concludes that for every $\lambda>1$ and every request $G$, if hosts exist
on $\lambda$-windows and every family in the request class eventually
satisfies its Selmer bound, then there are $e_D,e_L$ and $\varepsilon_1>0$.
For every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_1$ that class contains a family
with constants $K,c_{HH},e_K,C_L,x_0$ and tied data on every window scale
$x\ge x_0$.

D478.statement: Closed compatibility of the group lattices and closed second admissibility imply the group link: some C,x0 and delta tending to zero give the gain bounds at the inert or signal primes, served-orbit containment and mean-kappa bound simultaneously for every large member, with allowance b\textasciicircum{}delta(x).

D479.statement: On the enriched class D3(3,A), duty, tied real-place second-layer data, the mass-ratio estimate and the genus-mass hypotheses give two uniform implications. Chosen data of exponent 3 give fullness and the prescribed degree/rank relation. Tuple and discriminant-size bounds give the global comparison with constants 2, CH, 3, 2, 0.

D480.statement: Fix a spectral, base-level, column and height selection with compatible twists, primitive indefinite realizations, and the division and point rows. The selected definite-row and single-map hypotheses supply the corresponding comparison of the selected division-kernel rows with exponent 2.

D481.statement: Suppose a family class has a tail of division-kernel data and a closed uniform bound for those kernels whenever the tuple and discriminant-size estimates hold. Under these size estimates the covered-twist and eta-sum bounds imply the division height, frame and slope bounds on a common tail.

D482.statement: Assume the spectral and tied base-level selections, their column and height compatibilities, bounded primitive realizations, division and point rows, and the real-place second-layer ties. On D3(3,A) the tuple and discriminant-size bounds yield the remaining division bounds at exponents 2 and CH.

D483.statement: Given the Minkowski-to-design choice, twist selection, duty, closed tuple-size implication, class-number identity at every design index and thinness input, each sufficiently small positive epsilon and every transported threshold admit a family in the twisted, smoothed, level-enriched class and CH at least zero, simultaneously large and chosen at exponent 3 with tuple and discriminant-size bounds.

D484.statement: For the supplied spectral and real-family selections, decay and transport data, type and volume records, uniform constant c30 and large-scale hypotheses, the tuple-size bound implies the spectral link with C0=3 on D3(3,A). This controls off-diagonal Hilbert–Schmidt norms, diagonal deviation and total dimension under the prescribed dimension-ratio window.

D485.statement: With a twist selection and family duty, every sufficiently large member of D3(3,A) satisfies local coverage for the twisted data, uniformly over the indices at that scale.

D486.statement: Assume Green’s finite-group character input and the closed existence of injectively labelled, joined and counted rows with cIc positive. Eventually at every index the row deviations are nonnegative and their delta statistic is at most exp(\ensuremath{-}x\textasciicircum{}(ez/7)).

D487.statement: Assume the local reduced criterion for every datum, closed group compatibility and closed second admissibility. Then on the family class the uniform primewise group gain and cost bounds, served-orbit containment and mean-kappa bounds hold eventually with a subpower allowance.

D488.statement: With nested classes C\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}} inside C and E, designs for the twice-enriched C\ensuremath{{}^{\prime}}, eventual Selmer bounds on E, and the nine specified closed links on the designs for C, there exist exponents and a small-epsilon range. For each epsilon in that range some family in E admits fixed constants and a tied chain at every sufficiently large scale in its window.

D489.statement: Twist selection and duty on A give on D3(3,A) constants C,x0 and a function delta tending to zero such that for every x at least x0 and every index the group gain, orbit and mean-kappa estimates hold with the additive allowance b\textasciicircum{}delta(x).

D490.statement: For every datum and every four bounds for which the table-line hypotheses are admitted, the cleaning and plane-Gram hypotheses give a positive threshold beyond which the stated orbit-valuation bounds hold.

D491.statement: A closed form giving a positive threshold and all larger orbit-valuation bounds from the four admission constants remains valid when the source-cleaning and formal-chart plane-Gram witnesses are also supplied.

D492.statement: For a deep type-II tower meeting the stated rank-two context, each coefficient embedding admits an enlarged ring and a seed pair in the prescribed residual frame satisfying one of the two residual entry alternatives.

D493.statement: For a quadratic extension of totally complex fields and a rank-two cusp form of mixed weight with split bad places, there is a rank-four cuspidal induction matching the prescribed Satake system; its infinitesimal multiset is the sum at the two embeddings over each base embedding.

D494.statement: Assume cohomological control, bounded cyclotomic class ranks, the type-II and type-IV seed assertions and existence of a potential-modularity tower. For every eligible odd-prime good case below the host cutoff, the finiteness and no-end clauses hold and all irreducible points are automorphic for one choice of complex embedding.

D495.statement: For every fitted deep tower and embedding there is a coefficient ring such that every component at any sufficiently large coefficient extension admits a potential-modularity tower above it.

D496.statement: For a type-IV four-dimensional starting tower, its admissible ambient field and coefficient embedding, choose a split auxiliary prime and a residual point of prescribed support. Each eligible enlargement killing that prime then has the stipulated seed witnesses.

W06.statement:
Assume $H'$. For every algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$, large host
$(h,t)$, odd prime $\ell$, coefficient ring $O$, $0<e<t$,
$\psi\in X_h(O,e)$ and good rank-four symplectic datum $D$ in 
Case~II or III of W09, the following hold. Here the datum has character
$\psi$, ramification set the primes dividing $2\ell Np_1$, and an odd
auxiliary character built from a primitive character at $2^{n'}$ and
one of order $m_0$ at $p_1$. The prescribed $(n',p_1,m_0)$ is
$(n_{\rm II},1,1)$ in Case~II and
$(n_{\rm III},p_1(\chi),\operatorname{ord}\psi)$ in Case~III.
The goodness conditions fix the places, inertia and parity of the
characters, a lift of the mod-$\ell$ cyclotomic character of exponent
$\ell-1$, distinguished Frobenius elements and their residual
separation, and vanishing of the locally trivial residual cocycles for
$\alpha,\beta,\theta$ and their inverses. They include the distinguished
limit, the nontriviality of $\bar\alpha$ and $\bar\Psi$ on $g_0$, and an
inertial $s_0\in\ker\psi\cap\ker\omega$ of infinite cyclotomic order.
For every lift satisfying
the imposed component conditions, its weight-zero monomials generate a
module-finite $O$-algebra. At any geometric point with block image the
blocks indexed by $\{0,2\}$ span a proper subspace of $M_2$.
There is one $\iota:\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\simeq\mathbb C$ for
all irreducible geometric points. Whenever such a point is continuous
and stays irreducible on restriction to a quadratic CM field, that
restriction is attached via $\iota$ to a regular algebraic cusp form
and has the local witness of W07.

D497.statement: Under the stated Howe, local theta, toric, denominator, reflection and matching assumptions, the twelve simultaneous leading-term assertions hold, including theta and square bounds, field and denominator witnesses, bottom pairs, nonvanishing and tower compatibility.

D498.statement: The local theta inputs imply the uniform finite-place size condition, the off-support condition and the archimedean size condition of the sum.

D499.statement: The local theta inputs, the absolute functional equation, toric transport, denominator and reflection conditions, integral matching, separation of functionals and the lambda lower bound give uniform fitting of the constant function at every eventual point equipped with the required grid.

D500.statement: Fix the field and comparison rules and assume all the individual leaf estimates, kernel, height, rank, descent and admissibility conditions. There is a threshold on grid quality beyond which every qualifying eventual point has the fitted functional for every size parameter.

D501.statement: Toric conjugacy, the setting at each point, the family logarithmic-derivative bound and the field and toric witnesses imply the toric-ratio estimate for every sufficiently large grid and fitted comparison datum.

D502.statement: The local theta inputs and agreement and matching of integrals imply five joint local-sum properties: convergence/compatibility, nonzero constant coefficients, the linear relation, the second formula and rationality of the sum.

T10.statement:
Assume $F$, the automorphic join, the Hecke--Tate functional equation, both
theta comparisons of T11, separation as in T09, and the lower-weight
assertion of T05. Then some $C_{F,0}$ works for every $C_F\ge C_{F,0}$.
In each admissible family with \nolinkurl{DIVinN}, eventually every point
having the prescribed field grid of size $C_F$ satisfies, for every $C$,
the false-side functional bound
$\mu_{\max,RR}\le h_h-\operatorname{meanLog}(\kappa)$
for its numerical data $N(C)$.

D503.statement: Over an imaginary quadratic field, a regular rank-two cusp system with the weight-gap condition and almost-everywhere common Satake data over the same rational prime descends to a rational cusp system matching split Frobenius and infinite weights.

W03.statement:
Given the rank-$n$ literature record and W04, there is a common
record $H'$ with the following fifteen fields. It retains the rank-$n$
input, supplies the cohomological, conjugation and Borel-injectivity
assertions, and attaches Galois representations in rank two over totally
real fields. It supplies strong multiplicity one, the Gelfand--Kazhdan
duality, admissibility, quadratic base change and the newform
realization on the real side. Its last five fields give weak unitary
descent, the cyclic base-change and rank-two descent conditions,
definite quaternionic existence and semisimplicity of the real cuspidal
representation.

D504.statement: For a regular algebraic cuspidal representation over a totally complex field and each complex field automorphism, a cusp form realizes the conjugate finite component and the same weight multiset at each transported embedding.

D505.statement: The rank-n hypotheses, quadratic rank-two base change and admissibility over totally real fields attach a rank-two Galois representation, weight and Hodge–Tate multisets satisfying the prescribed row to every regular algebraic polarized rank-two cusp form.

D506.statement: At compact open level over a totally complex field, the cardinality of any finite family of pairwise inequivalent cohomological cuspidal representations with a fixed vector is at most the dimension of the specified coefficient-system cohomology.

D507.statement: Strong multiplicity one yields a nondegenerate complex bilinear pairing on every totally real cuspidal space, with the specified transpose-inverse, compact and infinitesimal invariance laws.

D508.statement: A totally real number field of even degree admits a central four-dimensional definite division algebra with the specified finite adelic matrix realization and complex realizations at its real places.

D509.statement: The rank-n record implies nonzero cuspidal cohomology for the chosen algebraic coefficient system whenever all infinitesimal characters match its negated weights over a totally complex field.

D510.statement: Assume a uniform construction extending each admissible field row, with the order, conductor, lcm divisibility and good prime pair stipulated in the source, to a good host with the character-share bound. For primitive psi the exponent-401 Selmer window and admissibility at all large eligible frames then give 3/2-power host windows for the cyclic level with constant 4 and Selmer bound sqrt(b).

D511.statement: For each allowed epsilon and C0 at least 1, fix uniform host constants and a lower threshold. An admitted initial host of an admissible rank tuple, with the prescribed conductor and lcm divisibility, good prime pair in its window and field rows up to floor(Y\textasciicircum{}(epsilon/5)), extends to a host at that scale and an auxiliary prime. It has the chosen constants, the four-parameter host bound, and character shares with tolerance x\textasciicircum{}(\ensuremath{-}1+epsilon).

D512.statement: For a primitive character psi, its exponent-401 Selmer window and eventual existence of scale-compatible admitted ranks on every eligible frame with the prescribed character kernel yield host supply of exponent 3/2. Every large selected scale has a host satisfying both the explicit-formula requirement for the cyclic level (constant 4) and the Selmer bound by the square root of b.

D513.statement: For each 0<epsilon<1/52, simultaneously for all sufficiently large scales and every frame of order in [x\textasciicircum{}(2+8epsilon),2x\textasciicircum{}(2+8epsilon)], there exist ranks inducing exactly that frame, with the prescribed exponent, rank, size and growth inequalities of RankVal.

B07.statement:
For each primitive character $\psi$, assume the bound of
Section~\ref{sec:mechanism} at $t=\lfloor x^{401}\rfloor$ with the
quantifiers of $V$ for this $\psi$. For every $0<\varepsilon<1/52$
there are $C_{T2},C_8,C_5,c_6,C_b,x_0$ with $C_8\ge1$ and
$C_5,c_6,C_b>0$, and a system of scales with exponent-$3/2$ windows.
At each eligible scale $s$ with $s.\varepsilon=\varepsilon$ and
$s.x\ge x_0$ there exist the specified ranks, a host with invariant
$C_{T2}$, and an auxiliary prime parameter satisfying the rank and
host-size conditions. The character request at these data enforces the
kept-character and share conditions for $\operatorname{cyc}(\psi)$,
the pointwise bounds on the other characters (logarithmic-derivative
constant $4$), and the finite-length Selmer bound with budget $\sqrt b$.

D514.statement: Given ranks R and a host axial datum H0 on their frame, every cutoff b and admissible set of choices with all field rows to b and both distinguished primes greater than 4tr+1 extend to a host with precisely H0, cutoff b and the same choices after identifying the number fields.

D515.statement: For each 0<epsilon<1/52 there is a uniform threshold: at every later scale and every frame of order between x\textasciicircum{}(2+8epsilon) and twice this value, a rank tuple realizes that same frame, satisfies its scale bounds and is admitted for the given initial host.

D516.statement: Closed discriminant-size control and the served-prime condition for the chosen twists yield a nonnegative C and a common eventual service bound at every index, with its prescribed local comparison, twists, level and error data.

D517.statement: On a class with the eight designated point, period, service, column, level and size inputs, there are eventual second and twelfth local quadratic admissibility assertions for every family index. Each assertion has its own threshold.

D518.statement: For designs of any class with fixed C0, eventually at every scale and index, for every word u its level prime T does not divide its stabilizer quantity DGam.

D519.statement: Rank-four density, cohomology, the algebraic comparisons, rank-four counting and rigidity, residual cocycle vanishing, and the two rank-one controls yield the individual bounds in Cases II and III.

D520.statement: For a rank-four datum in context 2 or 3, after choosing a level killing its three characters, every irreducible automorphic characteristic-zero point is rigid under the unramified-input and adjoint-vanishing hypotheses.

W09.statement:
Assume $H'$, W05 and the rank-four conclusions of W06. Each of the
following two cases has its own $C\in\mathbb N$ depending only on
$\chi$. For every large host, $0<e<t$, odd $\ell$, closure, coefficient
ring and $\psi\in X_h(O,e)$ in the case, the length is finite and
$v_\ell(\psi,e)\log\ell\le(\ell Ne)^C$:
\begin{itemize}
\item Case II requires $e\ge2$, even order of $\chi_P$, and either
$\ell\in B_\chi$ or $\ell-1\mid2e$.
\item Case III requires $\ell\notin B_\chi$, $\ell-1\mid2e$ and
$\psi$ nontrivial of odd order.
\end{itemize}

D521.statement: The classical hypotheses give a bounded nonzero integer testing rank-four families: every admissible pairwise inequivalent family has nonzero Frobenius trace gaps and the product of their norms dominates the norm of that integer.

D522.statement: Finiteness, duality, Euler characteristics, rank-three unitary lifting, the two algebraic comparisons and the four host controls yield the Case-V individual character bound on the specified scale.

D523.statement: Every marked characteristic-zero point of a host frame over the Gaussian field satisfying the unitary automorphy condition is rigid, assuming marked automorphy, adjoint vanishing and the unlinked-end bound.

D524.statement: For every frame realizing the stated host, dualities, finiteness, local Euler characteristic and the second-cohomology bound give the vanishing condition on its indexed graded lines.

W10.statement:
Assume $H'$, W05 and the reduced unitary rank-three lifting input.
Over a model of $\mathbb Q(i)$ this input selects, for each host frame, a
marked element at which the weight-zero piece of every universal lift
is module-finite and each Type~I specialization satisfies the prescribed
automorphy clause of weight $-1$. For every $\chi$ there is $C\in\mathbb N$
such that the individual finite-length bound of W09 holds for each large
host, closure, coefficient ring, $0<e<t$ and $\psi\in X_h(O,e)$
satisfying $\ell$ odd, $\ell\in B_\chi$, $e=1$ and
\[
 R_1=16\,\operatorname{ord}(\chi)(\ell\operatorname{cond}(\chi))^2
            4^{n_0}\le 2^{c_2(\psi)}.
\]
Here $c_2$ is the exponent of $2$ in the conductor of the local
$2$-component of $\psi$, and $n_0=v_2(\ell^{f_0}-1)$, with $f_0$ the
order of $\ell$ modulo the least common multiple of $4$ and the order
of the prime-to-$\ell$ part of $\psi$ stripped of its $2$-component.

D525.statement: For a Gaussian host, a common exponent controls the sum of valuations of pairwise inequivalent admissible rank-three trace gaps times log of the prime, and each gap from the residual trace is nonzero.

D526.statement: The residual product-character cocycle criterion supplies the auxiliary-prime vanishing condition for every host frame and admissible choice of that prime.

D527.statement: For Gaussian-field host frames the reduced rank-three unitary lifting assertion gives the full one: choose a marked element, obtain finite weight-zero part of each universal deformation and the unitary automorphy clause at each type-I characteristic-zero point.

D528.statement: Cohomological control, the three algebraic comparison lemmas, Kato input, two rigidity results, level admissibility and unramified automorphy bound a single finite Selmer length by twice a sum of trace-difference valuations for an admissible finite family.

W08.statement:
Assume $H'$, the uniform bound W05, the two-twist vanishing of W07,
and the rank-three automorphy input for unramified coefficient rings.
In the latter, a common marked element gives finiteness and the
Type~I automorphy and Type~II modularity conclusions for the
specializations of each allowed deformation ring. For every $\chi$
there are $C\in\mathbb N$ and primes $r_1,r_2$ such that, for each
large host with $q_1,d>\max(r_1,r_2)$, $0<e<t$, every algebraic
closure, every choice of coefficient rings $O_\ell$ and every finite
set $T$ of odd primes with $\ell\notin B_\chi$, $\ell-1\nmid2e$,
all the lengths below are finite and
\[
 \sum_{\ell\in T}\log\ell\!
       \sum_{\psi\in X_h(O_\ell,e)} v_\ell(\psi,e)\le (Nt)^C .
\]

D529.statement: For a type-II point and a continuous rank-two extension with the stipulated determinant and dense modularity, the marked cohomology and adjoint-lifting hypotheses force the indicated rank-two adjoint vanishing over the chosen CM field.

D530.statement: At a marked automorphic type-I local point, the rank-three representation obtained by restriction is admissible at the given weight and level, under cohomology, marking and unlinked-end control.

D531.statement: Rank-three family counting and the one-character estimate produce a nonzero integer of uniformly bounded logarithm for every admissible test prime; at other primes each relevant character-orbit sum of lengths is at most twice its local valuation.

D532.statement: The two-test-prime orbit bound implies Case I: for each primitive character choose two auxiliary primes and an exponent; beyond both primes the log-prime-weighted sum of lengths over every finite set of odd Case-I primes is bounded by (host level times cutoff) to that exponent, and every length is finite.

D533.statement: At a marked local point of type I which is automorphic with the indicated multiplier, the first rigidity implication gives vanishing of the adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer group under the cohomology, marking, adjoint-lifting and unlinked-end hypotheses.

D534.statement: The rank-n hypotheses and a uniform second-cohomology bound give the rank-three cohomology inputs, including the local record, Poitou–Tate, global finiteness and Euler characteristic, and that same uniform bound.

D535.statement: For arbitrary fixed window constants and positive cutoff, the four character counts and residual count imply the height/vanishing estimate under the K-bound and normalized global and local duality and finiteness.

D536.statement: For a primitive character, combine the joint window and odd-minus bound at the stipulated cutoff to get an interval from Y to Y squared inside the admitted scale range, with the Selmer bound at each point for every prescribed page function.

W13.statement:
Assume Poitou--Tate duality, local finiteness and local Tate duality.
Fix a $C_K$ satisfying W05's cohomological bound and constants as
in W12 giving its simultaneous bound at $C_t=401$. Assume W14's
minus-part bound, the collective estimate of W08, both individual
estimates of W09, the restricted Case~V estimate of W10 and the
individual estimate of W09's shape for Case~Z (odd
$\ell\notin B_\chi$, $\ell-1\mid2e$, $\psi=1$).
Then the Selmer window $V$ of \nodeid{P013} holds.

D537.statement: For each cutoff exponent at least one, the odd-minus bound along the prescribed windows is equivalent to the unrestricted estimate with one constant for all admissible composite fields and all integral heights and twists at least two.

D538.statement: Poitou–Tate, local duality and finiteness, the K and two-part tower bounds at 401, character Counts I, II, III and V and the residual Count Z yield one common height-and-length window at cutoff 401.

D539.statement: At any positive cutoff, the tower window and height/vanishing bound for the same constants imply simultaneous control on a single interval for all admissible prime-pair data.

D540.statement: The joint arithmetic window at exponent 401 together with the odd minus-part estimate at 401 yields the simultaneous Selmer window at exponent 401 for every primitive character.

D541.statement: A cyclotomic tower with generator bound R and the stated duality hypotheses admits at most R exceptional parameters; away from their p-adic neighborhoods the twist kernel in layer m has length at most R' times (max(m,j0)+c+B), together with the second tower bound.

D542.statement: The uniform K-bound and the fixed odd-prime and common two-primary bounds admit one system of constants for all cutoff exponents at least one, giving the fixed- and moving-prime window estimates together.

D543.statement: For each abelian datum, bounded cyclotomic class ranks give one R for all admissible pairs and all fields realizing their two-primary base, with both the generator and tower conditions.

W12.statement:
Assume Poitou--Tate duality, local finiteness and local Tate duality
in the coefficient models for W05, the class-rank bound W11 and W05.
There are functions $R_0(M),R_\ell(L)$ with values in $\mathbb N$
and a real $c>0$ such that the following works for every $C_t\ge1$.
Take an abelian field datum $M$ of modulus $m$, a finite set $B'$ of
odd primes with abelian data $L_\ell$ containing $\mu_\ell$, a real
$A_1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1/52$. Set
\[
 R=R_0(M)+\sum_{\ell\in B'}R_\ell(L_\ell),\qquad
 J=2^{R+2}(2cC_t/\varepsilon)^R .
\]
There is $X_0$ uniform in the integer functions $e,t$ satisfying,
for $x\ge2$, $2\le e(x)$, $2^{e(x)}\le x^{A_1}$ and
$2\le t(x)\le x^{C_t}$. For $X\ge X_0$ and primes $q\equiv3\pmod8$,
$d\equiv7\pmod{16}$ with $(qd,m)=1$ and
$\log(qd)\le X^{\varepsilon/(4J)}$, there exists $Y$ with
$X^{1/J}\le Y$ and $Y^2\le X$. At every $x\in[Y,Y^2]$ the sum over
$1\le k<t(x)$ of the localization-kernel lengths is finite term by term
and at most $\exp(x^{4\varepsilon/5})$ in each of two settings:
at $2$ in every field of type $(M,e(x),q,d)$, and at each
$\ell\in B'$ in every cyclotomic layer over a model of $L_\ell$
of degree $\ell^{\operatorname{Nat.log}_\ell(R_\ell(L_\ell))+3}$.
The integer logarithm at zero is zero. The field type uses the fixed
group in \nodeid{P013} with the defining kernel of $M$ in place
of $\ker\chi$.

D544.statement: Under those same two hypotheses, each abelian datum admits one R for all eligible moving prime pairs: at each pair there is a two-primary base field realizing the tower length bounds with this R.

D545.statement: For an odd prime and abelian datum containing its roots of unity, bounded cyclotomic class ranks provide R uniform over realizations of that base, bounding the generators of its Iwasawa module and giving the specified tower of layers.

D546.statement: Ferrero–Washington rank boundedness and the tower estimate give a suitable finite R and both length estimates for each fixed abelian base containing the odd prime roots of unity.

D547.statement: For a level and host satisfying the explicit-formula record and a compatible additive-character functional, the group-model prime sum over the kept characters, with weight 1/(3o+1), equals the level prime sum at every real y.

B08.statement:
For a level $\mathcal L$, fixed real $e_D,e_L,K,c_{HH},e_K,C$ and
$\varepsilon>0$ there exists $x_1$ such that, for every $x\ge x_1$,
frame, host on that frame and finite test set $TT$, the following two
conditions imply
\[
       \mathcal G_{\mathcal L}(x)\le x^{1/2+(e_D+e_L+7)\varepsilon}.
\]
First, the host and level have the same order $o$, represent every kept
character in the positive family, and agree on the distinguished
quadratic character's exceptional status. Each translate of the subgroup
$A_0$ has a share of $TT$ within $x^{-1+\varepsilon}$ of its target
($4/(3o+1)$ for $A_0$ and $3/(3o+1)$ otherwise, in the equivalent
unnormalised counting inequality). For the positive-family characters
outside the kept set and all negative-family characters the bounds are
$|G_\chi(x)|\le x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ and $|(L'/L)(1,\chi)|\le C\log x$.

Second, there are finite unit and word data, with nonempty word fibres,
a map onto every element of $A_0$, and arithmetic coefficients whose
nontrivial character logarithmic derivatives agree with the host's.
They identify the lattice top and place indices with $TT$ and the
index-two subgroup, and satisfy the lattice hypotheses, error-window
and $B_0,N_c$ bounds in \hyperref[sub:B10]{B10} and the size, thin,
cost and remaining-size conditions in \hyperref[sub:B09]{B09}, with
$T_2\subset A_0$. The scale and exponent of the lattice data are
$x,\varepsilon$; their division, loss and height exponents are bounded
above by $e_D,e_L,c_{HH}$ respectively.

D548.statement: For x>0, a host explicit-formula record and compatible functional give the zero character in the kept set, band membership and normalization at sgc0, at most 4o band characters, the TT character-share error at most 4o x\textasciicircum{}(\ensuremath{-}1+epsilon)|TT|, the fixed bound on nonzero kept characters, and C log x on the others.

D549.statement: With x>0, explicit-formula data and compatible character functional, the omitted-character correction SigA on the host subgroup and kept set is at most 4o x\textasciicircum{}(1/2+epsilon).

D550.statement: For positive epsilon and fixed K,cHH,eK there exists x0 such that for every x at least x0 both log x and the constant KBig(K,cHH,eK) are at most x\textasciicircum{}epsilon.

D551.statement: For each eligible CM subfield, procyclic local data and positive twist e, a power of the prime kills the minus kernel. Its exponent times log of the prime is bounded by C times the field degree, (e+1) and log(e times the prime times the conductor parameter).

D552.statement: There is a uniform nonnegative constant bounding the minus length times log of the prime for procyclic local data over every eligible CM subfield of a cyclotomic field, including finiteness of the length. The upper bound is C p [E:Q]\textasciicircum{}2 (e+1) log(e p N)\textasciicircum{}2.

W14.statement:
Assume the following character estimate. For every abelian CM field
$F$, compatible algebraic closure, and cyclotomic action of
$(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z)^\times$ on $F$ ($N>0$), take an odd prime
$\ell\nmid[F:\mathbb Q]$, a finite DVR
$O\subset\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ over $\mathbb Z_\ell$, $k\ge1$,
and a character $\psi$ of $\operatorname{Gal}(F/\mathbb Q)$ valued in
$O^\times$. Write $\chi$ for the induced character modulo $N$.
If $\chi(-1)=(-1)^{k+1}$, the $O$-length of the $\psi$-eigenspace
of the localization kernel with twist $-k$ is at most
$\operatorname{ord}_O(a)$ for every $a\in O$ representing the
denominator-cleared primitive Bernoulli value
$\operatorname{den}(N,k+1)B_{\rm prim}(k+1,\chi)$.
Then there exists a real $C$ such that for every abelian datum $M$,
$e,t\ge2$, prime pair $q,d$ as in W12 and CM field $E$ of type
$(M,e,q,d)$, all its odd-prime minus lengths $h_\ell^-(E,k)$ for
$1\le k<t$ are finite. Put $n=[E:\mathbb Q]$, $f=\operatorname{cond}E$,
$o=\deg M$. For every finite set $T$ of odd primes,
\[
\begin{split}
 \sum_{\ell\in T}\log\ell\sum_{1\le k<t}h_\ell^-(E,k)
 &\le 3nt^2\log(tf)\\
 &\quad+C\!\sum_{\substack{p\mid o\\p\ {\rm odd\ prime}}}
                  pn^2t^2\log^2(tpf).
\end{split}
\]

D553.statement: The characterwise prime estimate implies uniform finiteness at odd primes away from the field degree and the simultaneous weighted sum bound over any finite set of such primes.

D554.statement: For each eligible parity collection of characters of modulus N and positive weight k, there are nonnegative integral weights at the primes. Their weighted logarithmic sum is uniformly bounded and each controls the negative logarithm of the product of the corresponding local algebraic values.

D555.statement: For an admissible pair and any composite field belonging to its abelian datum, every odd prime dividing the degree of that field divides the index giving the degree of the original abelian datum.

D556.statement: For any commutative ring, module X, submodule P and scalar a, if the rth power of a kills P then length(P) is at most r times the length of the a-torsion of X.

D557.statement: A number field embedded in the Nth cyclotomic field admits an action of the units modulo N through rational field automorphisms compatible with every cyclotomic lift to the fixed algebraic closure.

D558.statement: For an open normal subgroup in the character kernel with the stated two-primary restriction and a nonzero twist, cyclotomic restriction on the indicated locally trivial Selmer group is injective, with its image equal to the prescribed character eigenspace.

D559.statement: At an odd prime, with any allowed finite coefficient DVR over the p-adic integers, the rational trivial-character Selmer length vanishes in each positive twist divisible by p minus one.

D560.statement: For a prime at least five, with any allowed coefficient DVR, the rational trivial-character Selmer length vanishes in even twists e with p\ensuremath{-}1 dividing 2e but not e.

W15.statement:
For every algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$, each prime $\ell\ge5$,
each allowed coefficient ring $O$, and every even $e\ge2$ such that
$\ell-1\mid2e$, the $O$-length of the localization kernel of the
trivial-character coefficient module twisted by $\kappa^{-e}$, at
modulus $\ell$, is zero. The proof term separates
$\ell-1\mid e$ from $\ell-1\nmid e$.

D561.statement: For the fixed host, character data, positive b, and x at least 3, impose the size, thinness and cost windows, T2 inside the subgroup, and the per-unit gap bound Err. If |TT|Y is bounded by the TT sum of the subgroup-band character terms, then |TT| m b (delta2(T2)/2) Y is at most Err + 2|TT| m b/x.

D562.statement: There is one nonnegative Cd such that for every finite additive group, arithmetic data and character functional, every nontrivial character satisfies the Lipschitz bound |Gpsi(y)\ensuremath{-}Gpsi(z)| \ensuremath{\le} |y\ensuremath{-}z|(log(max(y,z))+Cd+|ell(psi)|), and |Gz(y)\ensuremath{-}Gz(z)| \ensuremath{\le} Cd|y\ensuremath{-}z|, for y,z at least 1.

D563.statement:
Let $n,n_T,n_{T,2},m$ be natural numbers and $C,\varepsilon,x,b,k,a_E,\mathrm{Err},G_x$ real. Assume the size-window inequalities, including $x\geq3$, $n,b,\varepsilon>0$ and the bounds on $m,k,a_E$ and $\mathrm{Err}$ in the linked definition. If
        \[ n_T mb\,\frac{n_{T,2}}{2n}\bigl(G_x-4x^{1/2+\varepsilon}\bigr)
        \leq \mathrm{Err}+2n_T mb/x,\]
        then $G_x\leq x^{1/2+(C+3)\varepsilon}$.

B09.statement:
Fix $C\ge0$, $\varepsilon>0$, $|c|\le1$ and $C_E,K_o,M\in\mathbb R$.
There is $x_1$ such that the implication below holds for every $x\ge x_1$.
Take a finite abelian group $H$, its prescribed arithmetic host facts
at the finite excluded set $S$, character constants $\ell(\xi)$, and
$T_2\subset A_0\le H$, $TT\subset H$. Write $n=|H|$, $n_2=|T_2|$,
$n_T=|TT|$, $\delta_2=n_2/n$, and $f=|\Gamma_\Phi|$.
For $b,k>0$, $a_E\ge0$ and integers $m,N\ge0$ assume
$m\le x^{1/2+\varepsilon/2}$, $xm\le k$, and the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item The width parameters satisfy $\eta,\theta\ge0$, $b',X'>0$,
$b'X'\le xb$ and $|a_t/b-x|\le1$ on $TT$.
Each positive column weight $w_{u,j}(\rho)$ ($u\in A_0$,
$\rho\in\Gamma_\Phi$) is in $[b,b+\eta+1]$ on the thick places
indexed by $T_2+u$ and at most $2b'$ elsewhere. The cutoff obeys
$a_t/w_{u,j}(\rho)\le N$.
\item Every frequency satisfies $|G_\xi(y)|\le y\theta$ for $y\ge X'/3$;
$2f(x+1)\theta\le1/x$, $6f(x+1)(\eta+1)\le b/x$.
Also $a_E\le2xb$, $n_T\ge nx^{-\varepsilon/8}/2$,
$\delta_2\ge x^{-\varepsilon}$, $m\ge x^{1/2-\varepsilon}$,
and $k\le n^2x^{1/2-\varepsilon}$.
\item Write $A_0^\perp$ for the frequencies trivial on the embedded $A_0$.
The kept set $K'$ contains the trivial character, lies in $A_0^\perp$,
and its characters take value one at the distinguished element $s_0$;
$|A_0^\perp|\le M$. For kept characters nontrivial on the embedded $H$,
$|\sum_{t\in TT}\xi(t)-cn_T|\le M x^{-1+\varepsilon}n_T$.
The bounds on $|\ell(\xi)|$ are $K_o$ for kept nontrivial characters
and $C_E\log x$ for discarded members of $A_0^\perp$.
\end{itemize}
Set
\[
 \mathrm{Br}=n_Ta_E(1+m^2/k)+
 m\left(2nmbx^\varepsilon+
          \frac{n_2kbx^\varepsilon}{n^2x^{-\varepsilon}}\right).
\]
If for every $u\in A_0$ the gap (the sum of $\mathrm{ASK}-\Re\mathrm{MAIN}$
over $TT$ and the $m$ columns) is at most $x^{C\varepsilon}\mathrm{Br}$,
then
\[
 \sum_{\xi\in K'}\mathrm{wt}_c(\xi)\Re G_\xi(x)
 \le x^{1/2+(C+3)\varepsilon}+\sum_{\xi\in A_0^\perp\setminus K'}|G_\xi(x)|,
\]
where $\mathrm{wt}_c$ is $1$ on characters trivial on the embedded $H$
and $c$ otherwise.

D564.statement: With the designated subgroup, kept characters and TT amplitudes, assume the derivative bound, normalization and three explicit error bounds r1–r3 by R. For every character psi in the subgroup band, |TT| times (vv(psi)\ensuremath{-}R) is at most the sum over t in TT of the real part of psi(e1(t)) times the smoothed sum at y(t).

D565.statement: When every kept character belongs to the subgroup band, the sum over that band of the scalar comparison terms vv is the kept-character sum GmA minus the omitted-character correction SigA.

D566.statement: SizeWindows is equivalent to RestSize together with the bound Err \ensuremath{\le} x\textasciicircum{}(C·epsilon) times the error bracket, the two lower bounds x\ensuremath{\ge}3 and x\textasciicircum{}(3epsilon/8)\ensuremath{\ge}26, and the remaining sign, count and scale inequalities (including m \ensuremath{\le} x\textasciicircum{}(1/2+epsilon/2) and xm \ensuremath{\le} k).

D567.statement: If the listed error windows hold and x\textasciicircum{}epsilon dominates log x and the fixed largeness constant, the per-unit error ErrX5at is bounded by x\textasciicircum{}(CErr·epsilon) times ErrText for every u.

D568.statement: Under the ten size, division, comparison, counting, slope, height and finite-parameter assumptions, Ga(u) is at most Main(u)+log|W(u)|+K0v5+M plus (1\ensuremath{-}delBar) inverse times [4 log(1+x\textasciicircum{}cHH)(K3+M+b)+(etaBar+4sqrt(eBar))x\textasciicircum{}cHH b], where M is the weighted mean of Lo5.

B10.statement:
Take finite units $U_0$, nonempty finite word sets $W(u)$, finite top
indices, and lattice data with $m$ columns and $f$ places. Take a finite
abelian group $H$, a map $\operatorname{tr}:U_0\to H$, and arithmetic
data as in \hyperref[sub:B09]{B09}. Assume top and place bijections
identify the coefficients $a_t$, column weights, Euler constant and
$\Re\ell(\chi_C)$, and express the lattice $\mathrm{ASK}(u)$ as the
sum of its arithmetic terms at $\operatorname{tr}u$.
Assume the eleven lattice hypotheses of \nodeid{P021} and the following
bounds on the data. With $x\ge1$, $0<\varepsilon\le1$,
$b\ge1$, $xb\le a$, $n_T\ge1$, $m\le x^{1/2+\varepsilon/2}$,
$xm\le k$, one has
\[
 1\le k\le\min(a,x^{e_K}),\quad 0\le L,L_a\le2x^\varepsilon,\quad
 0\le kb'\le a,\quad 0\le X''\le a,\quad 0\le a_t\le2a .
\]
Also $e_K\ge0$, $\log|W(u)|\le(k-3)\log2$, $\bar\delta\le1/2$,
$\bar\eta,\bar e\ge0$, and
$(\bar\eta+4\sqrt{\bar e})x^{c_{HH}}b\le Kx^\varepsilon n_Ta$.
The seven constants controlling division, the $E$ and $H$ errors, counting,
slope, first-slope and loss bounds are in $[0,K]$; the exponents
$e_{\rm Div},e_{\rm Loss},c_{HH}$ are nonnegative. Finally
\[
\begin{gathered}
 0\le B_0\le 2nmbx^\varepsilon,\qquad
 0\le N_c\le n_2 k b x^\varepsilon/(n^2x^{-\varepsilon}),\\
 \max\{\log x,200(1+K)^2(1+c_{HH})(1+e_K)\}\le x^\varepsilon .
\end{gathered}
\]
For each $u\in U_0$ the gap at $\operatorname{tr}u$ is at most
$x^{(e_{\rm Div}+e_{\rm Loss}+3)\varepsilon}\mathrm{Br}$ with $a_E=a$.

P021.statement:
For any data, constants and real $X_{pp}$ as above, assume the eleven hypotheses of Definition \ref{def:L-hyps}. Then for every $u_0\in U_0$
\[
  ASK(u_0)\le\mathrm{Main}(u_0)+\mathrm{Err}(u_0),
\]
where, with
$M_{Lo}=c_{Sl1}Lo_P+c_{Sl1}n_Tm(a/k+b')\,c_{Count}mL+c_{Sl1}X_{pp}+1$,
$V=2mc_EB_0+c_H(n_TaLa+mB_0)+A\,c_{Count}\log k$ and
$\bar U=c_{Slope}n_TaLa(2+m/k)+V+c_{Sl1}mB_0+M_{Lo}$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathrm{Err}(u_0)={}&A\,c_{Count}\Bigl(La+\frac{m^2La}{k}\Bigr)+E_{Div}+m\,c_EB_0\\
 &+c_{Slope}n_TaLa\Bigl(1+\frac mk\Bigr)+\log|W(u_0)|+Lo_P+M_{Lo}\\
 &+\frac1{1-\bar\delta}\Bigl(4\log(1+x^{c_{HH}})\,(\bar U+b)+(\bar\eta+4\sqrt{\bar e})\,x^{c_{HH}}b\Bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

D569.statement: Assume the per-unit arithmetic/lattice identifications, including the chosen bijections onto TT and the character set. Then for every u, Main(u) equals the sum over t in TT and j<m of the real part of MAIN(ell,a(t),w(tr(u),j)).

D570.statement: Under the Hida size setting and Count5, the d(u)-weighted mean of the lower quantities Lo5 at any unit u is at most cSl1·IO(u)+K7v5.

D571.statement: Given finite strict representatives, compatibility with local products and joins, occurrence of the candidate parts, level openness, invariance under equivalence and admissibility, the candidate frame admits the prescribed finite local lists and their uniform bound.

D572.statement: Joining two pairs of strictly equivalent parts using the same two Hecke characters preserves strict equivalence of the resulting block data.

W16.statement:
Fix a local parameter reading rule, an everywhere finite-unramified CM
extension $E/E^+$, $n\ge1$, an automorphic $\pi$ on the unitary group,
a finite set $S$ and a comparison frame for $(\pi,S)$. Choose local test
data and an auxiliary finite set $T'$ of nonsplit places disjoint from
the frame's initial set $S_0$ and its bad set. For each partition
index $i$ and each $w\in T'$, the ordered pairs of joint Hecke
eigenvalue tuples of all candidate pairs lie in a finite set. For
each $w\in S_0$ a finite list of model products suffices. Every candidate
product has the same irreducible subquotients and the same dimension
of $K'_w$-invariants as one on the list, whose invariant space is
finite-dimensional. A single integer bounds, over all candidates and
all $w\in T'$, the dimension of the candidate pair's invariants under
the prescribed two-block subgroup $I_2$.

D573.statement: If every family satisfies the eventual two-and-three place bound, each reciprocity parameter is linked to a slot in which the class has that bound eventually, uniformly as required by closure.

T25.statement:
Assume the two-layer linkage hypotheses. For every reciprocity system $h$
and parameter $p$ over $h$, the following closed family assertion satisfies the
linked norm condition at $p$. There exist $C,x_0$ such that at all
$x\ge x_0$, $x>x_1$, and each index, for every compatible local
$HW,F$ with its comparison and every hub $X,C_2$ satisfying the specified
setup, the bound holds at each twisted place $i$ with $l_i=2$ or with
$l_i=3$ and $3$ outside the host's small set. For every good $\pi$ it reads
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 v_{cc}(i,\pi)&\le s_\pi(\rho_i)+\mathrm{midF}(L,C)
       +\mathrm{VVr}(l_i)+v_{hE}(l_i)+\varepsilon_L(l_i),\\
 \mathrm{midF}(L,C)&=C f m b\log x+C x^C\mathrm{large}_2(L)^2 .
 \end{aligned}
\]

T16.statement:
Assume the Hodge-bundle record. Let $K$ be a number field with no real
embeddings, $V$ a $K$-module compatibly acted on by $\mathcal O_K$, and
$\Omega/K$ a field. Let $N_\sigma$ on $V$ have Gram data and be invariant
under conjugating $\sigma$. Let $W\subset V$ be a finitely generated
$\mathcal O_K$-module spanning $V$ over $K$, and
$\mathrm{ev}:V\to\Omega$ linear with generating ratios. For degree index
$D\ge0$ suppose $d=\mathrm{imageDeg}(\mathrm{ev},D)>0$.
Let $(X,L)$ be its integral image model over $\mathcal O_K$ with the
specified embedding $\Omega\to K(X)$ and sections indexed by $W$ for
$N_\sigma,W,\mathrm{ev},D$. If the constant metric shift $L(t)$ has
self-intersection $a$, then
\[
 a\le [K:\mathbb Q](D+1)d\,
       \bigl(\mathrm{imageHeight}(N,W,\mathrm{ev},D)+t\bigr).
\]

D574.statement: A closed family condition P and an implication from P(F,CH) to Q(F,CH) for every positive epsilon, family and CH give closure of Q on the same class.

D575.statement: Assume the regular-character classification for finite general linear groups. For every prime field size g, permitted character pairing L and degree d>0, index the cuspidal characters by monic irreducible polynomials of degree d with nonzero constant coefficient. The characters have the prescribed degrees and Frobenius-orbit value formula; the labels identify equal characters and exhaust the cuspidal ones.

D576.statement: For a unitary Hecke character of the specified nonzero infinity type, its completed functional equation implies the form with a root number of modulus one and the absolute discriminant times conductor norm raised to one-half minus the argument.

D577.statement: For a local product in an admissible block datum, its invariants under any open subgroup of the standard maximal compact are finite-dimensional.

D578.statement: For any candidate in an admissible frame, every constituent of each of its two parts has both a level and an archimedean type in the corresponding prescribed lists.

D579.statement: Equivalent complex group representations have the same subquotient test and fixed-space dimension and simultaneous finite-dimensionality at every subgroup.

D580.statement: For every frame, finite auxiliary set and allowed block rank, both prescribed subgroups in the two finite adelic general linear groups are open.

D581.statement: Strict equivalence of two block data of the same rank over a CM field gives an intertwining isomorphism of their induced local products at each finite place.

D582.statement: At fixed CM field, rank, sets of levels and archimedean types, and fixed total infinitesimal character, finitely many strict representatives suffice for every allowed block decomposition.

T09.statement:
Assume $F$, unramified Howe duality in its two spherical-span directions, and
the convergent unitary Siegel--Weil input. For each $\varepsilon$ and
$C_F\ge6510$ some $x_0$ works for all size data of exponent $\varepsilon$
at $x\ge x_0$ satisfying the row sizes and the Eisenstein tie. For every
compatible finite-group family, real datum with its level character and group
record, grid $(1,C_F,b)$, Weil model above the datum, row volume and
nonzero smooth vector $w$, there exist a real vector $\rho$ and coefficient
functional $\xi$. For every nonzero $t$ in the trivial-character evaluation
space there are a column $\Psi$ and grid datum $\Phi$ for which the
pairing of the row form of $(w,t)$ converges and is nonzero.

D583.statement: The existence of the prescribed local parameter normalization implies that same existence assertion after adjoining the eleven listed additional assumptions about local and global representations.

P025.statement:
Assume local cohomological finiteness, Tate duality, the Euler
characteristic formulas and the local Bloch--Kato theorem in the
specified coefficient models. Assume the dense ordinary vanishing
hypothesis: at every locally generic automorphic point below each
allowed ordinary adjoint cocycle is a coboundary. Let \(L\) be CM with
\(\mu_\ell\not\subset L\), take a Hida setting and level \(V\) with
\(V.S'=S\), large coefficients, \(2\le n\le4\), an admitted residual
representation, and a locally generic automorphic point \(x,\rho\)
of its universal ordinary determinant ring. For each \(v\mid\ell\)
suppose there are strictly decreasing integers \(m_i\) and \(k>0\)
such that on inertia
\[
 \bigl(\psi_{v,i}\psi_{v,j}^{-1}\chi^{m_j-m_i}\bigr)^k=1
 \quad(i,j=1,\ldots,n).
\]
For every allowed polarizing form and adjoint extension \(R\), each
continuous cocycle \(z\) whose pullback satisfies the Bloch--Kato
finite condition has the form \(z(g)=R(g)X-X\) for one matrix \(X\)
and all \(g\).

P026.statement:
Let \(\ell\) be odd, \(e\ge1\), \(A\) a place above \(\ell\), and \(W\)
a continuous integral two-dimensional representation of \(G_{\mathbb Q}\).
Assume the specified normal form: \(W\) is unramified outside \(S\)
containing the primes over \(\ell\), its determinant \(\delta\) has
square one and takes value \(-1\) on complex conjugations, and its
restriction to \(\ker\chi\cap\ker\delta\) is irreducible. At \(A\),
\(W\) is upper triangular,
a positive power of its first diagonal character on inertia equals the
same power of \(\chi^e\), and that character differs from \(\chi\)
somewhere on the decomposition group. Let \(g\) be a newform of weight
\(2e+1\), of level prime to \(\ell\), with unit \(a_\ell(g)\).
Suppose there is a character \(\eta\) trivial on the subgroup fixing
\(\mu_\ell\) pointwise such that \(g\) is attached (via \(\iota\))
to \(W\otimes\chi^{-e}\delta^{-1}\eta\), and
\(W(s)_{22}\chi(s)^e\delta(s)^{-1}\eta(s)=1\) on inertia at \(A\).
There exist a common coefficient ring \(O\) for \(W\), an \(O\)-integral
continuous cocycle \(y\), and a finite set \(S'\) with the following properties.
On inertia away from \(\ell\), \(y\) is locally a coboundary.
There is no scalar \(x\) with \(y(s)_2=(W(s)_{22}-1)x\) throughout
the decomposition group of \(A\).
For every \(n\ge1,\ w\notin S',\ \ell^n\mid Nw-1\), and every admitted
surjective character to \(\mathbb Z/\ell^n\) trivial on the subgroup
fixing \(\mu_{Nw}\) pointwise, the same \(y\) satisfies the tame norm relation.

P028.statement:
Let \(O\) be a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field, \(A\)
an algebra graded by an abelian group, \(x:A\to O\) a point vanishing on
\(A_j\), and \(F_i\in A_j\). Fix \(0\ne c\in O\). Suppose an
additive injection \(D:M\to\operatorname{Hom}_O(A,O/(c))\) kills all
\(F_i\) at every value. Suppose each \(D(\mu)\) is the reduction of an
\(O\)-valued point derivation of weight \(j\) at \(x\). With the
saturated lattice as above,
\[
 \operatorname{length}_O M \le
 \operatorname{length}_O(L_j/\langle\overline F_i\rangle).
\]

P029.statement:
Assume the automorphic hypotheses \(H'\) and the CM level and
Satake--Frobenius correspondence \(\mathrm{LevelKNAlt}\).
For each CM field \(K\) and \(n\ge2\) there exist \(c,A\in\mathbb N\).
Let \(m_1>\cdots>m_n\) satisfy \(m_i+m_{n+1-i}=1-n\)
and \(|m_i|\le H\). Given \(M\ge1\) and \(w\mid p\) with \(p\) prime,
\(p\nmid M\operatorname{disc}(K)\), there are eigenvalue data \(D\)
at \(Nw\) of weight \(m\) and purity \(1-n\), with
\[
 |D.S|\le c[M(H+1)]^A .
\]
For every odd prime \(\ell\ne p\), closure and coefficient comparison
\(\iota\), these same data classify the admitted
\(\mathrm{AdmKNAlt}(\iota,M,m)\) representations of \(G_K\) at \(w\).

P030.statement:
Assume \(H'\), the level and Satake--Frobenius correspondence for
imaginary quadratic fields, and preservation of admissibility whenever
quadratic restriction is irreducible. For each \(n\ge2\) there exist
\(c,A\in\mathbb N\). For all \(m_1>\cdots>m_n\),
\(m_i+m_{n+1-i}=w_0\in\mathbb Z\), \(|m_i|\le H\), \(M\ge1\),
and \(p\nmid M\) prime, the rational place above \(p\) admits data
\(D\) of weight \(m\), purity \(w_0\), and \(|D.S|\le c[M(H+1)]^A\).
These data classify \(\mathrm{AdmRNAlt}(\iota,M,m,w_0)\) representations
of \(G_{\mathbb Q}\) at this place for every odd \(\ell\ne p\), closure
and \(\iota\).

P031.statement:
Let \(\ell\) be prime and let \(L_0\) contain a primitive \(\ell\)-th
root if \(\ell\) is odd, or a primitive fourth root if \(\ell=2\).
Write \(c_0\) for the largest \(c\) such that \(L_0\) contains a
primitive \(\ell^c\)-th root. There exists \(\gamma\in G_{L_0}\) whose
cyclotomic image topologically generates the image and satisfies
\(v_\ell(\chi(\gamma)-1)=c_0\). The base contains a primitive
\(\ell^{c_0}\)-th root. For every \(E\ge1\), every \(m\ge0\), and
every degree-\(\ell^m\) cyclotomic layer \(L_m/L_0\),
\[
 \operatorname{shaInv}(L_m,\ell,E)=
 \operatorname{length}_{\mathbb Z_\ell}
 \operatorname{coker}\bigl(x_{\mathrm{Tw}}(E,\gamma)^{\ell^m}-1\bigr).
\]
Here \(x_{\mathrm{Tw}}\) is the twisted action on the dual of the
infinite-layer character module with the specified local conditions.

P032.statement:
Assume functoriality and the boundary identities for chains and prisms,
the prism composition law, the specified basic bar cycle and its
coefficient relation, the interpolation distribution, and the Steinitz
transport hypothesis. In any layer as above take \(E=e+1\), \(e\ge0\),
\(m=2E+1<\ell^c\), and \(a=\kappa^E\). For any \(\alpha\in F^\times\)
satisfying the difference condition there are \(N\), a degree-\(m\)
bar cycle \(y\) on \(\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathcal O_L)\) over
\(\mathbb Z/q\), and \(0\ne b\in\mathcal O_F\) such that the following
holds. For every reduction \(r:\mathcal O_F\to k\) to a finite field
which is onto on \(\mathcal O_L\) and has \(r(b)\ne0\), for every
character \(v:k^\times\to\mathbb Z/q\), and for every additive
evaluating family \(\theta\) satisfying the scalar law for \(r(\zeta)\),
there is a residue \(u\in k^\times\) of \(N_a(\alpha)\) for which
\[
 \theta\bigl(\operatorname{red}_r y\bigr)=
 \prod_{\substack{0\le j<m\\j\ne E}}(a-\kappa^j)\,v(u)
 \quad\text{in }\mathbb Z/q.
\]

P033.statement:
Assume the chain, prism, prism composition and basic-cycle identities,
the transfer of scalar functionals and the scalar cocycle formula.
For any finite field \(k\), positive integer \(q\), \(e\ge0\),
primitive \(q\)-th root \(\zeta\in k^\times\), and character
\(v:k^\times\to\mathbb Z/q\), there is an additive evaluating
family \(\theta\) of degree \(2e+3\). For every finite \(k\)-vector
space \(V\), every \(x\in\mathbb N\), and \(g\in\mathrm{GL}(V)\),
\[
 \theta_V\!\left(P_g((j\mapsto\zeta^{xj}I_V)_*z)\right)
 = x^{e+1}v(\det g).
\]
Here \(P_g\) is the conjugation prism, and \(z\) is the specified
degree-\(2e+2\) cyclic bar cycle.

P034.statement:
Let \(L\) be totally complex, \(k\ge0\) even, \(q=k+1<r_2(L)\), and
\(n\ge2q+4\). Fix any integer \(t>0\). Starting with \(z_0(x)=x\)
in \(H_q(G_n,\mathbb Z)\), define
\[
 z_{j+1}(x)=(\operatorname{diag}_t)_*z_j(x)
                 -t^{j+2}\operatorname{stab}_*z_j(x),
\]
where block repetition and stabilization both land in rank \(t^{j+1}n\).
The integral span of all \(z_k(x)\) has rank at most \(r_2(L)\).

P035.statement:
For a totally complex field \(L\) and \(n'\ge n\ge 2m+4\), the torsion
in \(H_m(G_{n'},\mathbb Z)\) is finite, of order
\(\lvert H_m(G_n,\mathbb Z)_{\rm tors}\rvert\).

P036.statement:
Take a layer \(F/L\) with \(L\) totally complex, \(E\ge1\),
\(a=\kappa^E\), and \(b,B\in\mathbb N\). Suppose every finite family
of elements of \(F^\times\) satisfying the divisor difference condition,
with pairwise distinct classes of \(N_a(\alpha)^{\ell^b}\) modulo
\(q\)-th powers, has size at most \(B\). Let \(\mathcal H_q\) consist
of the functions on the prime ideals of \(F\) with values in
\(\mathbb Z/q\) that kill principal divisors and satisfy
\(\phi(\gamma^{-1}P)=a\phi(P)\). Writing \(v=v_\ell(E)\) and
\(g=2[L:\mathbb Q]+\lfloor\log_2 h_L\rfloor+2\), we have
\[
 \mathcal H_q\text{ finite},\qquad
 |\mathcal H_q|q^{r_2(L)}
       \le B\,\ell^{(b+v)g+c+v}.
\]

P037.statement:
Let \(L\) be totally complex and \(\ell\) prime. Suppose \(\ell^c\)
is the largest \(\ell\)-power order of a root of unity in \(L\),
\(c\ge1\) and \(c\ge2\) at \(\ell=2\). Fix \(E\ge1\). If for every
allowed layer \(F/L\) the preceding character group, defined with
\(a=(1+\ell^c)^E\), is finite of order at most \(B\), then there
exists \(s\in\mathbb N\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{shaInv}(L,\ell,E)=s,\qquad \ell^s\le B .
\]

P038.statement:
For every totally complex number field \(L\) and \(N,m\ge0\), let
\(d=[L:\mathbb Q]N\), \(s=3^{dN}\), and \(A=\mathrm{orbBound}(L,N,m)\),
the uniform face-orbit bound of the integral Hermitian complex through
degree \(m\). Then \(T=H_m(G_N,\mathbb Z)_{\rm tors}\) is finite with
\[
                    |T|\le(m+2)^A s^{m A s^m}.
\]

P039.statement:
There exists \(C\in\mathbb R\) such that for every totally complex \(L\),
\(e\ge1,\ 1\le N\le4e+6,\ 0\le m\le2e+1\), putting
\(n=[L:\mathbb Q]\) and \(D=|\operatorname{disc} L|\), the full torsion
\(T\) in \(H_m(G_N,\mathbb Z)\) is finite and
\[
          \log |T|\le \exp\!\left((2en)^C\log(2D)\right).
\]
