P040.statement:
Let \(F\) be a number field and \(\ell\) a prime such that \(\ell\ne2\)
or \(F\) has no real place. Assume finite-coefficient Poitou--Tate
duality, local finiteness and local Tate duality. For every allowed
set of local data \(D\) and every \(e\in\mathbb Z\), with
\(A_e=(\mathbb Q_\ell/\mathbb Z_\ell)(-e)\),
\[
 \operatorname{length}H^2(G_{F,S},\mathbb Z_\ell(e+1))
      +\nu_{\rm Gal}(\ell,F,|e|)
   =\operatorname{length}\Sha^1(D,A_e)
      +\sum_{w\in D.S}\operatorname{length}H^0(F_w,A_e).
\]
All lengths are extended \(\mathbb Z_\ell\)-lengths;
\(\Sha^1\) is the kernel of the specified localization.

P041.statement:
Assume that at \(\pi\) the family is the integral block sum of \(\rho_\pi\) and the specified characters, that all coefficient functions of \(\det(1-zr(g))\) belong to \(T\), and that the residual values of \(\rho_\pi\) span the whole matrix algebra. Give the orthogonal idempotents \(e_B,e_1\) and the element \(g_0\) with a corner perturbation \(s\) satisfying the prescribed evaluation and distinct-root conditions. There exists an ordered cover \(p:X'\to X\) with point \(\pi'\), scalar algebra \(T'\), matrix algebra \(R'\), block evaluations, and the prescribed ring and character data, for which
\[
 v_{\rm cc}(p(\pi'))=\operatorname{length}_O(O/\mathfrak c_\pi).
\]
The same \(R'\) is left Noetherian, its evaluations respect the \(T'\)-action, and its specialized block actions commute with \(O\) and respect both scalar towers. Its scalar cover has a spanning family independent on every fibre. Determinants of all matrix arrays over \(R'\) are values of functions in \(T'\), the distinguished specialization is block triangular and surjects onto each diagonal block, and the two rank-one operators satisfy the stipulated evaluated character and scalar identities. For each of the specified additive topologies on \(K,R'\) with the requisite continuous scalar actions and multiplication on \(R'\), every admissible system of rows and columns satisfies the universal length estimate. Specifically, write \(L\) for the congruence length, \(b'_w\) for the row quotient length, \(h_w\) for the local invariant loss, \(j_w\) for the column dimension and \(m_w\) for the column lift exponent. For \(d=v_O(\delta_O)\), scalar-block inputs \(s,\mathrm{Sha}_k\) in \(O\)-length units, invariant bound \(H_0\), and the auxiliary roots \(\zeta_w\), it gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 L\le{}&\sum_{w\in R}b'_w+\sum_{w\in C}\{a m_w+j_w(a m_w+d)+2d+h_w\}
       +s+\sum_{0<k<t}\mathrm{Sha}_k+a v_\ell(h_E)\\
 &+ta c_B\sum_{w\in R}([E_w:\mathbf Q_\ell]+2)
     +4(r+t)(|C|+1)d+t|C|H_0+t\sum_{w\in Q}v_O(\zeta_w-1).
\end{aligned}
\]
The same data give \(d=a\sum_{0<k<t}(s_0+v_\ell(k))\le a(t s_0+v_\ell(t!))\). The universal estimate assumes the off-\(Z\) condition, finite-class row images, column lifts, dimensions, global and local cohomological bounds, and character restrictions specified in the display.

P042.statement:
Let \(O\to O'\) be a finite free extension of coefficient DVRs with \(v_{O'}(x)=e v_O(x)\). Use two evaluated splitting algebras attached to compatible matrix data satisfying the distinct-eigenvalue corner hypothesis, their defining identities, Noetherianity and the prescribed scalar actions. If \(M\) over the first matrix algebra \(R\) has \(g\) specified generators, there is an \(R'\)-module \(M'\) on \(g\) generators such that for every \(Z\subseteq X\), nonzero evaluation Hom at every point above \(X\setminus Z\) downstairs implies the corresponding nonvanishing upstairs. For every distinguished block \(k\),
\[
 \operatorname{length}_{O'}\operatorname{Hom}_{R'}(M',V'_k)
   = e\,\operatorname{length}_{O}\operatorname{Hom}_{R}(M,V_k).
\]
Lengths are extended natural numbers, and the \(V_k\) are the specialized torsion coefficient blocks.

P043.statement:
Work on the normalized family \(r_N\) with its ring record and evaluation, topology, scalar and rank identifications. Assume G2 (local gain bound and crystalline twist), G4 (unramified away from the specified sets), G5 (inertia polynomial relations), tame generators, semisimple decomposition, Fontaine conditions above \(\ell\), local Tate \(H^1\) finiteness, and local coefficient compatibility. Assume goodness of the self coefficient extension, the specified auxiliary character powers, and \(TB(c_B)\) for \(r_N\). On these same data the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Block zero satisfies the fixed \(\rho\)-block conditions for the determinant presentation.
\item For \(c\ge1\), each admissible projected row cocycle is finite after multiplication by \(\ell^{c_B}\); the colength of the finite condition in its locally constant \(\ell^{c_B}\)-division part is at most \(ac_B([E_w:\mathbf Q_\ell]+1)\).
\item All higher character blocks \(c\ge2\) satisfy their character local conditions.
\item The first character block obeys its specified inertia and auxiliary-prime local conditions.
\item The row subquotient, orbit, matrix-lattice and target orbit continuity conditions hold simultaneously.
\end{enumerate}

P044.statement:
Assume G1--G6. The characteristic coefficients belong to \(T\) and the local gain and crystalline conditions hold. The constituents satisfy absolute irreducibility and distinctness with the prescribed residual characteristic polynomials and full residual span on block zero. Ramification away from the assigned sets is trivial, the assigned inertia elements satisfy their polynomial relations, and any parameter admitting the distinguished rational character line belongs to \(Z\). Assume tame inertia generators, the Bloch--Kato finite conditions and annihilator comparison, family continuity, semisimple decomposition, Fontaine conditions, local \(H^1\) finiteness and local coefficient compatibility. Assume condition 5.1 supplying an idempotent design at \(\pi\in Z\), and the unramified input for the decomposition. Let \(b_w,m_w,c_B\) satisfy the row colength, column lifting and \(TB\) hypotheses at the good coefficient extensions. If \(\ell\ne g_0,g_1,\ \pi\in Z\), the global \(s_\pi\) input is finite and the scalar lengths are finite for \(0<k<t\), then
\[
\begin{aligned}
v_{\rm cc}(\pi)\le{}&
 \sum_{w\in R\cup C}\operatorname{lenW}(w)+s_\pi+
 \sum_{0<k<t}\operatorname{shaLen}(k)+v_\ell(h_E)\\
 &+t c_B\sum_{w\in R}([E_w:\mathbf Q_\ell]+2)
 +4 n_V(|C|+1)v_\delta+t|C|h_0
 +t\sum_{w\in Q}\operatorname{lenUnit}(O/(\zeta_w-1)).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(R,C\) are the chosen rows and columns, \(n_V=r+t\), and \(\operatorname{lenW}\) is the normalized loss for the corresponding local datum.

P045.statement:
Fix a prime \(p\) and project systems \(X,Y,D\). Assume the integral exponential factorization for the formal group (\(\mathrm{RestGc}\)): in the indicated even cyclic coordinates, after adjoining a \((p^2-1)\)-st root of \(p\) and using the inverse Lubin--Tate parameter, the transformed exponential factors as the prescribed exponential times an integral series, with integral parameters. Assume each unweighted differential coefficient is zero or agrees with the corresponding coefficient of a local frame jet. If \(D\) admits \(X,Y\), then for any place \(v\), stage \(j<m\), \(1\le i\le r\), allowed integral parameter series \(U\), selected columns \(I\) and output monomial \(n\), the coefficient at \(n\) of the \(i\)-weighted differential of
\[
 \Theta_j\!\left(\exp(-\Phi_{j,v})\,U\right)
\]
satisfies the lower valuation bound \(g_v(j+1)\) in the comparison field \(Y\). Integrality of \(U\) here is in the chosen parameter coordinates.

P046.statement: Assume admission for the specified tied entries when the curve, series, character, local-law and comparison data at each stage are supplied, and existence of the indicated Lubin--Tate curve realization for each eligible inert prime. Fix a tied host, lattice system and kernel, comparison input \(I\), comparison hypotheses \(H\), labels and joint datum. At a place \(w\) of inert residue characteristic \(p\ge5\) outside the level primes, assume the host nonvanishing condition and \(p\nmid T_u\). Suppose \(\mu\) is used, the level-zero stabilizer condition holds, and \(2r_G\le k\). On the chain \(\operatorname{chainAt}(H,h_T)\) the semilinear comparisons satisfy the level-zero identification, kernel, rationality and terminal valuation conditions. The same chain admits a system at the specified place and levels, with its standard coordinates, uniformizer and ramification normalization, and \(d_G(0)=0,\ d_G(j)\le v_p(D_{\Gamma,u})\).

P047.statement: Assume the coefficient inequalities for orbits without the operator, medium inert primes, discriminant primes, and the remaining primes under the stabilizer-denominator identity. Assume the size and error definitions. Fix a word \(u\), a used tuple \(\mu\), a place \(w\) of residue characteristic \(p\ne T_u\) outside \(\{g_0,g_1\}\cup Q(\mu)\), and \(x\in S_{\rm ram}(u,w)\). The column of \(T\) at \(u,\mu,w,x\) has its prescribed lower bound \(\operatorname{lowS}(u,w)\).

P048.statement:
Take a base and pre-chart, an admissible column record \(I\) with its pinned frames and coefficients, its stage laws \(l\), later chart data and the level-zero lattice identification. Assume that the reference and twisted rows on this choice are integral. Choose the coefficient and tuple data with \(t_p.\xi=I.\xi\), and any divisor datum \(Y\). Under the stabilizer-denominator identity, for every word \(u\), used nonreference place tuple \(\mu\), integral point \(x\) of the twisted point lattice and \(F\) in the indicated ambient carrier and \(V_0(\mu)\), there exists \(y\in L_L\) such that its chosen complex image is the twisted period of the embedded \(x\) and the identified \(F\), and for every \(w\) with \(p_w\notin Q_Y(\mu)\),
\[
       y=0\quad\text{or}\quad v_w(y)\ \ge\ -e_w v_{p_w}(D_{\Gamma,u}).
\]

P049.statement:
Let \(K\) be a totally complex number field with its given star structure, \(V\) a finite-dimensional \(K\)-space with the compatible \(\mathcal O_K\)-action, \(b\) a basis and \(X_v\) invertible complex frames. For a \(K\)-independent family \(e_1,\ldots,e_j\), set \(B=\sum_i\mathcal O_K e_i\). Then
\[
 \operatorname{ht}_{b,X}(B)=\prod_{v\mid\infty}\operatorname{Re}\det\operatorname{Gram}_{v,b,X}(e).
\]
For every finitely generated \(\mathcal O_K\)-module \(L\supset B\) of \(K\)-rank \(j\), one has \(\operatorname{ht}_{b,X}(L)[L:B]=\operatorname{ht}_{b,X}(B)\).

P050.statement:
Let \(K\) be any number field with the given star structure, \(V\) a finite-dimensional \(K\)-space with compatible \(\mathcal O_K\)-action, \(b\) a basis, and \(X_v\) invertible complex frames at all infinite places. For a finitely generated \(\mathcal O_K\)-submodule \(L\), the realization is injective on \(L\), its image is discrete, and
\[
 \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}\rho_X L=[K:\mathbf Q]\,\operatorname{rank}_K L,
 \qquad \operatorname{ht}_{b,X}(L)>0 .
\]

P051.statement:
For a totally complex number field \(K\) with star structure, take \(D>0\), invertible complex frames \(X_v\), and a full \(\mathcal O_K\)-lattice \(R\subset K^D\). In the dual of the standard basis and the dual frame,
\[
 \mu(R^\vee)=\frac{\operatorname{lcv}(X,R)}{D}
 =\frac{2\log\operatorname{ht}_{X}(R)}{[K:\mathbf Q]D}.
\]

P052.statement:
For a totally complex number field \(K\) in the same finite-dimensional setting, let \(A\) be finitely generated over \(\mathcal O_K\) and span \(V\) over \(K\). Put
\[
 A^\vee=\{\phi\in V^*: \phi(A)\subseteq\mathcal O_K\}.
\]
For any basis \(b\) and invertible frames \(X_v\),
\(\operatorname{ht}_{b^\vee,X^\vee}(A^\vee)\operatorname{ht}_{b,X}(A)=1\).

P117.statement:
For tied data, let $i\le m$, let $\beta$ be a chart and let $x,x'$ be finite
adelic unitary points at $i$. For every rational $\gamma$ satisfying
$\gamma^*J_i\gamma=J_i$, if $x'=\mathrm{rat}(\gamma)x$ and
$p\sim_{i,\beta}x$, there exists $p'$ with $p'\sim_{i,\beta}x'$.

P118.statement:
For tied data, $i\le m$ and $\gamma\in\mathrm{GL}_{N_i}(E_D)$ with
$\gamma^*J_i\gamma=J_i$, there exists a linear automorphism $g$ of
$E_X^{N_i}$ preserving its standard Hermitian form for which
\[
                           s(g)= C_i\gamma C_i^{-1}.
\]

P119.statement:
For tied data at $j\le m$, let $\kappa$ belong to the level subgroup of a
chart $\beta$ and let $x_1=x\kappa$. For every pair of points
$p\sim_{j,\beta}x$ and $p_1\sim_{j,\beta}x_1$ one has
\[
 N(p_1)=N(p),\qquad f_{p_1,P}(w)=f_{p,P}(w)\quad\text{for every }P,w
\]
in the domain of the decoration.

P120.statement:
For tied data, fix a chart $\beta$ at $i\le m$ and a point
$p\sim_{i,\beta}x$. If $\kappa$ belongs to the chart level and the finite
adelic unitary point $x'$ satisfies $x'=x\kappa$, there exists a
point $p'$ in the same chart with $p'\sim_{i,\beta}x'$.

P121.statement:
For tied data, fix a chart $\beta'$ at $m_2+1$, a level element $\kappa'$
and a family of integral local automorphisms $u_P$ at $P\in B$.
Assume $\mathrm{InFrame}_P(\kappa',u_P^{-1})$ for all $P$.
For every $P$ and $y\in E_X^{N_{m_2+1}}$ one has
\[
                 u_Py\equiv_P y_{0,P}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                      y\equiv_P y_{0,P}.
\]

P122.statement:
For tied data at $m_2+1$, take $\beta',\kappa'$ and integral
automorphisms $u_P$ as in \nodeid{P121}. Assume
$\mathrm{InFrame}_P(\kappa',u_P^{-1})$ for every $P\in B$. There exist
$c_P\in K^\times$ such that
\[
 \mathrm{LevAt}_P(u_P,c_P)\quad(P\in B),\qquad
       \sigma_0\!\left(\prod_{P\in B}c_P\right)=\chi_{\beta'}(\kappa').
\]

P123.statement:
For tied data satisfying $\mathrm{MuLaw}$ take a chart $\beta'$ at
$m_2+1$, a level element $\kappa'$ there, and integral $u_P$ with
$\mathrm{InFrame}_P(\kappa',u_P^{-1})$ for every $P\in B$. Then
\[
    \mu_{m_2+1}(\det\kappa')=
       \sigma_0\!\left(\prod_{P\in B}\rho_{S,m_2,P}(\det u_P)\right).
\]

P124.statement:
Let $s$ identify the coefficient fields, let $d$ be a valid decoration
on an $n$-dimensional column space with its given function and frame prime
sets, and fix a frame prime $w$. Suppose $q_w\notin\mathfrak p_w^2$ in
the ring of integers. Let $g$ be a standard unitary automorphism of the
column space. If $y$ is an invertible finite adelic matrix of size $n$
and $\mathrm{Near}_{s(w),1}(y,s(\mathrm{liftFr}_w(d)))$, then
\[
 \mathrm{Near}_{s(w),1}
 \bigl(\mathrm{rat}(s(g))\,y,\,
              s(\mathrm{liftFr}_w((g,1)\cdot d))\bigr).
\]

P125.statement:
Let $s$ identify the coefficient fields, $g$ be an $E_X$-linear
automorphism of $E_X^n$ and $N$ any $\mathcal O_{E_X}$-submodule of
$E_X^n$. For the transported submodule $s_{\rm lat}(N)$ one has
\[
                 s_{\rm lat}\bigl(g(N)\bigr)=s(g)\bigl(s_{\rm lat}(N)\bigr).
\]
The action on the right is the matrix image of a submodule.

P126.statement:
For tied data satisfying $\mathrm{MuLaw}$ fix $j=m_2<m$, a chart
$\beta$ at $j$ and a level element $\kappa$. Suppose $g_P$ are rational
column automorphisms and $z_P\in K$ for $P\in B$, with both
$\mathrm{MidRel}_P(g_P,z_P)$ and $\mathrm{InFrame}_P(\kappa,g_P)$ at
every $P$. Then
\[
     \mu_{j+1}(\det\kappa)\,
       \sigma_0\!\left(\prod_{P\in B}\rho_{S,j,P}(\det g_P)\right)=1 .
\]

P127.statement:
For tied data, fix a stage index $i$, a column chart point $p$ there,
and finite adelic matrices $y_P,k_P$ for each $P\in B$. Suppose that
$\mathrm{Cong}_{s(P),0}(k_P)$ and $\mathrm{Cong}_{s(P),0}(k_P^{-1})$
both hold and that $\mathrm{Near}_{s(P),D_P}(y_P,s(F_P(p)))$ holds at
every $P$. A chart point $p'$ at $i$ then exists with
\[
 N(p')=N(p),\quad f_{p'}=f_p,\qquad
 \mathrm{Near}_{s(P),D_P}(y_Pk_P,s(F_P(p')))\quad(P\in B).
\]

P128.statement:
For tied data let $i=m_2+1\le m$, let $\beta'$ be a chart at $i$, let
$\kappa'$ lie in its level group and let $p'\sim_{i,\beta'}x'$.
If $x'_1=x'\kappa'$, there are a point $q'\sim_{i,\beta'}x'_1$ and
integral local automorphisms $u_P$, $P\in B$, such that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \phi_T(p,q';w)&=\phi_T(p,p';w)
               &&\text{for every source point $p$ at $m_2$ and every $w$},\\
 F_P(q')&=F_P(p')u_P^{-1},
 &\mathrm{InFrame}_P(\kappa',u_P^{-1})&\quad(P\in B).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here $\phi_T$ is evaluated on the decorations of the indicated two points.

P129.statement:
For tied data, let $i\le m$, let $\beta$ be a chart at $i$, and fix
$x_1=x\kappa$ with $\kappa$ in its chart level. Suppose
$p\sim_{i,\beta}x$ and $q$ is a chart point at this stage. Assume
$N(q)=N(p)$, $f_q=f_p$ and, for each $P\in B$, there is a prescribed
rational automorphism $k_P$ preserving the standard local lattice such
that
\[
       F_P(q)=F_P(p)k_P,\qquad \mathrm{InFrame}_P(\kappa,k_P).
\]
Then $q\sim_{i,\beta}x_1$.

P130.statement:
For tied data take a chart $\beta$ at $j=m_2<m$, a level element
$\kappa$, a chart point $p$ at $j$, rational column automorphisms $g_P$
and $z_P\in K$. Suppose that for every $P\in B$ one has
$\mathrm{MidRel}_P(g_P,z_P)$ and $\mathrm{InFrame}_P(\kappa,g_P)$.
Then there exist a chart point $q$, integral local automorphisms $k_P$,
and $c_P\in K^\times$ such that $N(q)=N(p)$, $f_q=f_p$, and at each
$P\in B$ one has all of
\[
\begin{gathered}
 F_P(q)=F_P(p)k_P^{-1},\qquad
 \mathrm{LevAt}_P(k_P,c_P),\qquad c_Pz_P=1,\\
 \rho_{S,j,P}(\det k_P^{-1})=\rho_{S,j,P}(\det g_P),\qquad
 \mathrm{InFrame}_P(\kappa,k_P^{-1}).
\end{gathered}
\]

P131.statement:
Let the number fields $F,E$, their algebra structure, and their space
data be given. Suppose $\det J$ is a unit in $E$, $c\in\mathrm{GL}_N(E)$,
$a\in\mathcal O_E$, and the invertible finite adelic matrix $x$ lies in
the unitary group of $J$. Let $L_b\subset E^N$ be a finitely generated
$\mathcal O_E$-submodule spanning $E^N$ with $L_b\subseteq L_b^\vee$.
For every finite prime $v$ of $F$ and every rational
$y\in\mathrm{latCo}(J,c,a,x,L_b)$,
\[
                \bigl((\mathrm{rat}(c)x)^{-1}y\bigr)_v
                           \in (L_b^\vee)^{\mathrm{int}}_v .
\]
Here $\mathrm{latCo}$ is the image under $c$ of the companion of the
adelically moved base lattice. The companion operation is given in
\nodeid{P139}.

P132.statement:
Let $s$ be a field identification satisfying its compatibility condition:
the prescribed archimedean embeddings commute with the field and index
maps after application of $\sigma_0$, and $s(\bar x)=\overline{s(x)}$.
For every $n$ and $G\in\mathrm{GL}_n(E_D)$ with $G^*G=I$, there is a
standard unitary automorphism $g$ of $E_X^n$ satisfying $s(g)=G$.

P133.statement:
For arbitrary such $s$, step level, $P,v,\iota$, let $d$ be a decoration
and $x$ any invertible finite adelic matrix of the appropriate rank.
Let $g$ be a rational linear automorphism of the column space and $h$
any element of the auxiliary frame group acting on $d$. Then
\[
 \mathrm{FunMoved}_{P,v,\iota}(x,d)
   \ \Longrightarrow\
 \mathrm{FunMoved}_{P,v,\iota}\bigl(\mathrm{rat}(s(g))x,\,
                                      \mathrm{act}(d,g,h)\bigr).
\]

P134.statement:
For tied data, fix a chart $\beta$ at $i\le m$, a represented point
$p\sim_{i,\beta}x$ and an element $\kappa$ of its level group. For every
$P\in B$ write $k=\mathrm{rat}(b_P)^{-1}\kappa\,\mathrm{rat}(b_P)$.
Then $\mathrm{Cong}_{s(P),0}(k)$ and $\mathrm{Cong}_{s(P),0}(k^{-1})$
both hold.

P135.statement:
For tied data, a chart $\beta$ at $m_2<m$ and $\kappa$ in its level
group, there exist rational column automorphisms $g_P$ and $z_P\in K$,
$P\in B$, such that
\[
 \mathrm{MidRel}_P(g_P,z_P),\quad
 \mathrm{InFrame}_P(\kappa,g_P)\quad(P\in B),\qquad
 \chi_\beta(\kappa)\,\sigma_0\!\left(\prod_{P\in B}z_P\right)=1 .
\]

P136.statement:
Fix the identification $s$, a step level at $i\le m$, a finite prime $v$
dividing $T$, a designated function prime $P$ and a residue map $\iota$
as above. For an invertible finite adelic matrix $y$, an element
$\kappa$ of this step level, and a decoration $d$,
\[
 \mathrm{FunMoved}_{P,v,\iota}(y,d)
          \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathrm{FunMoved}_{P,v,\iota}(y\kappa,d).
\]

P137.statement:
Over $E_D$, let $J$ be an $n$-by-$n$ matrix and
$C,\gamma\in\mathrm{GL}_n(E_D)$. Write $*$ for conjugate transpose
using the given conjugation of the coefficient field. If
$C^*C=J$ and $\gamma^*J\gamma=J$, then $H=C\gamma C^{-1}$ satisfies
$H^*H=I$.

P138.statement:
Let $E$ be a number field with the indicated involution, $P$ a finite
prime of $E$, $q=N(P)$, $d\ge1$ an integer and $k$ an $E$-linear
automorphism of $E^n$. Write $\Lambda_P=(\mathcal O_E)_P^n$. Suppose
for every standard basis vector $e_s$ and coordinate $\ell$ that
\[
                   q^{-d}(ke_s-e_s)_\ell\in(\mathcal O_E)_P .
\]
Then $k$ stabilizes $\Lambda_P$ and its induced automorphism belongs to
the prescribed depth-$d$ principal congruence subgroup, that is,
$q^{-d}(kw-w)\in\Lambda_P$ for every $w\in\Lambda_P$.

P139.statement:
For tied data in a chart $\beta$ at $i\le m$ let $p\sim_{i,\beta}x$.
Let $L_b$ be the base lattice of this chart's level and let
$L_b^\vee$ be its dual for $J_i$. At each $P\in B$ there is an equality
of submodules in the rational ambient space
\[
 b_P\bigl((\mathcal O_{E_D})_{s(P)}^{N_i}\bigr)
       =\bigl(L_b+(a)\langle L_b^\vee\rangle_{\mathcal O_{E_D}}
          \bigr)_{s(P)} .
\]
This is a local lattice calculation using the chart-point conditions.
The subscript on the right denotes localization at the transported prime.
The companion is \nolinkurl{Formalism.L2.PairingIndexBounds.F.compan},
\nolinkurl{IsOrthCo.lean:33--34}.

P140.statement:
For all tied data, every chart $\beta$ at $m_2+1$, every $P\in B$ and
every coordinate $\ell$ of its base coset representative $y_0(\beta,P)$,
\[
 q_P^{e_P}\,y_0(\beta,P)_\ell\in(\mathcal O_{E_X})_P,\qquad
       e_P=\begin{cases}1&P\in v_G,\\M&P\notin v_G.\end{cases}
\]

B01.statement:
Assume the following stable-range lift. Fix good CM base data, $n\ge1$ and
the Hermitian space with matrix $1$ and signature $(n,0)$. There is $d_0$
such that for every $d\ge d_0$, skew space with matrix $\delta I_d$ and
signature as in the lift, and splitting Hecke characters $\chi_X,\chi_W$
with the prescribed quadratic restrictions and infinity exponents $m_X,m_W$,
each automorphic $U$ with weights $\lambda_v$ satisfying
$d+m_W(v)\le2\lambda_v(k)$ for every $v,k$ has a target $U'$ satisfying
the specified theta-lift relation. Under this assumption every regular
algebraic polarised cuspidal pair as above admits $r$, $w_\pi\in\mathbb Z$
and Hodge--Tate multisets $H_\tau$ satisfying the whole row below.

The representation $r$ is continuous and semisimple. The multiset
$H_\tau$ is $(a-1)/2$ minus the infinitesimal character at $\iota\tau$,
and $H_{\tau c}=w_\pi-H_\tau$. At each $w\nmid\ell$ and for
\emph{every} parameter map satisfying the local laws in
\hyperref[sub:B04]{B04}, compare $\mathrm{WD}(r|_{E_w})$ with the parameter
of the algebraically normalised local component. They have equal dimension.
A toral target with zero monodromy gives equality; under the source's
large-residue-characteristic, tame and squarefree conditions, a target with
zero monodromy gives zero monodromy and equality of characteristic polynomials
on degree-zero Weil elements. For every tied local comparison datum and
inducing bridge above $\ell$, a spherical component gives crystallinity,
the de Rham property and jumps $H_\tau$ at every induced embedding.
A zero-monodromy toral target, or a zero-monodromy target satisfying the
three tame-range conditions, gives the de Rham and potentially semistable
properties, the same jumps and the preceding Weil--Deligne comparison.

B03.statement:
Suppose the geometric existence assertion in \hyperref[sub:B02]{B02} and
the stable-range theta lift specified in \hyperref[sub:B01]{B01} both
hold. For every CM field, closure, prime $\ell$, coefficient isomorphism,
rank $a\ge1$ and regular algebraic polarised cuspidal pair, there is a
single triple $(r,w_\pi,(H_\tau)_\tau)$ satisfying all the global,
away-from-$\ell$ and above-$\ell$ clauses of \hyperref[sub:B01]{B01}.

B04.statement:
For any number field $E$, algebraic closure $\Omega$, valuation subring
of $\Omega$ over a finite place $w$, and resulting local field $E_w$,
there exist an Artin map and a parameter map from irreducible smooth
$\mathrm{GL}_n(E_w)$-classes of all ranks to Weil--Deligne parameters.
The map preserves dimension, agrees with reciprocity in rank one,
takes Langlands quotients of multisegments to the corresponding segment
sums, takes cuspidals to irreducible parameters and commutes with real
norm twists. The absolute value of its determinant recovers that of the
central character. For classes with good cuspidal support it respects
character twists, the full central character and duality, is injective
against arbitrary classes, and yields a tame parameter in the presence
of principal-congruence fixed vectors. Here each good cuspidal constituent
has rank one or, over a field isomorphic to $\mathbb Q_p$, is a twist of
a representation with such fixed vectors.

The last law prescribes a tame type. Over the indicated unramified residue
extension of degree $n$, let $\vartheta$ be a regular residue-field character
and let the inflated cuspidal type have the prescribed elliptic character
values. The parameter has zero monodromy. At an inertia element whose Artin
image reduces to $z$, its inertial characteristic polynomial is
$\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(X-\vartheta(z^{p^j}))$, with restriction to the given
base as in the local law.

T11.statement:
Assume the doubling Eisenstein input (right-half-plane summation and
meromorphic continuation with moderate local regularizations) and the
standard value statement T12. Over every admissible number-field pair and
automorphism, each admissible triple of Weil models has real and finite
matching data. The unprimed integrals converge on Schwartz vectors. On
the prescribed primed test space the theta kernel has rapid decay in one
variable with polynomial growth in the other, the integral converges and is
moderate. For each matching choice some primed test integral is nonzero
and there is a unique nonzero $c$ with $I(\Phi)=c I'(\Phi')$ for every
matched pair, as functions on the common group. At good places the kernels
of both finite quotient maps are the augmentation spaces on the test vectors,
the primed local test spaces surject onto the quotient, and functionals
killing the primed augmentation factor on test vectors through the quotient.
The primed global test space is stable under the primed action.

There are two independent uniform triples of signs for the tower relations.
For two matching models with comparison constants $c,c_1$ and an adapted
pair of planes, $C\ne0$ depends on the geometry and real maps. Write
$F(z)$ for the signed \nolinkurl{stepFac} of the two plane ideals and $L(z)$
for the source's \nolinkurl{charL} of $\nu,S_0$. In the $\beta$ step,
with ranks $(a,b+2)$ and $(a,b)$ and $h=\lfloor (a-b-2)_+/2\rfloor$,
one has $cL(h+1)=u c_1$ for some $u$ such that $uCF(-h)=1$.
In the $\alpha$ step with ranks $(b+2,a')$ and $(b,a')$ and
$h=\lfloor(b+2-a')_+/2\rfloor$, one has $c=CF(1-h)L(h)c_1$.

T12.statement:
For every good number-field base $(F,E,\sigma,B)$ and spaces $A,Y$ of
ranks $m,n\ge1$, take opposite Hermitian and skew-Hermitian signs, with the
signature $(r,s)$ of $A$ satisfying $\min(r,s)=0$. Fix a Hecke character
restricting as $\eta^m$, any finite-index Darboux doubling model satisfying
its splitting, rationality, invariance and theta-summation rules, a frame,
standard compact $K$ and height $a$. For every Haar measure with a
fundamental domain $D$, every Schwartz vector $\Phi$ with finite-dimensional
$K$-span, and every $x$, the flat-section Eisenstein sum for
$g\mapsto l(\omega(g)\Phi)$ has a meromorphic continuation from a right
half-plane, holomorphic at $s_0=(m-n)/2$, with value
\[
 E(x,s_0)=
 \begin{cases}1,&n<m,\\2,&m\le n\end{cases}
 \ \mathop{\mathrm{avg}}_{g\in D}\,
       \theta_F\bigl(\omega(x)S(g)\Phi\bigr).
\]
The average is taken with respect to the specified Haar measure.

T17.statement:
Take finite blocks of homogeneous coordinates $y$ in a field $\Omega$,
their vanishing ideal $P$, a birational presentation of arithmetic dimension
$D+1$, and an intersection system $I$ satisfying its defining axioms.
Let $A$ be a conjugation-invariant Hermitian line, semipositive relative
to some $P_0\subseteq P$, nef on the fibres in its multidegree and nef on
the generic fibre in the specified sense. Then
\[
 I_P(A^{D+1})\le
 \mathrm{arVolP}\bigl(\text{small sections for }P,y,A,\,
       \mathrm{chartLat}(y,\deg A),1,D\bigr).
\]

T18.statement:
For each intersection system and finite multihomogeneous presentation as
above the following three statements hold.
(i) On an arithmetic variety of dimension $D+1$, relative semipositivity,
fibre nefness, conjugation invariance and nonnegative degree on every
arithmetic curve imply $I_P(A^{D+1})\ge0$.
(ii) For a birational characteristic-zero presentation with $D\ge1$,
small-generation data and conjugation invariance, the limsup of the
small-section count for \nolinkurl{chartLat}, divided in degree $n$ by
$n^{D+1}/(D+1)!$, is at most $I_P(A^{D+1})$.
(iii) For a birational presentation over a field with $D\ge1$, nonnegative
multidegree, relative semipositivity at $P_0\subseteq P$, bounded monomials
and conjugation invariance, the same limsup bound holds for
\nolinkurl{chartLatNm}.

T19.statement:
Given the open-literature record, for every characteristic-zero field $k$
and reduced separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, there is a sequence of
blowups $f:X'\to X$ with $X'$ smooth. Its restriction over the smooth
locus is an isomorphism. The reduced inverse image of the complement
is a simple normal crossings divisor. The formal wrapper uses a closed
resolution term independently of its record argument.

T20.statement:
Given the open-literature record, let $X/k$ be smooth of relative
dimension $d$, quasi-compact and separated over a characteristic-zero
field. Let $I$ be an ideal whose cosupport contains no irreducible
component of $X$, and $E$ a closed boundary that has simple normal
crossings at every point of $E$. There is a sequence of blowups in
smooth centres with normal crossings with the current boundary,
updating that boundary by total transform at every step. The resulting
$X'$ is smooth, $I\mathcal O_{X'}$ defines an effective Cartier divisor
with simple normal crossings reduced support, and $X'\to X$ is an
isomorphism off the cosupport of $I$. This wrapper also uses a closed term.

T21.statement:
Given the open-literature record, let $P$ have arithmetic dimension $n+2$
in a finite multihomogeneous coordinate ring, and let
$L_1,\ldots,L_n,A,B$ be smooth conjugation-invariant Hermitian lines.
Assume $B$ has zero multidegree and $s$ is a section of $A$ on $P$.
Write $J_Z(\omega;f)$ for the project's point integral on $Z$ with
potential list $\omega$ and integrand $f$, and $\omega_L$ for the
potentials of the $L_i$. With $b=\log h_B$ and $a=\log h_A$,
\[
 J_P((b,\omega_L);\log\|s\|_A)=
   \sum_{W\ \mathrm{horizontal~in~div}(s)}^{\mathrm{fin}}
       \mathrm{mult}_{W}(P+(s))J_W(\omega_L;b)
     -J_P((a,\omega_L);b).
\]

T22.statement:
Given the open-literature record, let $C$ be algebraically closed with a
nonnegative-real-valued valuation and let $R\to C$ identify $R$ as its
valuation ring. Every abelian scheme $A/R$ with a relatively ample
invertible sheaf admits group homomorphisms $i:A\to P$, $r:P\to A$
with $r i=1_A$. The scheme $P/R$ is abelian, smooth of a specified
relative dimension and carries a rigidified symmetric relatively ample
invertible sheaf with trivial polarization kernel.

T23.statement:
Given the open-literature record, let $y$ be a birational
multihomogeneous presentation in a characteristic-zero field with
arithmetic variety $P$ of dimension $D+1$, and let the integral
multidegree $a$ be nef on the generic fibre. Put
$V_n=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}(\mathrm{chartLatNm}(y,a,n))$.
Each $V_n$ is finite-dimensional and
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{D!\,\dim_{\mathbb Q}V_n}{n^D}
       =\mathrm{genDeg}(P,D,a).
\]

T24.statement:
Given the open-literature record, fix a prime $p$, an algebraically closed
characteristic-zero valued field $C$ with $v(p)<1$, a valuation ring $O$
which is a $\mathbb Z_p$-algebra complete for $(p)$, and a $p$-divisible
group $G/O$. Choose $\zeta_0=1$, $\zeta_{n+1}^p=\zeta_n$, $\zeta_1\ne1$.
Let $B$ pair the two $O$-extended Tate modules of $G,G^\vee$ bilinearly.
On pure Tate elements require the Weil pairing to be
$a\mu_{\mathrm{Tate}}(\zeta)$ and $B(1\otimes x,1\otimes\chi)=a$ in $O$
for some $a\in\mathbb Z_p$, for every $x,\chi$.
Then $\mathrm{HT}_G(x)=0$ if and only if $B(x,y)=0$ for all
$y\in\ker(\mathrm{dlog}_G)$ in the dual-side module.

W02.statement:
Let $E/E^+$ be CM, unramified at every finite prime, $n\ge1$, and $\pi$
an automorphic representation of the specified definite unitary group.
There is a partition $n=\sum_i N_i$ with positive parts and a discrete
$\mathrm{GL}_{N_i}(\mathbb A_E)$ constituent $V_i$ for each part.
Each is an ascending constituent built from a normalized unitary
conjugate-self-dual cusp form. There are local components $\sigma_{iw}$
and infinitesimal characters $m_{i\tau}$ of $V_i$. At each finite $w$
there is an irreducible subquotient $P_w$ of the local induced product
of the $\sigma_{iw}$. It is spherical when $\pi$ is unramified there,
has the base-changed Satake multiset for each inert unramified datum,
and realizes the unitary local component at split places. At each
embedding $\tau$, the sum of the $m_{i\tau}$ equals the infinitesimal
character attached to each weight of $\pi$ at $\tau$.

W04.statement:
Let $E/E^+$ be CM and unramified at finite places. Fix a prime $p$ and a
finite set $S$ of finite places of $E^+$ containing those above $p$,
all split in $E$. Let $2\le n\le4$ and let $\pi$ be a regular algebraic
cuspidal representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb A_E)$ with
$\pi^\vee\simeq\pi^c$ and Satake parameters at all places above the
complement of $S$. There exists an automorphic representation $\sigma$ of
the specified unitary group, unramified at every nonsplit finite place.
At all but finitely many split $w$ the component of $\sigma$, read
on $\mathrm{GL}_n(E_w)$, has the same Satake multiset as $\pi_w$.

W05.statement:
Assume the rank-$n$ literature record. There is a real $C_K$ such that,
for every prime $\ell$, totally complex field $L$ containing a primitive
$\ell$th root (a fourth root for $\ell=2$), algebraic closure and
local data, and $e\ge1$, the group $H^2(G_{L,\ell},\mathbb Z_\ell(e+1))$
is finite. With $r=[L:\mathbb Q]$ and $D=|\operatorname{disc}(L)|$,
\[
 \log\# H^2(G_{L,\ell},\mathbb Z_\ell(e+1))
 \le \exp\big((2er)^{C_K}\log(2D)\big).
\]

W07.statement:
Assume $H'$. Fix an odd prime $\ell$, $e\ge1$ with $\ell-1\nmid2e$,
an imaginary quadratic field $K$, an even positive level $N$ coprime to
$D_K=|\operatorname{disc}K|$, with $\ell\nmid D_K h_K$, and an
algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbb Q$ containing $K$. Write
$\kappa$ for the cyclotomic character and $\theta$ for the quadratic
character cutting out $K$. Take $\psi$ and $W:G_{\mathbb Q}\to
\mathrm{GL}_2(\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell)$ satisfying the source
conditions \code{Used}. Explicitly, $\psi$ factors through level $N$,
has prime-to-$\ell$ order, has square one on inertia at $\ell$, and
$\kappa^e\psi$ is even. The representation $W$ has level datum
$(ND_K;e,-e)$, the ordinary polynomial condition for $(e,-e)$, and
determinant $\theta$. On inertia at $\ell$ its trace is
$a+a^{-1}$ for $a=\kappa^e\psi$. Globally the residual trace is
$\theta a+a^{-1}$. At a chosen place above $\ell$, inertia lies
in $\ker\theta$ and the prescribed flag characters restrict to
$\kappa^{\pm e}\chi$ for a single character through level $\ell$.
The restriction to $G_{K(\mu_{\ell^\infty})}$ is irreducible.
Suppose a weight-$2e+1$ newform realizes $W\otimes\kappa^{-e}$
via $\iota$, and on every quadratic CM restriction on which $W$ is
irreducible it has the witness \code{WitA}: local unlinked flags
above $\ell$ become power-unlinked, and each attached regular
algebraic cusp form has a common real parameter for its local window
away from $\ell$ and at the power-unlinked places. For both $W$ and $W\otimes\theta$, every cocycle satisfying the
Bloch--Kato local conditions is a coboundary.

W11.statement:
Let $\ell$ be any prime and $K/\mathbb Q$ a finite abelian extension
containing $\mu_\ell$ for odd $\ell$, or $\mu_4$ for $\ell=2$. There
is an integer $r\ge0$ such that for every $n\ge0$ and every model
$K'$ of $K(\mu_{\ell^n})$ over $K$,
\[
    \big|\operatorname{Cl}(K')/\operatorname{Cl}(K')^\ell\big|\le\ell^r .
\]

P017.statement:
Let $\mathcal L$ be a level. For all $e_D,e_L\in\mathbb R$, $\varepsilon>0$, and every family $F$ at $\varepsilon$ satisfying \code{EFamC}$(\mathcal L,F)$, suppose there exist $K,c_{HH},e_K,C_L,x_0\in\mathbb R$ such that at every $x\ge x_0$ in $\mathrm{Win}(F)$ the condition \code{ChainTied}$(F;e_D,e_L,K,c_{HH},e_K,C_L;x)$ holds. Then some $x_1'$ satisfies
\[
 \mathcal G_{\mathcal L}(x)\le x^{1/2+(e_D+e_L+7)\varepsilon}
 \qquad(x\in\mathrm{Win}(F),\ x\ge x_1').
\]

P022.statement:
\par\noindent{\footnotesize \nolinkurl{landauWindow.lean:83}.}\par
Let $(g,\Phi,Z)$ be pole data, $0<\theta<1$ and $\delta>0$, and assume
$\mathrm{W}(g,\theta,\delta)$. Then $\operatorname{Re}\rho\le\theta$ for every $\rho\in Z$.

P023.statement:
\par\noindent{\footnotesize \nolinkurl{ZeroFreeOfRpowWindow.lean:11}, \nolinkurl{lemmaL.lean:13}, \nolinkurl{WindowHypOfRpow.lean:27}, \nolinkurl{WindowHypUOfWindowHyp.lean:29}.}\par
Let $F$ be a character family, $0<\theta<1$, $\delta>0$ and $C\in\mathbb R$. Assume that for every
$Y_0$ there is $Y\ge Y_0$ such that
\[
\mathcal G_F(y)\le C\,y^{\theta}\qquad\text{for all }y\in[Y,Y^{1+\delta}].
\]
Then $F$ is zero-free above $\theta$.

P018.statement:
\par\noindent{\footnotesize \nolinkurl{Imports.lean:8}.}\par
Let $\mathcal L$ be a level, $\lambda>1$ and $0<\theta<1$. If the set
$\{x:\mathcal G_{\mathcal L}(x)\le x^{\theta}\}$ has windows of exponent $\lambda$, then
$\mathcal L$ is zero-free above $\theta$.

P019.statement:
Fix a predicate $Q$ on $\mathcal P$, $\lambda>1$, and a system of families with core and tied predicates as in \nolinkurl{TopWin.lean:19--33}. For each $\psi$ satisfying $Q$, write $\mathcal L=\operatorname{cyc}(\psi)$ and suppose the following.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $e_D,e_L\in\mathbb R$, every $\varepsilon>0$ and every family $F$ at $\varepsilon$, the conjunction of \code{EFamC}$(\mathcal L,F)$ and eventual tiedness on its window set with $e_D,e_L$ implies $\mathcal G_{\mathcal L}(x)\le x^{1/2+(e_D+e_L+7)\varepsilon}$ at every sufficiently large point of that set.
\item The level-window implication of P018 holds for $\mathcal L$.
\item There exist $e_D,e_L\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon_1>0$, common to all subsequent $\varepsilon$. For every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_1$ there is a family $F$ at $\varepsilon$ satisfying \code{EFamC}$(\mathcal L,F)$ with exponent-$\lambda$ windows and eventual tiedness on that set with these same $e_D,e_L$. In both clauses eventual tiedness uses fixed $K,c_{HH},e_K,C_L,x_0$ for the selected family, as in P017.
\end{enumerate}
Then $L(s,\psi)\ne0$ for every $\psi$ satisfying $Q$ and every $s$ with $\Re s>1/2$.
